An Endearing Home, A Distinctive Global City
MND's vision reflects our growing emphasis not just on physical infrastructure, but also on the softer aspects of creating emotional attachment in our people, the global talents and corporations whom we attract here. At the same time, it articulates MND's goal of building upon Singapore’s unique distinguishing characteristics to develop Singapore as a global city of knowledge, culture and excellence.


Our Mission:

Develop World-Class Infrastructure
MND will provide quality physical infrastructure for the nation by working with our partners in the public and private sectors.

Create a Vibrant, Resilient and Sustainable Living Environment
MND will strive to make Singapore a livelier and more exciting city, and ensure our nation is well-prepared to face the growing uncertainties and complexities. MND will also maintain the quality and resilience of our built and natural environment to ensure high standards of living, and carry out development that meets the needs of the present without compromising that of future generations.

Provide Affordable and Accessible Public Housing
MND will commit to support Singaporeans' homeownership aspirations and ensure public housing remains affordable and accessible.

Build Rooted and Cohesive Communities
MND will strive to foster our citizens' attachment and love for our homeland and maintain social cohesiveness in our communities, even as Singapore continues to be an open and globalised society.
jobDescription:
Want a front-row seat to how ministry-level strategy is shaped – and a chance to influence it?

What the role is: 

Join MND’s Corporate Strategy team and work with senior leadership to tackle complex, cross-cutting challenges that shape Singapore’s built environment – from housing and land use to urban development, infrastructure, municipal services, technology and resilience. 

From supporting medium- to long-term strategic planning to navigating emerging risks, you will help translate issues and trade-offs into clear insights for senior decision-making, while building strong foundations in strategy, problem-solving, and stakeholder engagement early in your career.

Join the team that shapes how the MND Family thinks about its future.

As part of the Corporate Strategy team, you will help MND Senior Management make sense of complex, cross-cutting or emerging issues, connect perspectives across the MND and its Statutory Boards (i.e. MND Family), and align stakeholders around strategic priorities. 

This is a unique opportunity to gain exposure to how strategic issues are framed, discussed and progressed at the senior leadership level, across a wide range of challenges spanning housing, land use, urban development, municipal services, technological change, risk and resilience, while building strong foundations in strategy, stakeholder management, and enterprise risk governance.
jobResponsibilities:
- Shape strategic priorities and decision-making  
Support the development and refinement of the MND Family’s medium- to long-term priorities (5–10 years) by structuring issues, synthesising perspectives, and translating strategic considerations into clear papers and discussions.

- Drive cross-cutting strategy projects  
Lead and structure blue sky initiatives that cut across divisions and agencies - bringing together different perspectives to tackle current and emerging system-level challenges, such as public service experience in an AI-driven society.

- Shape senior leadership platforms  
Help design and drive key forums (e.g. senior management retreats and strategic discussions), ensuring that conversations are focused on the most critical issues and lead to clear outcomes.

- Strengthen organisational resilience  
Identify emerging risks and vulnerabilities, and work with stakeholders to develop strategies that enhance the MND Family’s ability to respond to a rapidly changing environment.

- Track what matters  
Develop and refine ways to monitor progress on key priorities, ensuring leadership has a clear, honest view of where things stand - and where course corrections are needed.

Why this role

- A panoramic view of how Singapore’s built environment is shaped across housing, land use, infrastructure, urban development and municipal services
- Exposure to how strategic issues are framed, discussed and progressed at senior leadership platforms across the MND Family 
- Rare early-career opportunity to experience how large, diverse organisations are managed from the inside 
- Build a whole-of-system perspective and develop range
- Accelerated learning and development in your career
jobRequirements:
- Strong analytical and critical thinking
- Clear and structured communication
- Ability to engage and influence stakeholders
- Ownership and initiative
- Interest in strategy, public policy and organisational management

• Experience leading projects or workstreams involving external stakeholders, funding governance, programme delivery and cross-functional coordination.

• Good understanding of public-sector governance, grant processes, budgeting, procurement considerations, outcome reporting and risk management.

• Experience working with training providers, employers, sector agencies, community partners, education institutions or workforce/skills ecosystem stakeholders will be advantageous.

• Familiarity with grant management, CRM tools, digital project management tools or dashboards will be advantageous.

• Strategic Partnership Development: Able to identify, cultivate and sustain partnerships that advance organisational priorities and translate collaboration opportunities into implementable initiatives.

• Programme and Pilot Design: Able to frame problems, design operating models, drawing on design thinking or human-centred design approaches where useful, test new approaches, evaluate outcomes and recommend whether to refine, scale, hand over or stop.

jobDescription: You will support the operational backbone of JTC's Investment Division, ensuring the accurate and timely execution of investment activities across internally managed portfolios and externally placed funds. You will also contribute to building robust operational infrastructure and governance frameworks as the Division grows.
jobResponsibilities:
Performance Reporting and Portfolio Valuation

  • Prepare and review periodic performance reports across internally managed and externally managed portfolios.
  • Perform portfolio valuation reconciliation against custodian and fund administrator records, investigating and resolving discrepancies in a timely manner.
  • Support the production of management reporting for senior stakeholders.

Securities Settlement and Trade Support

  • Support the end-to-end settlement process for the internally managed portfolio, including the confirmation, matching, and settlement of trades.
  • Develop and maintain operational procedures for the internal trading book, and liaise with custodians and counterparties to resolve settlement queries and exceptions.

Liquidity Management

  • Coordinate cash movements with custodians and fund managers to ensure sufficient liquidity for operational and investment needs.

Counterparty Relationship Management

  • Manage day-to-day relationships with fund managers' operations teams, custodians, trustees, fund administrators, and other key service providers.
  • Serve as the primary operational point of contact and ensure service levels and obligations are met.

Portfolio Compliance

  • Monitor portfolio compliance against investment guidelines, mandate parameters, and applicable regulatory requirements on an ongoing basis. Flag and escalate breaches and assist in their resolution.

Legal and Counterparty Documentation

  • Work with external counsel to review, negotiate, and execute investment management agreements, subscription agreements, side letters, and other legal documentation with investment counterparties.
  • Maintain a well-organised repository of all executed agreements and track key terms and obligations.

Tax and Regulatory Obligations

  • Review and monitor tax obligations arising from the investment portfolio, including withholding tax, GST, and fund-level tax considerations.
  • Liaise with tax advisors and counterparties on tax documentation such as W-8BEN and FATCA/CRS requirements.

Technology and Systems Implementation

  • Contribute to the evaluation, selection, and onboarding of operations and portfolio management systems appropriate for the Division's needs.
  • Work with internal stakeholders and vendors to configure systems, map workflows, and ensure data integrity across platforms.
  • Identify opportunities to improve operational efficiency through technology as the Division's activities scale.

Governance, Process Enhancement, and Audit Support

  • Identify gaps in existing operational processes and controls and implement enhancements to strengthen investment governance.
  • Contribute to the development of operational policies, procedures, and frameworks.
  • Liaise with internal audit and support periodic reviews of the Division's control environment, ensuring findings are tracked and remediated in a timely manner.
jobRequirements:
• 2–5 years of relevant experience in investment operations, fund administration, custody operations, or a related function at an asset manager, institutional investor, bank, or fund administrator.
  • Familiarity with the operational lifecycle of investment instruments, including fixed income securities and offshore institutional funds.
  • Experience with custodian and fund administrator reconciliation processes.
  • Exposure to investment management agreements and subscription documentation is an advantage.
  • Working knowledge of compliance monitoring and investment guideline frameworks.
  • Familiarity with tax documentation requirements (e.g. FATCA, CRS, withholding tax) is an advantage.
  • Strong attention to detail and a high degree of accuracy in handling data and documentation.
  • Ability to work independently and take ownership in a lean team environment, with the initiative to build processes from scratch rather than simply follow established ones.
  • Good interpersonal and communication skills, with the ability to manage external counterparties professionally.
  • A collaborative, can-do attitude and genuine interest in contributing to the broader success of the Investment Division.

jobDescription:
As Cluster Director, Media Development, you will lead the end-to-end strategy, delivery and transformation of Singapore’s public service media ecosystem, spanning broadcast, print, digital platforms, and emerging media.

You will oversee the Public Service Media (PSM) division, including both Mediacorp and SPH Media Trust (SMT), alongside New Media & Marketing and Media Capability Development, to drive integrated outcomes across content creation, distribution, measurement, and talent development.

This role is responsible for shaping how public service content is created, delivered, discovered and sustained, ensuring it remains relevant to evolving audience behaviours while strengthening social cohesion, national identity, and public trust.

You will work closely with MDDI, other IMDA divisions, and a wide range of industry, platform and international partners to deliver a coherent, future-ready public service media ecosystem that balances public value with long-term sustainability.

The ideal candidate for this role is a strategic generalist — someone who brings strong systems thinking, stakeholder management, and programme leadership skills, rather than deep domain expertise in media production or content. Given the breadth of this role, which spans industry development, grant management, strategic planning, and cross-agency coordination, candidates from strategy, management consultancy, or public sector policy backgrounds are strongly encouraged to apply. The ability to quickly understand a complex ecosystem, synthesise diverse inputs, and drive coordinated outcomes across multiple stakeholders will be far more critical than prior media industry experience.
jobResponsibilities:
Lead and integrate Singapore’s public service media ecosystem

  • Oversee the full PSM landscape across broadcast (Mediacorp), print (SMT), and digital platforms, ensuring a coherent national strategy and aligned outcomes.
  • Drive integration across content, distribution, measurement and capability development, breaking silos between divisions to achieve system-level impact.
  • Work alongside relevant divisions in MDDI to translate national priorities into coordinated strategies and programmes that deliver public service outcomes at scale.
  • Guide the evolution of PSM entities and programmes towards sustainable operating models, balancing public funding with efficiency and innovation.
  • Drive adoption of technology-enabled solutions to improve productivity, reduce costs, and enhance content delivery.
  • Anticipate shifts in media consumption, platform economics and information ecosystems, and position Singapore to respond proactively.

Drive content relevance, reach and impact across platforms

  • Shape strategies that ensure public service content remains audience-relevant across linear, digital and social platforms, including emerging formats.
  • Oversee New Media initiatives to strengthen digital content delivery, creator ecosystems, and platform partnerships.
  • Lead efforts to optimise reach, engagement and effectiveness, leveraging data, analytics and evolving platform dynamics.
  • Ensure strong alignment between content objectives and distribution strategies, across both traditional and digital channels.

Strengthen measurement, accountability and performance

  • Oversee the development and application of national media measurement systems and frameworks to assess reach, engagement and societal impact.
  • Drive the use of data, analytics and audience insights to inform content strategies, funding decisions and policy development.
  • Establish clear performance benchmarks and accountability frameworks across PSM entities and programmes.
  • Ensure public service media investments deliver measurable outcomes in trust, cohesion and inclusion.

Build a future-ready media industry and talent base

  • Oversee Media Capability Development to uplift industry capabilities in key areas such as creative development, production, and emerging technologies (where applicable).
  • Drive structured programmes that strengthen critical creative roles and support long-term industry competitiveness.
  • Foster partnerships with industry, platforms and educational institutions to accelerate skills development and technology adoption.
  • Ensure capability-building efforts are aligned with evolving industry needs and global trends.

Drive Marketing and Promotion of Made-with-Sg content

  • Shape strategies to ensure that Made-with-Sg content is effectively positioned, marketed and promoted across linear, digital and social platforms.
  • Ensure the delivery of B2B and B2C marketing efforts to elevate the visibility and positioning of Singapore’s content, talent and industry capabilities locally and internationally.
  • Oversee go-to-market strategies, campaigns and industry branding efforts, including on major platforms such as the Singapore Media Festival and other international markets.

Drive strategic partnerships and whole-of-government alignment

  • Lead engagements with MDDI and other government agencies to align policy, funding and delivery of public service media outcomes.

  • Build a high-performing leadership team with strong capabilities in strategy, programme delivery, partnerships and data-driven decision-making.

agencyDescription:

We enable employers to build a skilled, future-ready workforce, design quality jobs, and adopt skills recognition practices. Together with our partners, we build a trusted, high-quality, industry-relevant, and innovative ecosystem that meets the evolving workforce needs of both businesses and workers.   

Guided by our vision of a Singapore where everyone can grow in fulfilling careers, we live our promise of Building Skills, Growing Careers by nurturing lifelong learning, strengthening employability and enabling career growth for all, including our own officers, through a continuous learning culture and a supportive, flexible, inclusive working environment that fosters innovation, collaboration, and well-being.

So, join us to be part of a dynamic team driving the national SkillsFuture movement and building a strong Singaporean core. Together, we create opportunities, transform lives, and shape the future of work.
jobDescription:
The Skills and Workforce Development Agency (SWDA) is establishing an innovation programme as a strategic platform to identify, test, and scale innovative workforce solutions within the Careers and Employment Services (CES) ecosystem. 

In this role, you will support the planning and implementation of the innovation programme across its full cycle – from programme calls and application processing, to evaluation support, data tracking, dashboarding, reporting and knowledge management. You will work closely with internal teams and external stakeholders to ensure the programme runs smoothly, is well-documented and continuously improved. This role is suited for someone who is detail-oriented, organised, collaborative, and keen to contribute to meaningful workforce innovation.
jobResponsibilities:
Programme Operations

• Support the planning and execution of innovation programme calls,including preparing engagement materials, briefing notes, FAQs, application guides and templates
• Manage enquiries from prospective applicants and coordinate followup actions
• Coordinate engagement sessions, meetings and timelines with applicants and stakeholders
• Support proposal screening and coordinate evaluation processes with programme applicants and stakeholders
• Prepare meeting materials, minutes and documentation for programme governance and approval processes
• Track proposal statuses, assessment outcomes and approval timelines

Programme Administration

• Maintain the overall programme calendar, monitor key milestones, and track project deliverables, budget utilisation and claims submissions
• Maintain accurate records of approved projects, programme agreements and documentation
• Prepare management reports and programme updates using accurate and timely data
• Support design, maintenance and refresh of management dashboards and reports, leveraging digital and AI tools to surface programme trends and insights, key risks and decision points
• Monitor programme KPIs and outcomes, and present them in clear visual formats for management and stakeholder audiences 

Knowledge Management & Continuous Improvement

• Support documentation of pilot learnings and development of case studies
• Consolidate feedback from applicants and stakeholders to support process improvements
• Support implementation of automation and digitalisation initiatives to improve programme operations
jobRequirements:
• Relevant experience in areas such as programme management, project coordination, stakeholder engagement, partnerships and/or grants administration
• Familiarity with Singapore's labour market and the Careers and Employment Services (CES) ecosystem including intermediaries and solution providers
• Strong written and verbal communication skills for engaging internal stakeholders and ecosystem partners
• Proficient in using MS Office applications, particularly Excel and PowerPoint; hands-on experience with data visualisation tools such as Power BI or Tableau is strongly preferred
• Detail-oriented and adaptable, with the ability to manage multiple priorities effectively and navigate ambiguity and change
• Able to work both independently and collaboratively in a team setting
• Interest in innovation, workforce transformation and programme development

Candidates are encouraged to sign up for a Careers & Skills Passport (CSP) account and include your CSP public profile in your resume.  Please check out  www.myskillsfuture.gov.sg for details on the CSP.

All applicants will be notified on whether they are shortlisted or not within 4 weeks of the closing date of this job posting.

agency: Ministry Of Social And Family Development
agencyDescription:
Join Us at MSF for a Meaningful, People-Centric Career!

At MSF, our mission is to nurture and build resilient individuals, strong families, and a caring society. We offer meaningful and impactful people-centric careers in the design and delivery of policies, services and programmes. We are an all-inclusive and family friendly workplace where career growth is prioritised through a comprehensive suite of development opportunities to help our officers succeed today as well as be future-ready. We do this through various formal and informal learning and development programmes for officers to build different competencies and gain diverse work experiences within MSF, the Public as well as the Social Service Sectors.
jobDescription:
The Social Support Group (SSP) oversees all policy, planning and delivery of social services for low-income and vulnerable families, including persons with disabilities. 
The Service Delivery Division (SD) oversees all direct operations, including Social Service Offices (SSOs), service management of Family Service Centres, administration of schemes for student and childcare and Student Care Centre operations.
jobResponsibilities:
As a part-time Family Coach (FC) within the SSO, you will support the implementation of Community Link (ComLink), an initiative that provides proactive and integrated family-centric support to low-income, vulnerable families with children living in rental flats with the aim of empowering them to achieve Stability, Self-reliance and, ultimately, Social mobility (3‘S’). 
You will maintain regular engagement with these families at a reduced caseload relative to a full-time FC. These regular engagements will allow you to (1) befriend the family to build trust and rapport, (2) work with the family to come up with an action plan that would help them address their needs and achieve their aspirations, (3) coordinate with various agencies to bring in assistance for the families, where needed and (4) monitor the families’ progress towards achieving 3‘S’ goals. 
In delivering social support to these families, you are required to work closely with the team of MSF officers and other stakeholders such as government organisations, Social Service Agencies, Advisers & their grassroots leaders, community partners, as well as volunteers.
jobRequirements:
Candidate must be passionate about supporting vulnerable families and possess the following competencies: 
• 	Degree and/or Grad Dip in Social Work, Psychology, Sociology, Community Development or related degrees would be advantageous 
• 	Advantageous to have at least 3 years of relevant working experience in engagement or social service sector, and able to work independently 
• 	Strong interpersonal and communication (written and presentation) skills 
•	Strong analytical, planning and problem-solving skills 
• 	Proactive and self-motivated worker 
• 	Effective team-player 
• 	Empathetic 
• 	Able to speak a vernacular language/dialect would be advantageous 
• 	Meticulous 
• 	Stakeholder Engagement (Befriending experience, motivational interviewing and assessment skills would be an advantage) 
• 	Community Development 
• 	Project Management 
• 	Candidates who have relevant volunteering/working experience in the social service sector or other roles that help the needy would be an advantage. 
• 	He/she should be able to engage multiple parties, who may have differing views, to develop an integrated and coordinated client-centric plans that are in the families’ best interest.

jobTitle: Manager, Operations Policy, Occupational Safety and Health Division (OSHD)
agencyDescription:
Championing Human Potential for a Thriving Singapore
Singaporeans are at the heart of what we do. The Ministry of Manpower (MOM) empowers our people and fosters a thriving, inclusive workforce that drives Singapore's growth and prosperity. By working closely with our tripartite partners, industry and community stakeholders, we strive to create workforce and workplace policies that foster resilience, adaptability, and a bright future for a thriving Singapore. 

As an MOM officer, you will be part of this meaningful mission, contributing across diverse and impactful areas - from shaping forward-looking and effective manpower policies and strengthening industrial relations, to enhancing workplace safety standards and ensuring balanced local and foreign workforce regulations. Here at MOM, we are committed to creating an inclusive experience not just for our national workforce, but also for our officers who work tirelessly to champion human potential for a thriving Singapore.
jobResponsibilities:
•	You will develop, review, and update operational policies for WSH and WIC functions, ensuring they are legally grounded, operationally practical, and aligned with prevailing legislation and OSHD's strategic direction. You will conduct periodic reviews to keep policies current in response to legislative changes, emerging risks, and operational feedback, and work to identify and resolve gaps or inconsistencies across the suite of policies covering enforcement, engagement, and communications.

•	You will work closely with enforcement, engagement, and communications departments to gather ground-level feedback on the practicability of existing policies and liaise with legal and policy teams to ensure operational policies are anchored in legislative intent. Where operational policies interface with external parties, you will engage industry associations, unions, and other government agencies as appropriate.

•	You will also track feedback, incidents, and operational outcomes to assess policy effectiveness, and lead reviews and recommend revisions where gaps or issues are identified, drawing on insights from teams such as OSH Policy (WPSD), Ops Planning, WSHC, and CED.
jobRequirements:
•	We are looking for a motivated individual with a tertiary qualification, preferably in Engineering or a related science discipline, and at least three years of experience in WSH or WIC work with meaningful exposure to enforcement, engagement, or policy functions. Experience in developing or reviewing operational guidelines, SOPs, or regulatory frameworks would be an advantage.

•	You should have strong analytical and conceptual abilities, sound knowledge of WSH and WIC laws and legal principles, and excellent written and interpersonal communication skills. You are detail-oriented, results-driven, and able to manage multiple policy workstreams concurrently under pressure. The ability to reconcile operational realities with policy intent, and to coordinate effectively across departments and functions, will be key to success in this role.

agencyDescription: The Civil Aviation Authority of Singapore's raison d'etre is to develop the air hub and aviation industry in Singapore, expanding Singapore's links to the rest of the world. We enable opportunities through aviation, making connections, opening doors and enabling choices in people's lives.
jobDescription:
The CAAS Management Associate Programme (MAP) is designed to nurture the next generation of aviation leaders. As a Management Associate, you will embark on a structured developmental journey that equips you with the skills, experience and confidence to build a fulfilling career in CAAS and contribute to the growth of Singapore’s air hub and aviation industry.

Through project assignments, developmental programmes and job rotations, you will gain broad exposure across the aviation ecosystem and develop the capabilities required to become a future leader in CAAS.
jobResponsibilities:
Gain Hands-on Experience from Day One: You will undergo a suite of curated developmental programmes and on-the-job training to build expertise in your area of work. This will provide you with a strong foundation for a meaningful and rewarding career in CAAS.

Build Core Aviation Capabilities: During the early years of your career, you will undergo structured rotations across at least two functional clusters in CAAS. These postings will provide holistic understanding of the different aspects of aviation and develop a strong foundation in aviation policy, operations and industry development.

Contribute to Impactful and Meaningful Projects: You will have opportunities to participate in organisation-wide and sector-level initiatives that support the continued growth, transformation and resilience of Singapore's aviation sector. Working alongside colleagues from diverse disciplines, you will broaden your perspectives and hone your leadership capabilities.

Learn from Experienced Leaders and Industry Experts: You will benefit from mentorship by senior leaders within CAAS who will provide guidance and career advice to support your professional growth. Beyond mentorship, you will have opportunities to connect with aviation professionals across the industry, building valuable networks and learning from experienced practitioners.
jobRequirements:
Singapore Citizens in the final year of university study, or with less than 2 years of work experience Outstanding CCA / leadership track records.

Application

Apply through Careers@gov.

Only shortlisted candidates will be notified.

Shortlisted candidates will undergo a selection assessment comprising psychometric tests and panel interviews.

Successful candidates will join CAAS on a contract basis and may be offered a permanent role if found suitable.

jobTitle: [LTA-LO] ASSISTANT/DEPUTY/ MANAGER, LEARNING STRATEGY AND PLANNING
agencyDescription:
The Land Transport Authority (LTA) is a statutory board under Ministry of Transport that spearheads land transport developments in Singapore. We are seeking dynamic, energetic, highly motivated, passionate and qualified professionals to join us.

Many opportunities & challenges await those who are keen on an exciting career to realise our commitment to envision & implement an integrated transport system.
jobDescription:
The Learning Strategy and Planning Team is part of LTA’s Learning Office, and you will be at the forefront of driving a systemic shift in how the organisation approaches learning and capability development. We are moving beyond traditional learning and development to embed continuous organisational learning in LTA.

In this role, you will be instrumental in addressing key organisational challenges, including consolidating our learning landscape, strengthening a vibrant learning culture, and enhancing our agility to respond to emerging needs and transformation areas. You will take a systems view of learning, ensuring that capability gaps and opportunities, are systematically reviewed and that learning interventions drive measurable impact. Your scope of work will encompass four key pillars:

• Conduct Capability Diagnostics and Pulse on Learning. You will either lead or be involved in developing and deploying frequent dipsticks to gather learning-related data across the organisation. This includes measuring and analysing skills and performance gaps against desired organisational outcomes, and establishing a consolidated view of the LTA learning landscape (what, who, where, how, when).

• Design Learning Interventions and Approaches. You will either lead or be involved as a workplace learning partner to close identified capability gaps, and to design nimble and contextualised solutions, such as curating learning playlists and establishing action-learning project teams. The team would also need to respond rapidly to emerging needs and support LTA-wide transformation areas.

• Measure Learning Outcomes. You will either lead or be involved in defining clear behavioural and performance metrics to evaluate the impact of learning interventions, track the speed of upskilling across the organisation, and establish systematic reviews of performance gaps and the effectiveness of deployed solutions.

• Strengthen Learning Culture and Vibrancy. You will either lead or be involved in applying a systems lens to cultivate a healthy organisational learning culture, and implement strategies that target individual motivation, foster supportive team environments, and build organisational enablers.
jobResponsibilities: This role also involves direct partnering with LTA senior management and engaging of Groups, Divisions and colleagues very closely. To be part of our team, you should enjoy working with diverse groups of leaders and people to forge deep understanding of their operations and help create meaningful change within the organisation. You would need to be comfortable with creating communication materials and coming up with systematic processes, synthesizing information and data from diverse sources, and have strong communication skills to engage management and other stakeholders.
jobRequirements:
• Knowledge in Organisational Psychology, Organisational Development preferred
  • Strong advocate of and familiarity in AI tools utilisation and adoption
  • Familiarity with workplace learning methodologies, performance measurement frameworks, and diverse learning solutions
  • Currency on the latest learning trends and shifts in developmental approaches
  • Adaptable, creative, open to new ideas and able to execute effectively
  • Analytical and excellent writing and presentation skills
  • Comfortable in engaging people of different levels
  • For deputy manager applicants, 3 to 5 years of experience in learning and development
  • For manager applicants, more than 7 years of experience in learning and development and professional certifications in Learning and Development (e.g., CIPD, ATD CPTD, or similar)

As part of the shortlisting process for the role, you may be required to complete a medical declaration and / or undergo further assessment.

jobDescription: You will support SWDA’s evidence-based planning, programme evaluation and management reporting for initiatives related to career development and planning, employment services and capability building for the Career and Employment Services sector. jobResponsibilities:
You will be part of the Risk Assurance Division within IMDA’s Resilience and Cybersecurity Group. The Holistic Assessment team in this Division assesses the overall cybersecurity risk posture of critical digital networks and systems and the cyber capabilities of organisations operating these networks.

This includes integrating diverse sources of information, across the organisation’s external environment, its internal capabilities and the performance of its networks and systems. The team adopts an evidence-based approach to develop an objective assessment of the organisation and network’s key strengths and vulnerabilities. It also recommends key areas that senior management should track to uplift its cybersecurity risk posture.

The Holistic Assessment team works with teams across IMDA’s Resilience and Cybersecurity Group, and in partnership with industry stakeholders. It regularly engages senior management in both IMDA and the industry, to review its findings and recommendations. Through these, the Holistic Assessment team plays a critical role in ensuring that the critical digital networks and systems which underpin Singapore’s Digital Economy remain secure and resilient.

  • Conduct research and sense making of the evolving cybersecurity landscape in relation to Singapore’s digital infrastructure. This includes integrating threat intelligence information as well as international industry best practices for defending against current and emerging cyber threats.
  • Review and assess key priorities that inspections should focus on, based on the current and emerging threat landscape, as well as potential vulnerabilities surfaced in cyber audit reports and remediations implemented.
  • Design technical tests to validate the effectiveness of cybersecurity measures within these priority areas. This requires a deep understanding of the network design, what the cybersecurity measures are intended to protect against, as well as how they contribute to the overall cybersecurity of the digital network and systems as a whole.
  • Conduct the technical validation tests.
  • Synthesise key findings from the inspections, on the strengths and vulnerabilities of the network. Recommend remediations that should be implemented to improve the overall cybersecurity of the digital network and systems inspected.
jobRequirements:
• Background in Information Security, Engineering, Computer Science or equivalent with 8 years of experience in relevant fields or capacity.
  • Possess relevant OSCP, CREST or GIAC certification in offensive operations or equivalent.
  • Good understanding of the digital landscape and appreciation of how the different facets of cyber threats and defence interact and impact the cybersecurity of digital networks and systems.
  • Possess strong analytical skills and an attention to detail.
  • Have an inquisitive mind to explore and evaluate novel methods of testing.
  • Excellent writing and communication skills. This includes translating technical findings to their strategic and business impact.
  • Enjoy working in a fast-paced and dynamic environment.
  • Able to work independently as well as in a team/cross-team setting.

The position offered will be commensurate with experience.

jobTitle: Manager/Senior Manager, South East Asia and Oceania (SEAO)

jobDescription:
About EDB
The Singapore Economic Development Board (EDB), a government agency under the Ministry of Trade and Industry, is responsible for strategies that enhance Singapore’s position as a global centre for business, innovation, and talent. We undertake investment promotion and industry development, and work with international businesses, both foreign and local, by providing information, connection to partners and access to government incentives for their investments. Our mission is to create sustainable economic growth, with vibrant business and good job opportunities for Singapore.
For more information on EDB, please visit www.edb.gov.sg
jobResponsibilities:
About Southeast Asia and Oceania Division

The Southeast Asia and Oceania Division (SEAO) is a division in the Singapore Economic Development Board. SEAO plays a critical role in strengthening linkages between Singapore and the immediate region, and expanding Singapore’s economic hinterland. SEAO (i) develops and executes on government-to-government (G2G) partnerships; (ii) actively engages the region’s top private sector players – including major conglomerates, sectoral champions, and high growth startups, and (iii) facilitates the growth of global MNCs in Southeast Asia via Singapore. This positions Singapore as the choice location for companies to site their regional control tower, research and innovation, and advanced manufacturing operations, as they expand in the region.

Roles and Responsibilities

As a Manager/Senior Manager in the SEAO Division, you will operate at the unique intersection of bilateral economic policy, inter-agency stakeholder engagement, and investment promotion. You will have operational oversight over core cross-border economic initiatives, and support EDB’s corporate engagement in key regional markets including Malaysia, Indonesia and the Philippines. You will work with both global MNCs and regional conglomerates to best harness Singapore’s strengths and the complementary advantages of our immediate neighbours. You will need to understand and assess Singapore’s strategic interests, needs and develop the right solutions catered to Singapore’s position as a global business centre. You will also cultivate and maintain close ties with key influencers or decision makers in Singapore and the region ranging from government officials, industry leaders and company executives.

Bilateral Frameworks & G2G Policy Coordination

  • Drive Cross-Border Initiatives: Lead the operationalization and policy coordination for Singapore’s key regional partnerships, specifically the Johor-Singapore Special Economic Zone (JS-SEZ) and Batam-Bintan-Karimun region (BBK).

  • Inter-Agency Stakeholder Engagement: Work across multiple Singapore Government stakeholders to balance various interests and develop win-win solutions.

  • Bilateral Diplomacy: Work closely with bilateral government counterparts to align economic priorities, address cross-border regulatory frictions, and attract new investments into the region.

Corporate Account Management & Market Strategy

  • Portfolio Account Management: Support the management and engagement of strategic corporate relationships in Malaysia and the Philippines.

  • Engagement of key executives: Cultivate trusted relationships with senior company executives and next-generation business leaders to understand their regional expansion roadmaps and long-term priorities.
jobRequirements:
To succeed in this role, you should possess:

  • A Bachelor’s degree in Business, Economics, International Relations, Public Policy, Engineering, or a related discipline.

  • At least 3 to 5 years of relevant working experience in corporate strategy, investment promotion, management consulting, public policy, or international trade relations.

  • Deep Regional Context: Strong understanding of the Southeast Asian macroeconomic landscape, with specific familiarity regarding the corporate governance, regulatory environments, and market dynamics of Malaysia, Indonesia and the Philippines.

  • Excellent Interpersonal & Influencing Skills: Ability to navigate complex government-to-government sensitivities with absolute discretion, and influence internal and external stakeholders at all levels of seniority.

  • Keen Business Acumen: Exceptional conceptual and analytical thinking, with the ability to translate complex public policy frameworks into high-yield commercial incentives for private enterprise.

  • Exceptional Communication: Strong oral and written communication skills, with an ability to synthesize ambiguous trends into clear, succinct executive briefs and talking points for senior management and political leadership.

  • Agility & Adaptability: A self-starter who demonstrates high learning agility and execution rigor when operating in an unstructured, rapidly evolving business environment.

  • You should be a Singapore Citizen.

jobTitle: [LTA-T&ID] PRP / SENIOR / EXECUTIVE CYBERSECURITY ENGINEER, AV CYBERSECURITY
agencyDescription:

jobDescription: PRINCIPAL / SENIOR / EXECUTIVE CYBERSECURITY ENGINEER, AV CYBERSECURITY
jobResponsibilities:
Centre for Autonomous Mobility (CAM) leads Singapore’s national effort to deploy autonomous vehicles (AVs) at scale. As AVs move onto public roads, their cybersecurity becomes a matter of public safety: a compromised vehicle is not just a data breach but a physical risk. You will be part of the cybersecurity team responsible for developing the cybersecurity assurance regime for AVs, to ensure autonomous vehicles are deployed safely and securely in Singapore. You will drive to grow into AV cybersecurity. You will help build the function from the ground up assuring the cybersecurity of AVs themselves, and securing the systems CAM builds to oversee them.

Your responsibilities:

● Drive the development of the regulatory framework for AVs, such as establishing requirements for a Cyber Security Management System (CSMS) that covers the vehicle’s lifecycle — development, production and deployment.

● Assess AV developers’ cybersecurity submissions against our assurance criteria, applying Threat Analysis and Risk Assessment (TARA) and the R155 Annex 5 threats and controls, as well as standards such as ISO/SAE 21434.

● Define expectations for secure over-the-air software updates in line with the intent of UN R156 (a Software Update Management System), and for managing cyber risk across the AV supply chain.

● Establish monitoring, detection and incident response requirements for AVs, including analysing threats, vulnerabilities and mitigations to contribute to collective knowledge for the AV ecosystem.

● Maintain the policies, standards and playbooks for AV cybersecurity, and support engagement with local partners and international fora (e.g. UNECE WP.29 / GRVA).

Help secure CAM’s digital products / DevSecOps (secondary)

The other part of the team’s remit is making sure the systems CAM builds to regulate and monitor AVs — such as the Autonomous Vehicle Monitoring System — are themselves secure by design.

● Work with the Systems team to build security into the software development lifecycle, from design through CI/CD to production.

● Conduct security architecture and design reviews and risk assessments of CAM’s systems, and provide and implement remediation recommendations.

● Support security reviews of application code and architecture, and help design secure-by-default components.

● Set up automated security testing — SAST/DAST, dependency and secrets scanning, and infrastructure-as-code checks — in the delivery pipeline.

● Assist with breach detection and incident response for these products.

Help build the function

● As you grow into the role, you will naturally spot gaps and suggest tools, processes and improvements as the team and its remit grow.

● Evaluate emerging security technologies and recommend tools and approaches for the team to adopt.

● Provide security advice to CAM project teams on design and architecture decisions, and help build a security-minded culture across CAM, working alongside engineers, AV developers and agency partners.

For more senior hire, you will:

● Own and drive the AV cybersecurity assurance framework end to end, and set the assurance criteria AV developers must meet.

● Lead assessments of AV developers’ cybersecurity management systems and act as a technical authority in deployment-approval decisions on cybersecurity assurance adequacy.

● Help establish security architecture governance and compliance with relevant frameworks.

● Lead cybersecurity incident response for the AV fleet and our products, and define the team’s tooling, standards and processes.

● Mentor junior engineers and help grow the team.
jobRequirements:
● Knowledge preferably in Computer Science, Cybersecurity or a related field

● Thinks analytically about risk — can reason about threats, weigh trade-offs, and understand the limits of a cybersecurity control on safety outcomes.

● Eager to learn vehicle regulations — genuinely interested in standards and frameworks like R155, and able to pick them up quickly.

● Communicates clearly — can explain security issues to both technical and non-technical people.

● Takes initiative and cares about the public good — this is new ground, so you will help shape the standards rather than inherit them.

● Familiarity with automotive / vehicle cybersecurity standards and regulation — UN R155 and R156, ISO/SAE 21434, CSMS and TARA — or a track record of picking up new regulatory frameworks quickly.

● Exposure to automotive, operational-technology (OT) or embedded / safety-critical systems security, including security architecture of cloud-native applications and/or OT systems.

● Hands-on DevSecOps experience: secure SDLC, CI/CD pipeline security, cloud security (e.g. AWS), and SAST/DAST tooling.

● Hands-on experience with security tools such as SIEM, WAF, IPS, privileged access management (PAM), or data loss prevention (DLP).

● Professional accreditations such as CISSP, CISM, CRISC, GICSP, GCIH or OSCP.

● A strong interest in autonomous vehicles, emerging mobility technology and overall vehicular safety.

jobTitle: Senior Cybersecurity Consultant (ASG), Cybersecurity Engineering Centre
agencyDescription:
About the Cyber Security Agency of Singapore 
Established in 2015, the Cyber Security Agency of Singapore (CSA) seeks to keep Singapore’s cyberspace safe and secure to underpin our Nation Security, power a Digital Economy and protect our Digital Way of Life. It maintains an oversight of national cybersecurity functions and works with sector leads to protect Singapore’s Critical Information Infrastructure. CSA also engages with various stakeholders to heighten cyber security awareness, build a vibrant cybersecurity ecosystem supported by a robust workforce, pursue international partnerships and drive regional cybersecurity capacity building programmes. CSA is part of the Prime Minister’s Office and is managed by the Ministry of Digital Development and Information. For more news and information, please visit www.csa.gov.sg
jobDescription:
You will be part of the Attack Simulation Group (ASG) within the Cyber Security Agency of Singapore (CSA), a specialist team responsible for delivering advanced security testing and adversary-led assessments to strengthen the resilience of Critical Information Infrastructure (CII). This is a senior, hands-on role for experienced offensive security practitioners who want to apply real-world attack techniques to complex, high-impact systems in support of Singapore’s national cyber security mission.

ASG is a technically driven team within CSA focused on realistic attack simulation, penetration testing, red teaming, and purple-teaming outcomes. Our work goes beyond compliance-driven assurance, emphasising hands-on testing, attacker tradecraft, and practical security improvements.

Operating within the realities of government, we value curiosity, adaptability, and out-of-the-box thinking. Specialised training and development opportunities are provided to continuously deepen and expand our technical capabilities, and team members are expected to continuously learn, apply skills across domains, and contribute to the evolution of attack simulation practices across Singapore’s CII.

We also believe in sharing and growing our craft where appropriate. Some of our public work and tooling can be found at:
👉 https://github.com/hack-techv2/
jobResponsibilities:
- Lead and conduct penetration testing, red teaming, and adversary simulation activities across web, mobile, infrastructure, cloud, OT, and telecommunications environments.
- Execute realistic attack scenarios to assess the resilience of Critical Information Infrastructure (CII), including systems supporting essential services.
- Support purple-teaming activities by translating offensive techniques into actionable detection and response improvements.
- Lead engagements end-to-end, including planning, execution, reporting, and technical debriefs with stakeholders.
- Mentor junior consultants and contribute to raising the team’s overall technical standard.
- Drive continuous improvement of ASG’s testing methodologies, tooling, and research, including taking on problem spaces outside your primary domain when required.
- And because this is government, be prepared to occasionally switch gears by contributing to strategic initiatives, supporting and executing procurement activities, participating in industry outreach, or undertaking coordination work, all of which ultimately help us strengthen security outcomes and make Singapore a safer place to live and work.

Why Join ASG at CSA
- Work on nationally significant systems, including CII, OT, and telecommunications environments rarely accessible outside government.
- Engage in deep, technically challenging work that prioritises realism, learning, and security outcomes over high-volume testing.
- Apply your offensive security expertise to a public mission that directly contributes to Singapore’s cyber resilience.
- Be part of a specialist team that is deliberately building towards strong technical depth, continuous learning, and moving beyond compliance-driven assurance, and help shape what “good” looks like along the way.
jobRequirements:
- An attacker’s mindset with strong technical understanding of operating systems, networks, and modern enterprise environments.
- Proven ability to identify and execute real-world attack scenarios, beyond automated or checklist-based testing.
- Experience in penetration testing and/or red team operations, with exposure to adversary tradecraft and attack chaining.
- Demonstrated adaptability to transfer skills across technical domains (e.g. web to mobile, IT to OT, on-prem to cloud).
- Strong technical writing skills and the ability to clearly articulate security risks and impact.
- Typically 5–8 years of relevant experience in penetration testing, red team operations, or related offensive security roles, with demonstrated depth in hands-on technical work.
- Relevant industry certifications such as OSCP, CREST (e.g. CRT, CCT), CRTO, or equivalent are desirable.
- That said, we recognise that certifications alone do not define capability. Hands-on experience, problem-solving ability, and technical depth matter more to us than badges.

jobTitle: Lead Policy Analyst / Senior Policy Analyst, Prudential Advisory Division
agencyDescription: MAS is the central bank of Singapore. Our mission is to promote sustained non-inflationary economic growth, and a sound and progressive financial centre.
jobDescription: The Prudential Policy Department (PPD) fosters a sound and dynamic financial sector through prudential policy formulation.
jobResponsibilities:
Within PPD, the Prudential Advisory Division (PAD) formulates deposit insurance policies that support the orderly resolution of failing banks, with the aim of maintaining financial stability and protecting small depositors. You will help ensure that the deposit insurance framework strikes the right balance across competing policy considerations, and that its implementation processes run smoothly.

We also work with colleagues across PPD to design and implement the capital framework for banks, focusing on the eligibility of capital instruments (such as Additional Tier 1 instruments) and disclosure requirements. This work is grounded in the international Basel III regulatory framework and spans research and analysis, drafting legislative amendments, and engaging with banks on regulatory queries.

Beyond domestic policy work, we support senior management's participation in international fora — principally the Basel Committee on Banking Supervision and the Financial Stability Board. In this capacity, you will contribute to international policymaking on banking prudential issues and broader financial stability risks, while advocating for Singapore's interests. Work at these fora may touch on emerging or cross-cutting issues that do not fall neatly within any single department's remit. As the home of banking prudential policy in MAS, PAD takes the lead in coordinating and advancing Singapore's positions on such issues. Through this work, you will deepen your understanding of international dynamics and emerging risks, and how regulation is used to address them, while building close working relationships with colleagues across MAS. The role will also sharpen your writing, analytical, and interpersonal skills.

Successful candidates will be assigned a portfolio covering a subset of these responsibilities.
jobRequirements:
Successful candidates will:

  • Be able to assess complex issues critically, breaking them down into tractable components. This includes diving into the details, identifying the information needed to make decisions, weighing the pros and cons of various options, and recommending a course of action.

  • Have strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to explain their thinking clearly, concisely, and in a structured manner.

  • Have the ability to persuade stakeholders with entrenched views, and the resilience to revisit and refine positions through multiple rounds of feedback, while remaining open to pivoting as facts and circumstances evolve.

  • Enjoy working as part of a team — proactively seeking inputs from others, surfacing interactions between different workstreams, and navigating differences in opinion constructively.

  • Be self-directed learners who can identify gaps in their own knowledge and skills, and take initiative to develop themselves professionally.

The following would be an advantage:

  • A keen interest in Basel III, banking crisis management, international policy dynamics, and emerging issues in the financial and regulatory space.

  • A healthy scepticism and ability to stress-test assumptions - particularly useful when imagining adverse scenarios to craft robust deposit insurance policies.

  • An enjoyment of coordination work, stakeholder engagement, and staying current on banking regulatory and supervisory developments.

  • Good knowledge of banking operations and financial risks.

  • Have a basic level of AI literacy, or at least a willingness to learn and apply AI tools in the course of their work

  • A background in finance and/or accounting is preferred but not essential, provided you bring the qualities above.

You will be working in a fast-paced environment that would require the ability to manage multiple priorities and needs of stakeholders, as well as the agility to respond to changes and developments. As part of the shortlisting process for this role, you may be required to complete a medical declaration and/or undergo further assessment.

All applicants will be notified on whether they are shortlisted or not within 4 weeks of the closing date of this job posting.

Families are the bedrock of Singapore society. As Assistant Director (Family Policy), you will shape the policies and strategies that help Singaporeans build strong, resilient families — from supporting marriage and parenthood to ensuring that every child gets a good start in life, and that families are supported to care for elderly members with dignity.
You will lead a team of policy officers across three broad areas of work.

Strengthening Family Ties and Support Structures You will review and develop policies that promote strong family relationships across all life stages, with a particular focus on ensuring that elderly persons are well-supported by their families as they age. This includes identifying gaps in existing frameworks and working with MSF's Family Life Group (FLG) to translate policies into effective programmes and services on the ground.

Strengthening Safeguards for Vulnerable Persons You will lead the review of the Mental Capacity Act and related policies, including those governing professional donees and deputyship, to ensure the legislative framework keeps pace with evolving needs and adequately protects persons who lack mental capacity. You will also drive efforts to encourage Singaporeans, especially the elderly, to plan ahead through instruments such as the Lasting Power of Attorney (LPA), reviewing policies and strategies to improve awareness and uptake.

Funding and Legislative Review You will review MSF's funding approach for family services to ensure support is well-directed and fiscally sustainable, and lead reviews of key legislation including the Women's Charter, Mental Capacity Act, and Child Development Co-Savings Act to keep them aligned with policy objectives.
Throughout all of this, you will work closely with FLG, NPTD and other stakeholders to implement, monitor, and continuously refine your policies based on evidence and ground feedback.

jobTitle: Manager/Senior Manager, Youth Engagement and Research (ICPD)
agencyDescription:
The Skills and Workforce Development Agency (SWDA), a statutory board under the Ministry of Manpower (MOM), drives lifelong learning and workforce development to enable Singaporeans to take charge of their careers, learn for life, access good jobs, and grow in fulfilling careers. We enable employers to build a skilled, future-ready workforce, design quality jobs, and adopt skills recognition practices. Together with our partners, we build a trusted, high-quality, industry-relevant, and innovative ecosystem that meets the evolving workforce needs of both businesses and workers.   

Guided by our vision of a Singapore where everyone can grow in fulfilling careers, we live our promise of Building Skills, Growing Careers by nurturing lifelong learning, strengthening employability and enabling career growth for all, including our own officers, through a continuous learning culture and a supportive, flexible, inclusive working environment that fosters innovation, collaboration, and well-being.

So, join us to be part of a dynamic team driving the national SkillsFuture movement and building a strong Singaporean core. Together, we create opportunities, transform lives, and shape the future of work.
jobDescription:
You will be supporting SWDA's efforts to deepen our understanding of youths’ career aspirations and behaviours, and shape initiatives that strengthen youths’ engagement with career development and planning. You will lead research efforts, pilot programmes and associated funding and grants management processes that inform policy and engagement strategies to support youths’ school-to-work transitions and their early careers.

As a Senior Manager/ Manager in Youth Engagement and Research, you will:
jobResponsibilities:
• Conduct qualitative and quantitative research to understand perceptions, motivations, challenges, and behaviours of youths pertaining to work and career planning
  • Identify and explore emerging youths-related trends in education, employment, values and identity, and how these impact school-to-work transitions and early career decisions and pathways
  • Synthesize research insights into actionable recommendations to inform programmes, partnerships, and outreach strategies
  • Support internal teams with youth-related insights and frameworks to ensure initiatives are designed with empathy and relevance
  • Engage with youth-focused organisations, educators, community groups, and ecosystem partners to develop collaborative initiatives and expand outreach
  • Cultivate and maintain strong partnerships with youth organisations, education institutions and community stakeholders to co-develop impactful initiatives
  • Design and lead youth-centric pilot initiatives and engagements to test new approaches to career development and planning, including both digital and in-person formats
  • Develop funding proposals, grant applications and programme budgets for youth-related initiatives and pilots
  • Manage and monitor grants and programme funding for assigned initiatives, ensuring compliance with funding requirements, proper governance, and effective utilisation of resources
  • Work closely with internal stakeholders to ensure timely funding disbursement, tracking and reporting of programme outcomes
  • Track and evaluate the outcomes and effectiveness of youth-related initiatives and surface insights for broader implementation
  • Present insights and recommendations clearly and persuasively to internal and external stakeholders, including senior management and external partners
jobRequirements:
You should have the following work experience and knowledge:

  • Relevant experience in youth engagement, market and consumer/user research, programme development, community development and/or grants/funding management
  • Strong grasp of qualitative and/or quantitative research methods, including survey design, interviews, focus groups, or user testing
  • Familiarity with trends in youth development, education-to-work transitions, and socio-economic issues affecting young people
  • Experience working with or designing initiatives for diverse youth profiles, including students, graduates, and early-career workers
  • Proficient in MS Office, especially PowerPoint and Excel; familiarity with data visualisation or research tools is a plus

You should possess the following skill sets:

  • Youth Empathy and Engagement: Able to relate to and connect with diverse youth mindsets; comfortable designing programmes or touchpoints that resonate with their needs and realities
  • Research and Insight Development: Skilled in gathering, analysing and interpreting data to surface insights that shape programmes and strategies
  • Stakeholder Engagement: Confident in engaging partners across public, private, and people sectors to co-create initiatives or amplify outreach
  • Partnership Development: Capable of identifying, cultivating and sustaining strategic partnerships with youth-focused organisations, education institutions and community groups to co-develop initiatives that better support youths in their career exploration and transitions
  • Communication: Strong written and verbal communication skills to convey research findings and initiative proposals with clarity and influence
  • Initiative and Adaptability: Self-motivated, adaptable and resourceful; able to navigate ambiguity and move ideas forward from concept to execution
  • Project Management: Strong planning and coordination skills to manage pilots, studies, or outreach initiatives from start to finish
  • Finance and Grants Management: Ability to manage programme budgets, oversee grant administration, and ensure compliance with funding and reporting requirements

Successful candidates will be offered a contract in the first instance and may be considered for an extension or be placed on a permanent tenure.

Candidates are encouraged to sign up for a Careers & Skills Passport (CSP) account and include your CSP public profile in your resume. Please check out www.myskillsfuture.gov.sg for details on the CSP.

jobDescription: The Strategic Planning and Research Group (SPRG) was set up with the mission of gearing HDB up to address future challenges, in light of the increasingly rapid shifts in HDB’s operating environment and growing complexity of issues. To that end, SPRG performs horizon-scanning and foresight work to identify longer-term issues that may affect the public housing landscape, and spearheads the development of cross-cutting strategies to respond to these issues.

  • Study emerging gaps in Singapore's housing landscape and develop policy initiatives and responses to address them

jobDescription: As a key member of the Organisation and Talent Development team, you will play a central role in shaping and embedding the organisational culture and building workforce capability. You will lead the development and implementation of the Core Competency Framework (CCF) and functional competency frameworks, working closely with business units to translate these into meaningful programmes and interventions. Culture Building

jobDescription: The Ministry of Social and Family Development (MSF) is transforming how citizens access services through a new service delivery channel for digitally challenged and vulnerable users. This position will be with the central Customer Experience Division (CXD) as it works with a team to transform the service experience for its service users.
jobResponsibilities:
As an intern, your primary role will be to support data-driven evaluation of the service model, to inform operational and strategic refinements, including possible scaling. The key role is to support the team’s work to understand what is working, for whom, and why, so that decisions about how the service model should evolve are grounded in evidence.

You will help produce analyses, charts and dashboards that surface patterns in client behaviour, support pathways and performance trends, contributing to evidence-based discussions on how the service model could evolve over time. 

Where opportunities arise, you may also contribute to improving how insights are generated—such as by streamlining dashboarding or strengthening analysis workflows, including through the use of AI-enabled tools.

Building on quantitative insights, you will also support user testing and qualitative research as a complementary stream of work. This includes assisting with research preparation, observations and synthesis to help the team understand the why behind observed data patterns and validate emerging service model hypotheses.

You will work at the intersection of service design, operations and product teams, gaining exposure to how evidence is used to shape service decisions in a real-world public sector context.

Singapore's casinos operate under a robust regulatory framework designed to balance economic benefits with strong social safeguards. As the government reviews the effectiveness of existing responsible gambling measures, there is a need for a rigorous, evidence-based study of casino social safeguards— both locally and internationally — to inform policy development.
jobResponsibilities:
Project Overview
The intern will support the preparation of a comprehensive casino study that examines the effectiveness of social safeguards and responsible gambling measures, and generates insights to strengthen Singapore's policy framework.

Key Project Components
•	Conduct a comparative review of casino regulatory regimes and responsible gambling frameworks across selected jurisdictions (e.g., Macau, Australia, UK, Japan), identifying best practices and policy gaps.
•	Support the development of a research proposal to study the effectiveness of casino social safeguards and responsible gambling measures in Singapore and new potential measures to implement 
•	Supplement findings by drawing on available data, literature, and stakeholder perspectives.
•	Synthesise findings into a structured policy report or brief with actionable recommendations.
•	Present findings to divisional management at the conclusion of the internship.

Learning Objectives
By the end of the internship, the intern will have developed skills in policy research and comparative analysis, an understanding of gambling regulation and social policy trade-offs, experience in synthesising complex information into clear policy recommendations, and exposure to the practical workings of a government policy division.

Developmental Opportunities
The intern will have the opportunity to participate in relevant divisional meetings and policy discussions, engage with on-the-ground perspectives through potential site visits or stakeholder engagements, and present their research findings to divisional management.
jobRequirements: The intern should have strong research and analytical skills, good written communication, and an interest in public policy, social regulation, or governance. Familiarity with data analysis or policy research methods is an advantage.

jobTitle: Assistant Director, Asia Tech x Programme Office (Programming and Content)
agencyDescription:
Info-communications Media Development Authority (www.imda.gov.sg) offers a rewarding career that gives you a front seat in the fast-changing infocomm media sector, where technology and content are shaping the way people view the world more than ever.

We offer a wide range of opportunities, where talented individuals and teams can make a difference. Whether you are developing a telecommunications policy affecting consumers or spearheading a scheme to nurture budding media talents, each member of IMDA contributes towards driving innovation, enhancing productivity for economic growth, and improving the quality of life for all Singaporeans.

jobDescription:
The Asia Tech x Programme Office (ATxPO) sits within IMDA's International (INTL) Group and manages Asia Tech x Singapore (ATxSG), Singapore's flagship technology event platform that convenes change-makers and thought leaders from government and industry to explore how technology can create meaningful impact.

INTL amplifies Singapore's influence and presence in the global digital economy, enabling the nation to transcend its physical limitations and emerge as a bigger red dot on the international stage. The Group focuses on building robust relationships with countries worldwide and lays essential groundwork for the next phase of development in ASEAN's
digital economy. Through its comprehensive approach to international engagement, INTL creates opportunities for Singapore to capture greater value and strengthen its position in the rapidly evolving digital landscape.

As Assistant Director for Programming and Content, you will lead the team responsible for conceptualising, developing and executing the ATxSummit and ATxInspire series. You will also collaborate with IMDA's industry partner Informa Tech to advance the broader ATxSG agenda, including B2B opportunities through the ATxEnterprise brand.

In this role, you play a central part in shaping the core experience of ATxSummit. Your team drives the development of strategic themes, crafts thought-provoking agendas, and designs engaging sessions that inspire insight and action. You will curate and guide speakers to ensure every session is relevant and impactful. Beyond the main plenary, you will coordinate fringe activities and partner-led programmes to deliver a cohesive and memorable experience across the ATxSG ecosystem. Working closely with internal divisions, senior leadership and global partners, you will help advance Singapore's digital leadership on the world stage.

What You Will Be Exposed To
This role offers a unique vantage point on the issues and actors shaping the global digital economy. You will engage with thought leaders from government and industry, locally and internationally, as well as leading technology companies, research institutions and academia working on next-frontier technologies. Internally, you will work across multiple IMDA divisions and with inter-agency partners, building a broad understanding of Singapore's digital economy priorities.
jobResponsibilities:
You will lead and manage a team to develop and execute the programme, content, partnerships and sponsorships for ATxSG across two key areas:

Programme and Content

You will lead the programming and execution of the agenda for the ATxSummit (Plenary and Village) and ATxInspire series, developing content strategies for panels and sessions in close collaboration with internal and external stakeholders. This includes identifying, engaging and cultivating government and industry speakers, and applying a data-driven approach to programme development and execution.

Sponsorships and Partnerships

You will drive the development and execution of knowledge and event partnerships, serving as the key point of contact for strategic partners including government agencies and key industry organisations. This includes sourcing, developing and executing sponsorship arrangements with industry partners to grow ATxSG as a platform.
jobRequirements:
We are looking for a purpose-driven leader with a strong sense of ownership and accountability, and a genuine interest in technology and its role in shaping society. An understanding of the tech zeitgeist of the day is critical for success in this role.

You should be a self-motivated individual who thrives in a fast-paced, dynamic environment and is energised by complexity and ambiguity. You are a natural networker who builds relationships for the long term, and a strong team player who can work effectively across functions including marketing and events management.

You are mature and professional in your approach, proactive in reaching out to potential partners across industry, associations and government agencies. You communicate with clarity and purpose whether in writing, presentations or stakeholder conversations, and bring with you strong storytelling instincts and meticulous attention to detail.

The ideal candidate would possess 15 to 20 years of experience in conference programming, content development and/or partnership management.

Position will be commensurate with the candidate’s qualifications and experience.

Please note that only shortlisted applicants will be notified.
