jobTitle: Asst Director/Snr Asst Director/Deputy Director (Medical Service Scheme)
agencyDescription:
The Ministry of Health’s (MOH) vision is to champion a healthy nation with our people – to live well, live long and with peace of mind. As an open country constantly exposed to an interconnected world, Singapore faces complex issues in public healthcare. MOH constantly grapples with new challenges brought on by an increasingly globalised world, a rapidly ageing population and rising expectations. MOH’s responses to these challenges include preventing and managing the outbreak of diseases such as SARS and Influenza A (H1N1), designing a healthcare system that delivers care in an integrated and effective manner, growing the capacity and capabilities within the sector, and managing healthcare inflation.

As an MOH officer, you will be involved in formulating and implementing policies that guide Singapore’s healthcare ecosystem. You will work alongside a team with varied skills and backgrounds, but with the common goals of (i) promoting good health and reducing illnesses; (ii) ensuring that Singaporeans have access to good and affordable healthcare; and (iii) pursuing medical excellence. Your work will have far-reaching impact on the health and lives of Singaporeans.
jobDescription:
Shape Singapore’s Health at the National Level

Are you a medical doctor looking to make an impact beyond a clinical setting? Whether you are a junior doctor exploring your career options, or an established clinician contemplating new challenges to contribute at the national level, consider a career at the Ministry of Health (MOH).

Under the MOH Medical Service Scheme employment, you will bring your clinical lens and expertise to national healthcare policies and influence decisions that shape the health of Singapore. You will work at the intersection of medicine and policy to design the healthcare systems and frameworks that aim to improve the health outcomes for the nation, and be part of the national health leadership. 

You will be working in a fast-paced environment that would require the ability to manage multiple priorities and stakeholders at the same time. This is a role for doctors who are energised by complexity, motivated by purpose, and ready to drive healthcare transformation at a national scale.
jobResponsibilities:
You will contribute across four key domain areas:

•	Healthcare Regulation — Safeguarding standards and ensuring the safety, quality, and integrity of Singapore's healthcare system.
•	Manpower Development & Capability Building — Shaping the pipeline and professional development of Singapore's healthcare workforce.
•	Population Health & Health Services — Designing and delivering health programmes and services that keep Singaporeans healthy across their life course.
•	Quality, Value & Informatics — Driving innovation, data-driven decision making, and value in healthcare delivery.

At more senior levels, you may also lead and manage a team.

As part of your development, you may also be rotated to other public sector agencies and organisations within the broader healthcare ecosystem — such as the Ministry of Manpower (MOM), Health Promotion Board (HPB), Communicable Diseases Agency (CDA), or the public healthcare clusters. Your postings will be carefully designed to broaden your exposure and deepen your understanding of how policy translates into operations on the ground, equipping you with a well-rounded perspective to grow and contribute meaningfully throughout your career with MOH. 

While you will mostly be involved in healthcare policy work, you may also continue with sessional clinical practice, if you prefer, at the public healthcare institutions, so that you can maintain your clinical currency and familiarity with ground operations.
jobRequirements:
We welcome applications from medical doctors who are registered with the Singapore Medical Council (SMC) and remain in good standing. Beyond your medical qualifications, we are looking for doctors who embody the following:

•	Collaborative Spirit: You work effectively in multidisciplinary teams and are energised by cross-agency initiatives that drive system-wide change.
•	Critical Thinking: You bring your medical perspectives to bear on complex policy questions, evaluating evidence rigorously to inform national healthcare decisions.
•	Capacity for Change: You are adaptable and responsive to evolving health priorities, emerging challenges, and shifting policy landscapes.
•	Commitment to Continuous Learning: You are passionate about growing beyond clinical practice — into the domains of healthcare policy, regulation, and population health strategy.
•	Compassion: You connect with diverse stakeholders with empathy, and understand how policy decisions translate into real outcomes for real people.

We are also looking for doctors who demonstrate strength in systems thinking — the ability to understand complex healthcare ecosystems as a whole— as well as strategic thinking and the leadership capacity to inspire and guide teams through transformation.

As part of the shortlisting process for this role, applicants may be required to complete a medical declaration and/or undergo further assessment.

agencyDescription: The Civil Aviation Authority of Singapore's raison d'etre is to develop the air hub and aviation industry in Singapore, expanding Singapore's links to the rest of the world. jobDescription:
The officer will support the Principal Economist in establishing a new team dedicated to aviation economic analysis in support of Singapore's air hub strategy. As the middle-level manager of the team, the officer will have supervisory responsibilities for a junior-level economist and will be integral in formulating the team’s analytical direction, ensuring the quality and rigour of work, and translating economic insights into actionable recommendations for senior leadership and policy stakeholders.

The officer will play a crucial role in shaping evidence-based aviation policy and hub development strategy, drawing on deep expertise in econometric analysis, quantitative modelling, and transport economics. Working together with the Principal Economist, the officer will have opportunities to lead research projects across government agencies and the OneAviation community that meaningfully inform national aviation policy and Singapore's long-term hub competitiveness.
jobResponsibilities:
The officer will have responsibilities in the following areas:

a. Day-to-day direction and oversight of the unit’s demand modelling, including projections, policy counterfactuals and other quantitative research programme to inform national aviation policy.

b. Analysis on global aviation trends, market dynamics, and competitive positioning, with a focus on translating findings into strategic insights for decision-makers.

c. Middle-level engagement with government agencies, industry stakeholders, and inter-agency partners to ensure the unit's analytical work is well-integrated into air hub strategy and policy.

d. Presentation and communication of economic analysis and forecasting results to senior management and MOT to support policy, programme, and investment decisions.

e. Stewardship of the unit's work on economic assessments and data-driven insights for industry consultations and public-facing engagements.

Beyond the unit’s core analytical mandate, the officer will be responsible for building and sustaining organisational capabilities in economic analysis and transport economics across CAAS. This includes mentoring junior staff, establishing best practices, and contributing to the development of a strong analytical culture.
jobRequirements:
• Strong training in Economics, Econometrics, or a quantitative discipline with substantial economics content. Advanced studies in Economics would be an advantage

  • Strong background in theoretical and empirical economics

  • Minimum of 8 years work experience, with at least 5 years professional experience in quantitative economic analysis

  • Proven record of conducting independent research

  • Advanced programming skills (for eg Python, R, Stata)

  • Excellent written and oral communication

  • Passion in contributing to Singapore’s aviation sector and public policy in general

Note: Your appointment designation will commensurate with your relevant work experience. Successful candidates will be offered a 3-year contract in the first instance, and may be considered for placement on a permanent tenure or subsequent contract renewal.

jobTitle: Associate Trade Mark Examiners, Registry of Trade Marks
agencyDescription: The Intellectual Property Office of Singapore (IPOS) is the national authority that registers and is responsible for the administration of IP rights in Singapore. IPOS helps businesses use intangible assets (IA) and IP to grow and is committed to building Singapore into an international IA/IP hub. We help to catalyse a future driven by life-enhancing, commercially successful ideas created by businesses, professionals and everyday people. We help to turn today’s ideas into tomorrow’s assets. IPOS is a statutory board under the Ministry of Law.
jobDescription:
A trade mark can be any word, name, letter, numeral, device, shape, colour, aspect of packaging, or a combination of such elements. In some cases, even sounds or holograms may qualify. From the Singapore Airlines bird logo to the DBS quatrefoil, trade marks help businesses build distinctive brands and protect their reputation. 

We are currently seeking Associate Trade Mark Examiners to join the Registry of Trade Marks. In this role, you will work closely with fellow examiners to assess trade mark applications and ensure they comply with the legal requirements for registration. You may also contribute to the formulation and implementation of national trade mark policies, supporting Singapore’s position as a global hub for intellectual property and intangible assets.

The role includes an initial structured training period of approximately 18 months, during which successful candidates will progressively develop the legal, analytical and professional judgment required for independent trade mark examination. This training combines on the job learning, with mentoring and formal instruction provided, and requires sustained commitment and dedication from the job holder.
jobResponsibilities:
Examining a trade mark application requires a combination of sound thinking, good judgment, strong analytical skills, and some understanding of, or an interest in how businesses brand, market and identify themselves.

As a Trade Mark Examiner, you will:
1.	Assess distinctiveness
Determine whether a proposed trade mark is capable of distinguishing the trade origin of the relevant goods or services.
2.	Conduct searches for conflicting marks
Identify earlier trade marks on the Singapore trade mark register that may conflict with the application.
3.	Review specifications of goods and services
Examine the description of goods and services applied for, with reference to international classification standards.
4.	Communicate examination outcomes and provide guidance
Correspond with applicants or their legal representatives on examination outcomes, including raising objections where necessary, and assessing responses received. Provide guidance and assistance to members of the public who have queries on trade mark related matters.

Beyond examination work, Trade Mark Examiners may take on administrative and project based responsibilities that support the effective functioning of the Registry and the broader objectives of IPOS.

As you gain experience and seniority, your role will broaden to include mentoring, training and supervisory responsibilities, contributing to the professional development of junior colleagues.

As Singapore's first polytechnic, Singapore Polytechnic (SP) prides ourselves in providing the best learning experience for our students in pre-employment and continuing adult education. The mission of SP is as a polytechnic for all ages, we prepare our learners to be life ready, work ready, and world ready for the transformation of Singapore. jobResponsibilities:
We are looking for an experienced and hands-on professional to join our FabLab team. In this role, you will develop and deliver applied learning in digital fabrication, electronics, programming and maker education, while supporting the safe, reliable and effective operation of SP FabLab. You will help students and partners translate ideas into functional prototypes through design, making, testing and iteration.

Key Responsibilities

1. Curriculum Design & Development

Design, implement, and review curriculum that integrates digital fabrication, innovation, and maker education aligned with SP’s Education Model and MOE directions. Lead the development of hands-on, interdisciplinary learning modules to promote applied learning and innovation.

2. Teacher Capacity Building & Professional Development

Conduct training and mentoring for teachers within SP and partner schools to strengthen teaching capability in design thinking and digital fabrication. Develop resources, workshops, and frameworks to scale Maker Education across schools.

3. Strategic Leadership & Partnerships

Lead and execute the FabLab Strategic & Scaling Plan to position SP as a national hub for Maker Education. Represent SP FabLab in national MOE initiatives, industry collaborations, and international networks (e.g., Fab Academy).

4. Innovation & Research

Drive innovation in pedagogy and applied technology integration within curriculum and outreach programs. Undertake research or pilot projects to evaluate impact and improve programme scalability.

5. Programme Quality Assurance

Ensure programme alignment with institutional and national quality standards. Establish sustainable systems for student and teacher engagement, evaluation, and progression.
jobRequirements:
Essential Requirements

Bachelor’s Degree in Education, Engineering, Design, Technology, or a related field. At least 5 years of relevant teaching and curriculum development experience, preferably in tertiary or applied learning environments. Demonstrated experience in curriculum design, project-based learning, and innovation pedagogy. Proven ability to plan, deliver, and evaluate hands-on, technology-enabled learning experiences. Strong communication and stakeholder engagement skills to collaborate with schools, MOE, and industry partners.

Preferred Requirements

Fab Academy Diploma or equivalent certification in Digital Fabrication / Maker Education is a plus. Experience in leading teacher training, educational innovation projects, or national education initiatives. Recognized track record in curriculum innovation, STEM/STEAM education, or design thinking integration. Experience working with national education agencies, research institutions, or international Maker networks. Curriculum and pedagogy innovation in Digital Fabrication, Design Thinking, and Maker Education. Integration of technology-enhanced learning and applied innovation into formal and informal education contexts. Leadership in scaling sustainable education models across schools and institutions.

Candidates should be prepared to present a technical portfolio and may be required to complete a teaching demonstration and/or practical technical assessment as part of the selection process.

Successful candidate will be offered a 2-year contract in the first instance.

If you are shortlisted for the position(s), you should hear from us within 30 days of the closing date of the advertisement.

jobTitle: CBRNE Scientist (Tuas Checkpoint), CBRNE COE  (2 -YR Contract)
agency: Home Team Science and Technology Agency (HTX)
agencyDescription: HTX is the world’s first Science and Technology agency that integrates a diverse range of scientific and engineering capabilities to innovate and deliver transformative and operationally-ready solutions for homeland security. As a statutory board of the Ministry of Home Affairs and integral to the Home Team, HTX works at the forefront of science and technology to empower Singapore’s frontline of security. Our shared mission is to amplify, augment and accelerate the Home Team’s advantage and secure Singapore as the safest place on planet earth.
jobDescription:
HTX is Singapore's Science and Technology agency that brings together diverse scientific and engineering capabilities to develop transformative, operationally ready solutions for public safety. As a statutory board under the Ministry of Home Affairs, HTX works at the forefront of science and technology to empower the Home Team with cutting-edge capabilities. Guided by our mission to amplify, augment and accelerate the Home Team's advantage, we are committed to keeping Singapore the safest place on planet Earth.

The CBRNE Centre of Expertise (CoE) at the Home Team Science and Technology Agency (HTX) is at the forefront of developing and enhancing Singapore's capabilities to detect, protect against, and respond to Chemical, Biological, Radiological, Nuclear, and Explosives (CBRNE) threats. Our work supports the Home Team in safeguarding public safety and national security through cutting-edge science and technology.

We are seeking a motivated and technically skilled scientist to join our Specialised laboratory team based in Tuas Checkpoint. This is primarily a hands-on, lab-based role where you will be responsible for the day-to-day running of analytical operations, ensuring that laboratory functions are maintained to the highest standards of accuracy, safety, and compliance. You will also contribute all aspect contributing to the operation of the lab such as method development, evaluation of CBRNE-related technologies, working closely with Home Team agencies and industry partners in support of Singapore's security needs.
jobResponsibilities:
This role is centred on the CBRNE Specialised Lab, with the majority of your work involving hands-on analytical functions, sample management, laboratory administration and quality system. Key responsibilities include:
•	Conduct laboratory analysis and support field-based studies on technologies related to CBRNE preparedness, detection, and decontamination, including the development of new detection chemistries and next-generation sensing technologies.
•	Perform routine analysis of chemical and biological samples in a specialised laboratory setting, including ad-hoc screening and verification of samples in accordance with established SOPs.
•	Perform method development, method validation, and troubleshooting on analytical instruments including GC-MS/MS and LC-MS/MS. Competency in ICP-MS is an advantage.
•	Develop and maintain technical documentation, validation reports, and SOPs to support the CBRNE Specialised Lab in alignment with ISO/IEC 17025 requirements.
•	Handle explosives and hazardous materials as part of routine work, in compliance with safety protocols and risk assessments.
•	Undergo cross-training in basic bio-analytical techniques such as PCR and microarray analysis.
•	Deliver practical training and demonstrations to uniformed officers as required.
•	Maintain accurate records of chemical inventories, consumables, and laboratory supplies, ensuring stock levels are monitored and replenished in a timely manner.
•	Conduct procurement activities and contract management for laboratory supplies, project materials, and research equipment.
•	Assist in the upkeep and housekeeping of laboratory facilities.
jobRequirements:
Candidates should possess:
•	Degree in Chemistry, Analytical Sciences, Environmental Science, or a related discipline. Candidates with no prior experience are welcome to apply. 
•	Experience with analytical instrumentation such as mass spectrometry, GC/LC systems, or spectroscopic sensors is an advantage.
•	Knowledge of safety protocols and risk assessment practices in the handling of explosives and hazardous materials.
•	Familiarity with ISO/IEC 17025 requirements and laboratory documentation practices is preferred.
•	 Experience with laboratory inventory management and procurement or contract management processes is an advantage.
•	Able to work effectively in a dynamic, fast-paced environment and manage multiple concurrent technical workstreams. Can be a team player and a team lead.
•	Strong analytical, problem-solving, and technical writing skills.
•	Good written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to convey technical concepts clearly to diverse stakeholders.
•	Knowledge of data science, statistical analysis, machine learning, artificial intelligence, and scientific programming languages (e.g. Python or R) is an advantage.
•	Willingness to work at Tuas Checkpoint, where the HTX CBRNE Centre of Expertise (CoE) is based.
•	A committed individual who is prepared to respond to exigencies of service, including availability beyond regular working hours when operational needs arise.


This position is offered on a two-year fixed-term contract. As part of the shortlisting process for this role, you may be required to complete a medical declaration and/or undergo further assessment.

All applicants will be updated on the status of their applications within 4 weeks upon closing of the advertisement.

We aim to lead in applying AI to language-related tasks, with a focus on advancing speech and natural language capabilities. We explore how these capabilities can be harnessed and adapted to meet the unique needs of the Home Team.

We delve into emerging language AI technologies, analysing and evaluating its potential before implementing practical solutions. Our research focuses on translating cutting-edge innovations into applications tailored for the Home Team. •	Minimum 8-12 years of experience in software engineering, AI/ML, data science or product engineering, with at least 5 years in a leadership role managing multidisciplinary engineering teams.

agency: Ministry of Sustainability and the Environment
agencyDescription:
The Ministry of Sustainability and the Environment (MSE) is committed to providing Singaporeans with a clean and sustainable environment, and safe and secure supplies of food and water. MSE’s key priorities are to ensure a sustainable, resource-efficient and climate resilient Singapore. Our three strategic directions include economic resilience, resource resilience and climate resilience.

We enjoy challenging and diverse careers, which are bound together by the common cause - making Singapore’s living environment among the best in the world. Everyone who works at MSE has a role to play in helping to shape our environment – not just for now, but for generations to come.

We are constantly on the lookout for energetic, pro-active and committed individuals to join us. Successful candidates can expect a fulfilling career with competitive remuneration package and comprehensive range of benefits, as well as opportunities for cross-deployment within MSE and our Statutory Boards as part of our holistic career development.

To learn more about us, please visit https://www.mse.gov.sg.

At MSE and our family of agencies – PUB, NEA, and SFA – we drive sustainability and resilience initiatives that improve the everyday lives of Singaporeans. As part of the MSE Family, you will be at the forefront of innovation, leading efforts to safeguard water resources, protect public health, and ensure food safety. Through partnerships across sectors, we tackle evolving challenges while fostering an inclusive, safe, and supportive workplace. Join us in shaping Singapore’s sustainable future and making a lasting impact on the everyday lives of generations to come.

Climate change poses an asymmetrical challenge for Singapore – we contribute only around 0.1% of global carbon emissions, but will be disproportionately impacted by its effects.
 
In Feb 2021, the Government launched the Singapore Green Plan 2030, a whole-of-nation movement to advance Singapore’s national agenda on sustainable development. In Oct 2022, Singapore announced that it would raise its national climate target to achieve net zero emissions by 2050. 
 
There is much work to be done to realise the climate aspirations of Singapore. The available mitigation options have trade-offs, and need to be considered in the context of the overall triple transition of carbon, energy and the economy. Your work will therefore revolve around carefully weighing trade-offs, whether that be in exploring new possibilities for Singapore or ensuring existing policies remain fit-for-purpose.

jobDescription: [LTA-PT] SENIOR MANAGER, BUS RAPID TRANSIT DEVELOPMENT
jobResponsibilities:
As Senior Manager, Bus Rapid Transit Development, you will lead the development and implementation of a new Bus Rapid Transit (BRT) system for Singapore, starting with the Tuas South study and potential deployment. This role places you at the forefront of shaping a scalable medium-capacity public transport mode that can complement the MRT and conventional bus network, providing faster, more reliable and cost-effective connectivity for suitable corridors.

Working across system planning, engineering, technology, infrastructure, operations, safety, regulatory, and implementation domains, you will lead multidisciplinary efforts to assess international BRT models and develop a Singapore-specific solution that is safe, reliable, scalable and operationally sustainable. The BRT concept may include higher-capacity articulated or bi-articulated buses, dedicated running corridors, traffic signal priority, station-based fare collection, platform-level boarding, advanced vehicle guidance and automation technologies.

What You Will Be Working On:

As the Senior Manager, Bus Rapid Transit Development, you will provide overall leadership for the BRT programme from feasibility study through concept development, procurement, implementation and operational readiness, including:

  • Overall BRT Lead: Establish the project vision, objectives, requirements, governance structure, key milestones and delivery strategy for the BRT initiative. Lead the development of the preferred BRT concept and make recommendations to senior management on the long-term implementation pathway.

  • System Architecture and Concept Development: Oversee the end-to-end BRT system architecture covering vehicles, dedicated lanes or corridors, stations and platforms, traffic signal priority, passenger information, fare collection, depot and charging infrastructure, control systems, vehicle guidance, accessibility, safety and emergency systems.

  • Feasibility, Business Case and Option Evaluation: Lead assessments of alternative BRT concepts based on demand, journey time, capacity, reliability, safety, land requirements, capital and operating costs, maintainability, flexibility and scalability. Develop whole-life cost and benefit assessments to support investment decisions.

  • Stakeholder and Government Coordination: Lead engagement with internal LTA divisions, MOT, URA, JTC, government agencies, public transport operators, utility providers, consultants, technology suppliers and industry partners to align system requirements, corridor planning and implementation priorities.

  • Procurement and Commercial Strategy: Develop procurement strategies for the BRT system and major components, define technical and functional requirements, lead supplier and system integrator evaluation, and ensure appropriate allocation of performance, interface, reliability and lifecycle risks within contracts.

  • Safety, Reliability and Regulatory Readiness: Establish system-level safety requirements, assurance processes, hazard management approaches, testing and commissioning frameworks, and operational readiness plans for new BRT technologies and operating concepts.

  • Programme and Risk Management: Maintain the overall project risk register, monitor programme progress, cost, quality and deliverables, resolve cross-disciplinary dependencies and escalate strategic issues with recommended mitigation measures.

  • Team Leadership and Capability Building: Lead and develop a multidisciplinary BRT team, set priorities across system planning, vehicle, infrastructure, operations and technology workstreams, mentor junior officers and build organisational capability in BRT, high-capacity bus and automated transport technologies.

Your work will directly shape the future of medium-capacity public transport in Singapore by establishing a robust, evidence-based and scalable BRT concept for Tuas South, while creating a framework that could support deployment in other suitable corridors. This role offers significant national impact and senior-level visibility across transport planning, infrastructure delivery and emerging mobility technologies.
jobRequirements:
We are seeking a strategic and results-driven leader with deep interest in public transport systems, emerging mobility technologies and complex infrastructure delivery. The ideal candidate will possess:

  • Educational Background: Knowledge in Engineering, Transport, Urban Planning, Science, or a related discipline.

  • Experience: At least 10 years of relevant experience in public transport, transport infrastructure, rail, bus systems, automotive, mobility systems or major infrastructure projects. Demonstrated experience leading complex multidisciplinary projects involving multiple stakeholders will be essential.

  • Technical and Commercial Expertise: Strong understanding of public transport systems, preferably with experience in buses, rail or BRT. Experience in systems engineering, infrastructure development, vehicle technology, transport operations, major procurement, commercial strategy or project delivery will be advantageous.

  • Skills and Abilities: Excellent analytical, written, presentation, stakeholder management and project management skills, with the ability to assess emerging technologies objectively and translate concepts into practical transport solutions.

  • Attributes: A strategic, resilient and self-motivated leader who can make sound recommendations under uncertainty, manage complex risks and build alignment across diverse stakeholders.

  • Improve the design system: Work with technology colleagues to continually refine the design system, building a shared design language and component library that exhibits a high standard of craft and aesthetics.

  • Guide vendor design delivery: Review and shape what vendors produce, from concepts to final interfaces. Protect design integrity and work constructively through differences.

  • Design AI into the experience: Shape how AI is introduced to users, endeavouring to make AI clear and useful, with sensible expectations and graceful recovery.

  • Own adoption, not just launch: Track how designs function after launch. Keep improving the experience until the evidence shows it delivers meaningful value for users.

As a UX Designer in NCSS Digital Products and Platforms (DPP) division, you will help shape digital products, platforms and internal systems that enable NCSS and the social service sector to work more effectively.

You will work across the design process - from understanding users and framing problems, to prototyping, testing and supporting delivery. A key part of your role is making sense of complex services, workflows and operational constraints, and turning them into experiences that are clear, accessible and practical.

You will work closely with the Design Lead, product managers, engineers, business teams, vendors and users to ensure what we build is grounded in real needs and works in the real world. This role is suited for a designer who is curious about how things work, comfortable navigating ambiguity, and able to turn complexity into clarity through research and design.
jobResponsibilities:
Understand users and frame the right problems

  • Plan and conduct user research, including interviews, contextual inquiry, workshops, surveys, usability testing and concept validation, to uncover user needs, behaviours, pain points and service constraints.
  • Synthesise research, product data and operational knowledge into clear insights, user journeys, service blueprints and opportunity areas.
  • Frame problems through evidence rather than assumptions, helping teams align on the right priorities before moving into solutions.
  • Facilitate workshops and co-creation sessions to build shared understanding between users, stakeholders and delivery teams.
  • Turn complexity into clear experiences.
  • Simplify complex workflows, business rules and information into experiences that are intuitive, accessible and easy to navigate, while balancing user needs with business, policy, technical and operational realities.
  • Structure user journeys, task flows, interaction patterns and information architecture across digital products, platforms and internal systems.
  • Create and iterate wireframes and interactive prototypes, using testing and feedback to refine solutions from early concepts to detailed designs.
  • Apply and contribute to reusable design patterns and systems that improve consistency and quality across products.

Drive design from insight to delivery

  • Own design work from problem framing and exploration through validation and refinement.
  • Partner with product managers and engineers to shape feasible solutions, make clear trade-offs and maintain design intent through implementation.
  • Use prototypes and experiments to make ideas tangible early, reduce uncertainty and help teams make better product decisions.
  • Apply research findings, usability evidence, product data and user feedback to continuously improve products after launch.

Collaborate and influence

  • Bring together product, engineering, business, operations, vendors and other stakeholders to shape solutions that are desirable, feasible and workable.
  • Communicate research findings, design rationale and trade-offs clearly, using evidence, prototypes and storytelling to build shared understanding.
  • Advocate for users while recognising the operational and organisational context in which services need to work.
  • Constructively challenge assumptions and contribute to raising the quality and maturity of design practices across DPP.

Experiment and improve how we design

  • Explore AI-enabled and emerging tools to improve research synthesis, ideation, prototyping and design workflows, while applying sound judgement to their outputs.
  • Share practices, patterns and lessons with designers and product teams to improve how NCSS designs digital services.
jobRequirements:
Competencies

  • Thinking Clearly and Making Sound Judgements
  • Working Effectively with Citizens and Stakeholders
  • Systems Thinking
  • Project Management
  • Business Partnering


Skills Required

  • 5–8 years of experience in UX design, product design, service design or a related discipline, with experience designing and shipping digital products end-to-end.

  • Strong interaction design skills, with the ability to create clear flows and prototypes for complex workflows, systems and services.

Over the years, the department has continued to evolve and our roles expanded in tandem with the changing security environment. Today, our roles also include Counter Terrorism and Cyber Security.
jobDescription: The mission of MINDEF/SAF is achieved through the twin pillars of diplomacy and deterrence. Our soldiers train and acquire equipment from all over the world, which is made possible only through the strong assurances forged through security partnerships with our counterparts. The international engagements team is a key interface with foreign nations to forge a common understanding on security measures for the mutual protection of each other’s information.
jobResponsibilities: You will be part of a team that helps to build and strengthen security relationships with MINDEF/SAF’s security counterparts. You will help to review security agreements and various MOUs to ensure that MINDEF/SAF’s security interest is protected, and be the key point of contact when it comes to handling security requests between nations. You will be required to plan for visits by foreign counterparts and will also occasionally be assigned to staff principals’ trips overseas.
jobRequirements: Someone who has excellent communication skills and is comfortable to forge partnerships with international stakeholders. You will need the aptitude to very quickly be familiar with our protection policies, so as to effectively review security documents and agreements with partner nations. Strong grasp of the English (particularly legalistic) language is necessary, and structured writing skills is a must. Some travelling is required for this job.

jobTitle: Senior Forensic Scientist (Fire Research), Forensics COE
agency: Home Team Science and Technology Agency (HTX)
agencyDescription: HTX is the world’s first Science and Technology agency that integrates a diverse range of scientific and engineering capabilities to innovate and deliver transformative and operationally-ready solutions for homeland security. As a statutory board of the Ministry of Home Affairs and integral to the Home Team, HTX works at the forefront of science and technology to empower Singapore’s frontline of security. Our shared mission is to amplify, augment and accelerate the Home Team’s advantage and secure Singapore as the safest place on planet earth.
jobDescription:
HTX is Singapore's Science and Technology agency that brings together diverse scientific and engineering capabilities to develop transformative, operationally ready solutions for public safety. As a statutory board under the Ministry of Home Affairs, HTX works at the forefront of science and technology to empower the Home Team with cutting-edge capabilities. Guided by our mission to amplify, augment and accelerate the Home Team's advantage, we are committed to keeping Singapore the safest place on planet Earth.
 

The Forensics Centre of Expertise (CoE) in HTX plays a critical role in strengthening Singapore’s Home Team forensic capabilities through science, technology, and innovation. Leading a global shift in forensic science, the CoE’s mission extends beyond solving crimes by harnessing innovative technologies to revolutionise investigations, enhance public safety, and keep Singapore ahead of an evolving threat landscape.

We are seeking a motivated and technically strong Senior/Forensic Scientist (Fire Research) to join the HTX Forensics CoE. The jobholder will lead, identify, and actively contribute to cutting-edge research aimed at enhancing fire safety and investigation capabilities.  The role focuses on battery-related fires, electrical fires, and other emerging fire scenarios, approached from a rigorous scientific perspective. 
Key responsibilities include the design, conceptualisation, development and implementation of innovative methodologies and approaches that transcend conventional approaches, frameworks, and workflows.
The ideal candidate is hands-on, scientifically grounded, and comfortable working across multidisciplinary teams to translate operational needs into robust, deployable forensic capabilities.
jobResponsibilities:
The scope of work includes the following:
•	Conduct horizon scanning to identify novel scientific approaches/technologies/ solutions and develop game-changing or new capabilities (e.g. CFD models for battery or electrical fire scene reconstruction; novel fire suppression strategies) to enhance and support Home Team Departments and allied agencies.
•	Contribute to technical road-mapping, and develop a deep understanding of battery operating principles, degradation, and failure mechanisms, battery or electrical fire behaviour, and associated technologies and equipment, as well as proficiency in fire science analytical instruments, with the expectation of developing into a subject matter expert in battery-related fire science and other emerging new energies (sustainability and clean energy technologies).   
•	Independently spearhead research initiatives from concept to delivery, including method development, validation, field trials, performance evaluation, troubleshooting, and stakeholder engagement.
•	Support technology readiness assessment and transition of R&D outputs into operational deployment.
•	Forge collaborations with both national and international stakeholders, contributing to the advancement of HTX’s interests, and foster a robust network with pivotal stakeholders in Home Team Departments, as well as within HTX.
•	Cultivate partnerships with forensic counterparts, academia, industry peers, vendors, and other research partners and solution providers on both local and global scales, driving the innovation of fresh methodologies, practices or products.
•	Provide technical mentorship and guidance to junior scientists or project team members to facilitate collective progress. 
•	Ensure adherence to quality, safety, data integrity, cybersecurity, and ethical research practices in all development activities.
jobRequirements:
•	Possesses a tertiary qualification in material science, engineering, or a related discipline.
•	Relevant industry or research experience in fire science, lithium-ion battery and other emerging energy technologies and systems, and/or fire investigation, with strong knowledge of battery/energy storage systems, including cell components, battery pack configurations, charging & discharging mechanisms, voltage–current (V–I) characteristics, and thermal runaway mechanisms.
•	Hands-on experience with using battery testing related equipment such as Accelerating Rate Calorimeter, battery cyclic tester, impedance meters etc.
•	Proficiency in fire safety design, practices, relevant codes/standards/guidelines related to batteries, sustainability and clean energy, and/or electrical fires.
•	Experience in material characterisation techniques such as Scanning Electron Microscopy, Failure Mode and Effects Analysis (FMEA), AI-driven approaches, and/or computational methods such multi-physics computational modelling on fires will be advantageous.
•	Knowledge of research methodology, and practical experience in execution of scientific research projects in academia and/or industry.
•	Able to work in a dynamic, fast-paced environment, manage multiple concurrent technical workstreams, and address operational exigencies beyond conventional office hours.
•	Strong analytical, problem solving, and technical writing skills.
•	Demonstrated ability to work independently and effectively within multidisciplinary teams.
•	Good written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to explain technical concepts to diverse stakeholders.


* All new hires are appointed on a two-year contract in the first instance and will be assessed and considered for permanent tenure over time, based on performance. As part of the shortlisting process for this role, you may be required to complete a medical declaration and/or undergo further assessment.

All applicants will be updated on the status of their applications within 4 weeks upon closing of the advertisement.

jobResponsibilities:
As a Security Consultant in our Cybersecurity Governance & Assurance team, you will play an important role in safeguarding the systems and information that millions of CPF members rely on for their retirement, healthcare and housing needs.

You will contribute to strengthening CPF Board’s cybersecurity governance, risk management and assurance capabilities, helping to ensure that cybersecurity risks are effectively identified, assessed and managed. Working with stakeholders across the organisation, you will provide cybersecurity advice, conduct security assessments and assurance activities, and support the continuous improvement of the Board’s cybersecurity posture and resilience.

In this role, you will:

• Conduct cybersecurity risk assessments and security assurance activities across systems, applications, infrastructure, cloud environments and technology initiatives to identify security risks, vulnerabilities and control gaps, assess the adequacy and effectiveness of cybersecurity controls and recommend appropriate risk treatment and remediation measures.
• Provide cybersecurity risk and assurance advice to system owners, project teams and other stakeholders, translating findings into practical recommendations and supporting the implementation of appropriate security controls and mitigation measures.
• Assess cybersecurity risks arising from new and emerging technologies, including Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Generative AI (GenAI), as well as new solutions and changes to existing systems across application, infrastructure, network, cloud and security architecture, and contribute to the development of appropriate security, risk management and assurance measures to strengthen resilience and support secure adoption.
• Plan, coordinate and conduct penetration testing and security testing of applications, infrastructure, networks, cloud environments and other technology solutions, working with relevant stakeholders and external security testing providers, where appropriate, to address relevant cybersecurity risks and attack scenarios, identify vulnerabilities and validate the effectiveness of security controls.
• Analyse and validate penetration testing findings, assess their exploitability and cybersecurity risk, perform or coordinate retesting and validation to ensure identified security vulnerabilities are adequately addressed.
• Leverage penetration testing results together with vulnerability assessments, threat intelligence, External Attack Surface Management (EASM), Adversarial Exposure Validation (AEV) and other technical security assessments to identify systemic security weaknesses and strengthen cybersecurity assurance.
• Explore the use of scripting, automation and data analytics, including Python where appropriate, to improve the efficiency and effectiveness of cybersecurity risk assessment, assurance, monitoring and reporting activities.
• Support and participate in internal and external cybersecurity audits, reviews and regulatory assessments, including the coordination, assessment and remediation of findings.
• Assess compliance with applicable cybersecurity policies, standards, regulatory requirements and industry frameworks, and recommend improvements where necessary.
• Develop, review and enhance cybersecurity policies, standards, procedures and governance frameworks to address evolving cybersecurity risks, regulatory requirements, emerging technologies and organisational needs.
• Contribute to the continuous improvement of cybersecurity governance, risk and assurance methodologies, processes, tools and capabilities, including the adoption of threat-informed and risk-based approaches.
jobRequirements:
We value the diverse talents and experiences that each individual brings to the table. While mastery of every requirement may not be necessary, familiarity and expertise in some of the following areas will position you for success within this team.

Cybersecurity Governance & Assurance

• Relevant experience in cybersecurity, information security, technology risk, security assurance, cybersecurity governance or related areas.
• Experience in conducting cybersecurity risk assessments, security reviews, control assessments and/or other security assurance activities, and recommending appropriate risk treatment and remediation measures.
• Good understanding of cybersecurity risks, threats, vulnerabilities and security controls, with the ability to assess how these may affect systems, applications, infrastructure, network, security architecture and technology environments.
• Ability to assess cybersecurity issues and translate technical findings, vulnerabilities and control weaknesses into clear risk implications and practical recommendations.
• Familiarity with relevant cybersecurity standards, frameworks and regulatory requirements, such as the NIST Cybersecurity Framework, ISO/IEC 27001, CIS Controls, Singapore Government Instruction Manuals, and applicable cybersecurity legislation, Codes of Practice and regulatory requirements.
• Good analytical, problem-solving and stakeholder management skills, with the ability to evaluate cybersecurity risks and controls in the context of business, technology and operational requirements, and communicate cybersecurity risks and recommendations effectively to both technical and non-technical stakeholders.
• Adaptable, inquisitive and keen to broaden cybersecurity expertise through exposure to different areas of cybersecurity risk, assurance, governance and emerging technologies.
• Awareness of emerging cybersecurity threats and technologies, including developments relating to Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Generative AI (GenAI), and an interest in understanding their cybersecurity risks and implications.

Penetration Testing & Security Assessment

• Experience or knowledge in penetration testing, vulnerability assessment or security testing, including the identification, validation and assessment of security vulnerabilities.
• Good understanding of common application, infrastructure, network and cloud security vulnerabilities, attack techniques and security controls, including familiarity with frameworks and references such as the OWASP Top 10, OWASP Web Security Testing Guide (WSTG), MITRE ATT&CK and CVSS.
• Familiarity with penetration testing methodologies and commonly used security testing tools, such as Burp Suite, Nmap, vulnerability scanners and other relevant security assessment tools.
• Ability to analyse penetration testing and vulnerability assessment findings, assess their exploitability, potential impact and cybersecurity risk, and translate technical findings into practical remediation recommendations.
• Ability to document and communicate security testing findings clearly to both technical and non-technical stakeholders and work with system owners and technical teams to address identified vulnerabilities.

Experience or knowledge in one or more of the following areas would be an advantage:

• Hands-on experience conducting web application, API, mobile application, infrastructure, network, Active Directory or cloud penetration testing.
• Experience in Red Teaming, Purple Teaming, adversarial security testing or threat-informed security assessments, including the use of realistic attack scenarios to evaluate security controls.
• Experience with External Attack Surface Management (EASM), Adversarial Exposure Validation (AEV), breach and attack simulation or continuous security validation approaches.
• Experience analysing and validating complex vulnerabilities, attack paths and chained security weaknesses beyond automated vulnerability scanning.
• Knowledge of scripting or programming languages such as Python, PowerShell or other relevant languages for security testing, data analysis or automation.
• Relevant offensive security or penetration-testing certifications, such as OSCP, OSWA, OSWE, CREST certifications, GPEN, or equivalent professional certifications.
• Relevant cybersecurity such as CISSP, CCSP, CISM, CRISC, CISA, ISO/IEC 27001, or equivalent certifications, would be advantageous.

The seniority of appointment and actual corporate job title will commensurate with individual work experiences.

Position is on a 2-year full-time contract directly under the payroll of CPF Board with potential for emplacement into a permanent position.

What you can expect
Being part of #TeamCPF means embarking on a challenging and rewarding career in a progressive workplace that values productivity and growth. Here’s what awaits you:

• Opportunities to engage in a mix of formal and informal training, keeping your skills sharp in our ever-evolving technological landscape. 
• Promotion opportunities based on your capability and on-the-job performance. 
• A vibrant community of like-minded and friendly colleagues, where collaboration and creativity thrive. 
• A hybrid work model that offers flexibility for remote work, subject to exigencies of service. 
• Flexible dress code that empowers you to choose your appropriate outfit for the day.

agencyDescription:
Join Us at MSF for a Meaningful, People-Centric Career!

At MSF, our mission is to nurture and build resilient individuals, strong families, and a caring society. jobDescription:
We want families to realise their hopes and aspirations. We want families to remain resilient when faced with challenges and bounce back higher after adversity. We want strong families as the building blocks of a caring community, where families readily help other families. 

Description of Division - Family Support Division (FSP): 
We focus on providing a continuum of support for mainstream and early-risk families in the areas of marriage, divorce and family counselling support.
jobResponsibilities:
As part of the service management team at FSP, you will design, implement, manage, and review services to support couples and families who faced stressors and challenges in their marriage and family life journey. The service management team also participates in policy discussions led by the policy teams from other MSF divisions and government agencies to provide views on operational angle. On a day-to day basis, you will partner divisions in MSF, the Family Justice Courts, the Syariah Court and Social Service Agencies (SSAs) to develop solutions in the best interest of these families. 

Job Responsibilities 
•	Communicate, operationalise and ensure adherence to programme and service requirements for MSF/FSP-appointed SSAs operating the Strengthening Families Programme (FAM) and Early Risk Marriage programmes, including translating policy intent into clear service guidance, updates and implementation instructions for agencies.
•	Ensure smooth operations at MSF/FSP-appointed SSAs by coordinating and supporting case discussions and conferences for selected cases, conducting audits, addressing operational concerns, monitoring service delivery issues and providing timely process updates.
•	Facilitate inter-agency collaboration and develop aligned, client-centric solutions with internal MSF divisions, government agencies, courts, SSAs, vendors and community partners, balancing stakeholder feedback, operational feasibility, cost, timeline and service continuity considerations.
•	Review and analyse operational data, service feedback, registration trends, client pain points and programme information to generate insights, identify support gaps and enhance understanding of client needs and service effectiveness.
•	Develop, review and update Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs), service workflows, referral processes, public-facing notices and implementation guides to ensure processes remain current, easy to understand and effective in supporting families.
•	Develop, coordinate and review training policies, plans and learning resources for counsellors and staff in MSF/FSP-appointed SSAs, including supporting induction, capability-building and consistent application of programme requirements.
•	Handle public queries, feedback and appeals professionally and sensitively, including identifying recurring pain points, coordinating responses with relevant stakeholders and recommending improvements to reduce confusion or service disruption.
•	Provide secretariat support for meetings with partners and stakeholders.
•	Any other responsibilities as accorded by the Ministry.
jobRequirements:
•	Relevant qualifications, preferably in social work, psychology, counselling, or a related discipline.
•	Past experience working directly with clients, families or vulnerable groups is an advantage, especially in marriage, divorce, counselling, family support or community-based service settings.
•	Able to work, communicate and engage well with different internal and external stakeholders, including SSAs, public agencies, courts, vendors and community partners to clarify issues, gather feedback and align parties towards common goals.
•	Demonstrates client-centricity, empathy and sound judgement when supporting families who face challenges, while balancing operational requirements and policy intent.
•	Strong project management skills, with the ability to manage timelines, coordinate multiple workstreams, follow through on clearances and approvals, and keep stakeholders updated on progress and risks.

jobDescription:
The OSC is a new government agency set up to support the office of the Commissioner of Online Safety (“Commissioner”) established under the Online Safety (Relief and Accountability) Act 2025 (“OSRAA”).

The OSC comprises four teams, namely Case Resolution (“CR”), Investigations (“INV”), Operations Policy (“OP”), and Specialised matters, Appeals and Reconsideration (“SAR”), with CR and INV being the OSC’s two frontline operational units, focused on assisting victims who report online harms get these removed from the internet as well as ensuring compliance with the directions issued by the Commissioner.

Reporting to the Commissioner, the Deputy Commissioner (Operations) is the senior leader responsible for the end-to-end delivery of OSC’s victim complaints operations. This appointment will directly oversee CR and INV, ensuring that OSC’s processes are fair, robust, trauma-informed, evidence-driven and consistent with the OSRAA, while building a high-performing organisation capable of responding to fast-evolving online harms.

You will translate strategic intent into operational reality: designing and refining complaint handling frameworks, overseeing and developing strategies for investigations and case outcomes, setting service standards, and building strong inter-agency and industry operating relationships to achieve effective victim relief.
jobResponsibilities:
Strategic leadership and organisational set-up

  • Co-develop OSC’s multi-year operational strategy and implementation roadmap with the Commissioner and other members of the OSC’s leadership team, including the OSC’s operating model, resourcing plan and performance measures.
  • Establish the OSC as a trusted authority for online safety victim complaints through transparent standards, consistent decision-making and measurable service quality.
  • Establish the OSC’s as a global thought leader for online harm victim relief.

Oversee the OSC’s case resolution and investigations (core accountability)

  • Lead and partner with Assistant Commissioner (Case Resolution & Investigation) in owning the end-to-end lifecycle for the reporting of online harms, including intake, triage, evidence gathering, investigations, case assessment, outcomes issuance and post-outcome follow-up.
  • Set and enforce casework quality standards (e.g., timeliness, consistency, proportionality, victim-centred practice, record-keeping and audit trails).
  • Develop investigation protocols and escalation pathways for complex, high-risk or high-impact cases (e.g., coordinated or crossfire harassment, high virality online harmful activity, involving highly vulnerable victims).
  • Drive continuous improvement using case data and trend analysis to refine triage logic, prioritisation rules and operational playbooks.

Operational policy, frameworks and controls

  • Architect and maintain OSC’s operational frameworks and internal policies to implement OSRAA effectively (including guidance, decision frameworks, standard operating procedures and training standards).
  • Ensure strong governance, risk management and internal controls across case operations (including information handling, evidentiary integrity, oversight checks and process assurance).

Stakeholder engagement and ecosystem collaboration

  • Build and sustain effective working relationships with relevant government agencies, technology platforms, app stores, industry partners and community organisations to enable timely victim relief and reduce friction in cross-entity case handling.
  • Represent OSC in operational coordination fora, driving shared protocols and clear lines of accountability during incidents and surges.

People leadership, capability building and culture

  • Build, lead and develop multidisciplinary teams (e.g., case resolution officers, investigators, operations policy officers).
  • Establish a culture of professional rigour, empathy, learning and resilience, including strong supervision practices and quality coaching for case resolution officers.
  • Put in place workforce wellbeing measures, including structured debriefs, vicarious trauma support and safe operating norms for exposure to harmful content.

Corporate leadership and organisational management

  • Provide senior oversight of operational planning and resource allocation; partner corporate functions on workforce planning, budgeting, procurement, performance management and internal communications.
  • Support external communications on OSC’s operations (where appropriate), balancing public assurance with confidentiality and operational sensitivity.
jobRequirements:
Experience and domain expertise

  • At least 10 years’ supervisory experience leading operations, investigations, trust & safety, technology policy, regulatory operations, enforcement, or complex service delivery in public or private sectors.
  • Demonstrated experience in designing and running high-volume, high-stakes casework operations with clear service standards and quality controls.
  • Familiarity with how online platforms operate (including content moderation and enforcement processes, reporting tools, recommender systems at a conceptual level, and app ecosystem dynamics). Experience with online trust & safety, public policy, or online content regulation is advantageous.

Leadership and professional competencies

  • Strong judgment and ability to lead decision-making in ambiguous, sensitive and time-critical situations.
  • Excellent stakeholder management—able to build constructive partnerships while holding firm to statutory intent, public interest outcomes and operational integrity.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to craft operational policies, decision rationales, and executive-level briefings.
  • Proven people leader who can build capability, create psychological safety, and enforce high standards of professional conduct and confidentiality.

Resilience and wellbeing

  • You may be exposed to graphic content including (but not limited to) sexual material, minor safety, suicide and self-harm, violent extremism and bullying. (C2R) Group. C2R strengthens the cybersecurity and resilience posture of
the telecommunication and media sectors in Singapore.

trusted, and robust against an evolving and increasingly
complex threat landscape.
jobResponsibilities:
• Proactively identify and mitigate cyber threats to Singapore's digital infrastructure by designing and executing structured threat hunting programmes, reporting to the Advanced Cybersecurity Division lead and collaborating closely with asset owners and security teams across IMDA.
  • Design and deliver comprehensive Cyber Threat Hunting programmes, establishing structured methodologies and frameworks to proactively surface hidden threats across Singapore's digital infrastructure.

  • Manage and coordinate threat hunts with asset owners and security teams, ensuring hunts are conducted in a structured, collaborative and operationally responsible manner.

  • Proactively track evolving cyber threats, threat actor profiles and emerging attack techniques to continuously update and enhance the organisation's threat hunting capabilities and intelligence posture.

  • Draft comprehensive reports and present findings, threat assessments and actionable recommendations clearly to both technical teams and senior stakeholders.

  • Relevant experience in threat hunting and risk assessment would be a distinct advantage, particularly in complex enterprise or critical infrastructure environments.

  • Good communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to present technical findings and threat intelligence clearly to both technical and non-technical audiences.

The Child Development (CD) division in ECDA spearheads a wide range of initiatives to support young children with developmental needs and young children from lower-income families, to ensure that they have a good start. You will also provide guidance to programme teams on funding arrangements, compliance requirements, documentation standards and risk management.

You will analyse grant, budget, operational and audit information to identify trends, risks and opportunities for improvement, and translate findings into practical recommendations for management, funding reviews and programme oversight.

You will lead improvements to grant administration processes through standardisation, process redesign and system enhancements, working with programme teams, Finance, Audit and system teams to streamline workflows, strengthen audit trails and improve data capture.

jobDescription:
Position Overview

The Land Policy team drives planning and policy development on industrial land and space to support Singapore’s manufacturing sector and long-term economic growth. The team also oversees policy and corporate matters relating to JTC Corporation as a 5th Schedule Statutory Board.

As Deputy Director (Land), you will lead a team to formulate and implement industrial land policies that ensure Singapore has the land and infrastructure needed to support economic transformation, attract investments, and anchor high-value manufacturing activities. Working closely with economic agencies, planning agencies, and industry stakeholders, you will shape policies that keep Singapore’s industrial landscape competitive, sustainable and responsive to emerging opportunities.

Drawing on rigorous data analysis and extensive stakeholder engagement, you will oversee efforts to understand economic and industrial land market trends, sharpen policy levers, and ensure that industrial land resources are deployed effectively to support Singapore’s economic priorities.
jobResponsibilities:
What you will be working on

You will lead a team that works with multiple stakeholders across Government to formulate and implement Singapore’s industrial land and space policies. This includes:
•	Leading a fundamental review of Singapore's industrial land pricing framework in close collaboration with the Ministry of Finance and sector agencies, ensuring our pricing approach remains competitive, sustainable and aligned with broader economic objectives.
•	Ensuring that there is sufficient industrial land and space to support Singapore’s medium- and long-term economic needs, including through the creation and safeguarding of industrial land, reviewing land recycling and intensification strategies, and identifying opportunities to optimise land use.
•	Working with MTI’s economic agencies and industry partners to ensure that industrial land policies continue to support emerging growth sectors, facilitate business transformation, and anchor investments that create good jobs for Singaporeans.
•	Partnering JTC Corporation on the development of innovative industrial facilities and next-generation industrial districts to support evolving manufacturing trends, enhance enterprise competitiveness, and improve productivity.
•	Monitoring developments in the industrial property market and working with JTC to ensure that land supply, pricing and rental policies remain stable, sustainable and competitive.
•	Overseeing policy, governance and corporate matters relating to JTC Corporation and its subsidiaries, including organisational development, fiscal sustainability, strategic planning and Board-related matters.
•	Representing MTI on inter-agency platforms and engaging industry stakeholders to build consensus, address emerging issues and advance policy objectives.
•	Leading and developing a team of officers, fostering a high-performing and collaborative team culture, while ensuring officers are given opportunities for growth and development.
jobRequirements:

You should have:
•	At least 8–10 years of relevant experience in public policy, economic development, land use planning, infrastructure planning, or related areas.
•	Strong analytical and strategic thinking skills, with the ability to assess complex policy issues and develop practical, evidence-based recommendations.
•	Excellent communication and stakeholder engagement skills, with the ability to work effectively across Government agencies, statutory boards, industry stakeholders and senior management.
•	Strong leadership and people management skills, with the ability to guide teams through ambiguity and drive outcomes in a dynamic environment.
•	The ability to appreciate and synthesise diverse perspectives, balance competing priorities, and build consensus across stakeholders.
•	A strong interest in Singapore’s economic development and industrial transformation.
•	Comfort working with data, economic concepts and market trends to support policy analysis and decision-making.

agencyDescription:

jobDescription:
The Radiation Protection and Nuclear Science Group in the National Environment Agency (NEA) is the national authority for radiation protection in Singapore and serves to protect the public, radiation workers and the environment from the harmful effects of radiation. Its Nuclear Safety Division is responsible for developing capabilities, plans and ecosystems to support national nuclear safety & security assessment, radiological emergency response, and nuclear regulatory development efforts. The division is also responsible for ensuring that Singapore fulfils its obligations to international conventions and agreements with respect to the safe and peaceful use of nuclear material and technology.

Singapore is studying the potential deployment of nuclear energy as part of its long-term energy strategy. Singapore will also need to prepare for the possibility of nuclear power deployment by other countries in the region. These endeavours involve planning and strategizing the development of legal and regulatory infrastructure required for a potential nuclear power programme and building up capabilities in nuclear safety, emergency preparedness and response and radiation protection.

You will be a key member of the team that will review and strengthen Singapore's nuclear and radiological emergency preparedness and response to a range of possible domestic and regional incidents. The team will also formulate nuclear regulatory policies and develop drawer legislation, including determining how a potential nuclear regulatory body would be set up.

This is a rare opportunity to be at the forefront of Singapore’s nuclear energy journey.
jobResponsibilities:
Nuclear is a complex and emotive topic, and requires a diverse range of expertise to fully assess its implications for Singapore.

By joining this team, you will have the opportunity to shape Singapore’s nuclear regulatory landscape, collaborate with international experts, and contribute to nuclear safety, security, safeguards and radiation protection capability building efforts domestically and regionally.

  • Lead upstream emergency planning by identifying key policy decisions, analysing options and their implications, and developing policy recommendations.

  • Develop, review and enhance radiological and nuclear emergency plans, identifying gaps and proposing improvements to strengthen Singapore's preparedness and response to both a range of possible domestic and regional incidents.

  • Collaborate closely with relevant stakeholder agencies to develop and operationalise emergency response plans, ensuring alignment across the whole-of-government.

  • Engage international organisations such as the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) and draw on the expertise of mature nuclear regulators for guidance on emergency plan development and exercise scenario planning.

  • Organise table-top exercises; ensure that emergency response capabilities are always kept current and operationally ready for deployment.
jobRequirements:

  • Degree in science or engineering.

  • Excellent analytical, coordination and communication (written and verbal) skills are critical for this position.

  • Aptitude to understand concepts in radiation protection and nuclear technology and communicate with internal and external stakeholders in a clear and concise manner.

jobDescription:

As Manager / Senior Manager, you will work closely with SWDA's leadership to develop and strengthen the ecosystem of career and employment services partners, define and uphold quality standards for career and employment services such as career planning services, and support the development of career and employment services practitioners. You will play a key role in shaping how the ecosystem operates, identifying opportunities for collaboration, and ensuring that services delivered across the ecosystem are aligned with SWDA's vision of quality career and employment services.

  • Specifically for career planning services, to
    • Design and refine pathways that support career practitioners in building and sustaining the skills, knowledge and professional practices needed to deliver quality career planning services
    • Review and assess the effectiveness of existing standards and professional development initiatives, recommending enhancements to ensure they remain relevant, rigorous and aligned with evolving workforce needs

  • Identify and engage relevant partners from intermediaries, Trade Associations and Chambers (TACs), HR service providers, and Institutes of Higher Learning (IHLs) to collectively review and strengthen the quality of career and employment services
  • Facilitate structured conversations and working sessions with ecosystem partners to surface synergies, identify gaps, and develop collaborative initiatives that enhance service delivery across the ecosystem
  • Engage internal stakeholders across SWDA to ensure alignment on ecosystem strategies, share insights from the ground, and co-develop approaches that support the broader goals of the organisation

jobDescription:
The Fiscal Policy Directorate in MOF is responsible for formulating and implementing fiscal strategies and frameworks to optimise the allocation of finite public resources, to maintain macroeconomic stability (e.g. through countercyclical fiscal policies), support economic growth, and promote social equity. This requires making difficult trade-offs across competing strategic priorities in the social, economic, security and infrastructure domains, while considering progressivity and inter-generational equity. Our work ensures that we can balance the budget and have sufficient resources to advance Singapore’s key priorities, for the benefit of Singaporean households and businesses. 

We ensure fiscal sustainability over the medium to long term by setting out plans for our revenue (e.g. taxes, returns on investment of reserves, Government fees), financing (e.g. use of bonds), expenditure, and public sector manpower priorities. This requires close collaboration with our colleagues across MOF, as well as other Government agencies.  

We are looking for a self-driven and highly motivated individual, with an interest in working with data, to join our dynamic and collaborative team. You will have the opportunity to gain a strategic overview of the government’s priorities, manage trade-offs among competing needs, and shape the public policy agenda. You will also have the opportunity to review and operationalise our budgetary policies (e.g. Block Budgets, Programme Budgets, Reinvestment Fund, Manpower Management Framework, debt management) to support our macro-allocation objectives. As a Fiscal Policy Associate, you will be required to consult widely at all levels, synthesise and analyse information effectively, generate robust policy options and exercise sound judgment over trade-offs.
jobResponsibilities:
Key areas of work could involve the following: 

Policymaking 
1.	Formulate, review and implement fiscal, budgeting, revenue, financing, debt management and public sector manpower policies to enable optimal allocation of resources across the Government and ensure fiscal sustainability 

Strategic Planning 
2.	Horizon scanning and research of future economic and social challenges/opportunities, and study the implications for Singapore 
3.	Formulate Singapore’s fiscal strategies and response to these key challenges and seed ideas for major public policy shifts 

Managing Stakeholders and Trade-offs 
4.	Work closely with stakeholders to shape the Government’s revenue and expenditure plans and ensure alignment and coherence with the Government’s strategic priorities 
5.	Analysis of fiscal impact of major policy changes and public spending programmes and manage the trade-offs across different sectors 

Data Analytics 
6.	Analyse fiscal and macroeconomic data to sense-make the impact of fiscal policies 
7.	Model and project our revenue and expenditure over the medium to long term

•	Keen interest in public policy.

agencyDescription:

• Civil Aviation and Air Transport
• Maritime and Ports
• Land Transport

Besides providing an efficient and cost-effective transportation in Singapore, it also strives to make Singapore an international civil aviation and maritime centre for the region.

The ministry sets the strategic and policy direction while operations and regulatory works are carried out by the statutory boards under its charge. •	Serve as a subject matter expert and trusted technical advisor to Home Team Departments on enterprise infrastructure services and sustainment matters.
•	Lead automation initiatives that improve service delivery, operational efficiency and support effectiveness.
•	Work with project teams early in the planning phase to incorporate maintenance, supportability and operational readiness considerations into project requirements.

•	Establish best practices, operational support standards and maintainable infrastructure designs across MHA and HTX.

•	Work on enterprise ICT infrastructure that supports national security operations and frontline Home Team agencies.
•	Gain exposure to large-scale infrastructure sustainment, technology refresh, automation and cybersecurity initiatives.
•	Collaborate with multidisciplinary teams across engineering, operations, cybersecurity and service delivery.
•	Contribute to reliable, secure and operationally ready services that make a meaningful impact.
