jobDescription: Executive Engineer / Engineer, Vehicle Technology
jobResponsibilities:
You will play a key role in safeguarding the cybersecurity of vehicles on Singapore's roads. You will contribute to the regulatory oversight, technical audits, and compliance assessments of vehicle cybersecurity systems submitted for approval — evaluating technical evidence, conducting structured audits, investigating cybersecurity incidents, and performing targeted technical checks as part of the vehicle approval process. Your key responsibilities include:

  • Regulatory Audit Assessment — Evaluate cybersecurity documentation and test reports to ensure compliance with relevant standards and requirements, including assessments based on Cybersecurity Assurance Levels (CAL). Where necessary, you may conduct penetration testing, fuzzing, and vulnerability scanning to assess a vehicle's cybersecurity posture and identify potential vulnerabilities.

  • Incident Investigation — Lead and support cybersecurity incident investigations involving approved vehicles or in-market fleets. Analyse technical evidence, assess the scope and severity of incidents, and determine whether manufacturers have fulfilled their obligations under applicable regulations. Technical testing may be conducted on a case-by-case basis to support findings.

  • Review of Annual Reports — Assess the completeness and technical rigour of cybersecurity annual reports submitted by manufacturers, including test logs and Vehicle Security Operation Centre (vSOC) monitoring data. Ensure that the evidence meets the standards required for regulatory acceptance.
jobRequirements:
• Knowledge in Information Technology, Computer Security, Computer Science, or any other relevant fields

  • At least 3 years of relevant experience in automotive cybersecurity or a related technical field

  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills

  • Excellent communication and teamwork abilities, with a proactive approach to collaboration

Familiarity with the following will be advantageous:

  • Automotive cybersecurity standards, including ISO/SAE 21434, ISO 27001, and UN Regulations No. 155 & 156.

  • Embedded security concepts such as HSM, Secure Boot, and SecOC, along with vehicle communication protocols (e.g., CAN, LIN, Automotive Ethernet) and their security implications.

  • Vulnerability assessment techniques including threat modelling, fuzzing, and penetration testing, particularly in the context of connected vehicle components and attack surfaces such as telematics units, infotainment systems, and wireless interfaces.

  • Technical audit and investigation skills, including the ability to review cybersecurity documentation, produce clear and defensible findings, and conduct basic digital forensics such as evidence handling and technical analysis across vehicle systems.

As part of the shortlisting process for the role, you may be required to complete a medical declaration and /or undergo further assessment.

• Land Transport

agencyDescription: The Military Security Department (MSD)’s core business is in Counter Intelligence and internal security for MINDEF/SAF. Over the years, the department has continued to evolve and our roles expanded in tandem with the changing security environment. Today, our roles also include Counter Terrorism and Cyber Security.

You must possess good written and verbal communication skills, be an adaptable team player, and demonstrate a strong proactive learning mindset to stay ahead of rapidly evolving AI technologies. jobDescription: As Director (Assurance), you will serve as a trusted advisor and strategic partner to public agency leadership, leading high-performing internal audit teams delivering Shared IA Services to Ministries and Statutory Boards. This is not simply an audit leadership role — you will be a change agent, driving the evolution of IA practices across the public sector through digital innovation, agile methodologies, and a broadened risk lens that encompasses technology, cybersecurity, and sustainability. You will shape the future of the public sector IA community by building capabilities, professionalising practices, and fostering a culture of continuous improvement and intellectual curiosity.
jobResponsibilities:
Strategic Audit Leadership

You will direct the planning, management, and execution of risk-based audit engagements across agencies under AGD's portfolio of clients, ensuring timely delivery and consistently high audit quality. Moving beyond traditional compliance-focused auditing, you will develop and maintain a forward-looking audit universe that reflects emerging risks and align audit priorities with the broader governance and risk landscape of the public sector. You will also champion agile auditing methodologies, designing shorter and more iterative audit cycles that deliver faster, more actionable insights to stakeholders.

Digital Transformation 

You will lead the integration of data analytics, robotic process automation (RPA), and AI-assisted audit tools into the audit methodology to enable continuous monitoring and deeper audit insights. You will oversee the adoption of audit management platforms to improve workflow efficiency and documentation standards. Staying ahead of developments in generative AI, machine learning, and other emerging technologies, you will assess their applicability to the IA function and build the team's capacity to leverage these tools effectively. Experience with data analytics tools such as Power BI, or Python in an audit context will be particularly valued.

Emerging Risk and Advisory

As a strategic advisor, you will engage credibly with C-suite and senior public sector leadership, translating complex audit findings into clear, business-relevant insights that drive meaningful governance improvements. You will provide assurance and advisory perspectives on a broadened risk landscape, including IT general controls, cybersecurity risk, digital business processes, third-party and supply chain risk, and increasingly, sustainability and ESG governance frameworks. You will work closely with agency leadership to anticipate risks before they materialise, positioning IA as a forward-looking function rather than a retrospective one.

Community Building and Capability Development

You will work with IA heads across the public sector to build a vibrant community of practice, driving the development of shared frameworks, toolkits, and upskilling programmes that raise the overall standard of public sector IA. You will implement capability development roadmaps that equip IA practitioners with both technical audit competencies and digital skills — including data literacy, AI fluency, and agile ways of working. You will represent AGD in cross-agency forums and professional bodies to advance the ambition of public sector IA.

People Leadership and Culture

You will manage, mentor, and develop a team of IA professionals, building a pipeline of future audit leaders who are technically strong, digitally capable, and strategically minded. You will foster a team culture that values psychological safety, diversity of thought, intellectual curiosity, and a genuine commitment to public service excellence. Attracting and retaining talent in a competitive market will be an important part of your mandate.
jobRequirements:
•	A strong background in accountancy or a related discipline is essential, along with at least 10 years of progressive audit experience with a meaningful portion in a leadership capacity. 

•	CIA certification is preferred, and additional credentials such as CISA, CFE, CDMP would be advantageous, reflecting the multi-disciplinary nature of the modern IA director.

•	You should have demonstrated experience applying data analytics tools in an audit context, familiarity with AI-assisted audit platforms, and a working understanding of IT general controls, cybersecurity risk, and ESG governance. Experience with agile audit methodologies and continuous auditing frameworks would set you apart.

•	Excellent leadership, communication, and stakeholder management skills are essential, as is the ability to influence and engage with management at all levels — from operational teams to Audit Committees. 

•	Above all, you bring a growth mindset, a genuine enthusiasm for driving innovation in the audit profession, and a deep commitment to strengthening governance in Singapore's public sector.

jobDescription: As a Learning and Development (L&D) partner, you will play a pivotal role in shaping MSD’s high-performing workforce. You are expected to engage and collaborate closely with our internal stakeholders to drive performance, growth and capability development. A key aspect of your role will be partnering with Divisions to conduct comprehensive training needs analysis, identifying skills gaps and learning requirements to develop targeted solutions that address their specific needs. These responsibilities include developing, implementing, and reviewing competency frameworks and training roadmaps, as well as designing and implementing L&D strategies, plans, and policies. You will collaborate with external stakeholders (MINDEF/SAF, Whole-of-Government (WoG) agencies, and commercial entities) to source, manage, and evaluate local and overseas training courses to ensure alignment with MSD’s L&D objectives and evolving training needs. jobResponsibilities:
As a Learning and Development (L&D) Partner, you will contribute across the full spectrum of learning capability development. Your key responsibilities include: 
• Develop, implement, and review L&D policies, competency frameworks, training plans, and roadmaps in close collaboration with internal stakeholders to support their long-term capability development. 
• Manage and review local and overseas training programmes to ensure they remain relevant, comply with governance standards, align with MSD’s organisational strategy and adapt to the changing workforce needs. 
• Coordinate and manage training operations, from budget planning and training providers management to participant enrolment and stakeholder engagement, while ensuring smooth logistical execution. 
• Design, deliver, and evaluate in-house training and curricula using varied instructional methods suited for adult learners across different skill levels. 
• Use feedback and evaluation data to assess training effectiveness and enhance both programme quality and outcomes. 
• Source, curate and collaborate with partners (e.g., MINDEF/SAF, Whole-of-Government, commercial providers) on their course delivery, training resources, and evaluation efforts. 
• Provide regular progress updates, key findings, and strategic recommendations to Management to inform L&D decisions and goals.
jobRequirements: You should possess a tertiary qualification, preferably in a relevant discipline, along with at least 3 years of related work experience. Strong team player, effective written and verbal communication, and stakeholder management skills are essential. You should also have a good understanding of user-centric design and change management principles, as well as strong analytical and organisational abilities. The ability to think and take a systematic approach to implementing L&D policies and executing learning interventions in a timely manner is critical. Additionally, strong planning, coordination, and people management skills are important for executing training plans and managing courses effectively while optimising training resources. The ability to work both independently and collaboratively in a fast-paced, dynamic environment is key to success in this role.

MOH’s responses to these challenges include preventing and managing the outbreak of diseases such as SARS and Influenza A (H1N1), designing a healthcare system that delivers care in an integrated and effective manner, growing the capacity and capabilities within the sector, and managing healthcare inflation.

As an MOH officer, you will be involved in formulating and implementing policies that guide Singapore’s healthcare ecosystem. You will work alongside a team with varied skills and backgrounds, but with the common goals of (i) promoting good health and reducing illnesses; (ii) ensuring that Singaporeans have access to good and affordable healthcare; and (iii) pursuing medical excellence. Your work will have far-reaching impact on the health and lives of Singaporeans.
jobDescription:
The Division: 

Singapore keeps healthcare affordable through government subsidies and the 3Ms: MediShield Life, MediSave and MediFund. For these schemes to work, every part of the supporting systems must function accurately and without interruption. The Finance Systems Policy (FSP) division at MOH owns the systems that make this possible. These include the National Platform for Healthcare Claims, means-testing systems administering healthcare subsidise such as the Community Health Assist Scheme (CHAS), and the accreditation framework that governs which institutions and practitioners may participate in financing schemes. Together, these systems process tens of thousands of claims daily and form the operational backbone of Singapore's healthcare financing architecture.

The Role: 
 
Your starting assignment is the Financing Schemes Accreditation E-service (FSAE) system. Before a patient can use MediSave or MediShield Life at a medical institution, that institution and its practitioners must be accredited by MOH. FSAE manages that process: it handles accreditation applications, verifications, and decisions for medical institutions and practitioners across Singapore. The system operates across multiple agencies, including the Central Provident Fund Board (CPFB), the Singapore Medical Council (SMC), the Singapore Dental Council (SDC), and the Agency for Integrated Care (AIC) and so on.

A practitioner who cannot submit claims means a patient who cannot access financing for their treatments. Keeping accreditation accurate, expedient, and aligned with policy is what this role exists to do.

Over time, as you develop your understanding of FSP's portfolio, there is scope to take on other systems within the division. The capabilities you build on one system transfer directly to others.

You will be working in a fast-paced and dynamic environment that would require the ability to manage multiple priorities and stakeholders at the same time
jobResponsibilities:
Product Ownership
You will be responsible for FSAE and its related accreditation systems end-to-end. This means understanding what each system does, why it was designed the way it was, where it falls short, and how it can be improved. You will work with MOH policy teams, IT vendors, and technical teams to translate requirements into system design, develop and prioritise the feature roadmap, conduct usability and end-to-end testing, and ensure that changes work as intended before they reach end-users.
 
Policy-to-System Translation
Healthcare financing schemes evolve continuously. New services become claimable. Accreditation criteria are updated. Licensing requirements change under the Healthcare Services Act. Each change requires someone who understands both the policy intent and the system's behaviour well enough to ensure nothing is lost in translation. This thread is a distinct part of the role, not a subset of product ownership.
 
Operational Continuity
Accreditation is not a set-and-forget process. Institutions encounter issues. Data needs to be reviewed and sometimes corrected. Systemic problems need to be identified, traced, and resolved before they compound. You will maintain oversight of day-to-day system health, manage data access and sharing in accordance with whole-of-government data governance guidelines, and handle requests from external stakeholders appropriately.
 
This is not a delivery coordination role. It requires genuine ownership of both the policy intent behind a system and the technical design that carries it out.
 
The Team: 
You will report to an Assistant Director in FSP and work within a division of about 14 officers. 

FSP runs a structured capability development programme for its officers, built around four areas: product thinking, policy domain knowledge, communications, and technical skills. In practical terms, this means that 18 months in, you should be able to read a policy paper and interrogate whether FSAE's design actually implements it, hold your own in a technical review with a vendor, and produce a brief that helps Senior Management make a good decision.
jobRequirements:
We are looking for someone with 3 to 5 years of working experience in policy, operations, technology, or a field that required you to translate between these domains.
 
Beyond that, what matters is how you think. You should be able to form a clear view from incomplete information, hold it under pressure, and communicate it without ambiguity across technical, operational, and policy teams.
 
Key competencies required:
 
•	Thinking Clearly and Making Sound Judgements.  In FSP, this means tracing why a system behaves the way it does, identifying where it diverges from policy intent, and forming a clear recommendation with the evidence available, not the evidence you wish you had.
•	Learning and Putting Skills into Action.  Healthcare financing is a domain you build over time. What matters is the drive to understand it rigorously and to apply what you learn in a system where the consequences are real.
•	Improving and Innovating.  FSP's systems serve a policy environment that changes. The ability to identify where a process or system has not kept pace, and to propose a concrete improvement while managing the risks of change, is central to this role.
•	Working Effectively with Stakeholders.  FSAE operates across MOH, CPFB, AIC, SMC, and SDC and others. The ability to work across agencies, technical teams, and policy owners to reach a clear and workable outcome is not optional.
  
Your background is less important than how you approach problems. That said, the following thinking patterns tend to predict success in this role:
 
•	You ask why something works the way it does before accepting that it does.
•	You can hold a policy document in one hand and a system specification in the other, and identify where they diverge.
•	You build your position from evidence, not from what the room expects you to say.
•	You treat stakeholder complexity as a problem to be structured, not managed around.
 
Prior experience in healthcare, the public sector, or a regulated industry and familiarity with Singapore's healthcare financing schemes (MediSave, MediShield Life, CHAS) will be useful.

As part of the shortlisting process for this role, candidates may be required to complete a medical declaration and/or undergo further assessment.

jobDescription:
Within the Strategy, International & Research (SIR) Directorate, the Systems Governance & Operations Policy (SGP) Branch under the CaseCentral Product Office (CCPO) is responsible for establishing robust governance frameworks, operational policies, and ICT system enablers that underpin MSF's frontline social service delivery.

CaseCentral is a case management platform, which aims to empower caseworkers from the social service sector to deliver holistic, coordinated, and efficient support – driving better client and family outcomes. This role plays a critical part in ensuring the system is well-governed, operationally ready, and continuously improved to meet evolving service delivery needs.

You will support ops policy development and governance to change management, stakeholder engagement, inter-agency coordination, and product operations. Working at the intersection of policy, operations, and technology, you will partner closely with internal teams, social service agencies, and ICT stakeholders. You may also be required to supervise and guide contract, temporary, or junior staff, providing day-to-day direction and quality assurance, as well as contribute to the team's capability building through knowledge sharing, coaching peers, and supporting a learning culture.
jobResponsibilities:
1. Governance and Ops Policy Framework Development
•	Co-develop or support the review of ops policies, governance frameworks, and Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) to ensure CaseCentral operates within MSF's and Whole-of-Government (WOG) Information Management (IM) and data governance standards.
•	Translate policy intent into clear, implementable operational workflows and process documentation.
•	Proactively identify governance gaps and propose solutions to strengthen accountability and compliance across the system lifecycle.

2. System Change Governance and Prioritisation
•	Manage the end-to-end intake, assessment, and prioritisation of system enhancement requests from business owners and operational stakeholders.
•	Facilitate structured stakeholder discussions to surface needs, resolve competing priorities, and build alignment across divisions and agencies.
•	Ensure policy and operational decisions are systematically documented to support traceability, auditability and governance oversight.

3. Operationalisation and Implementation Readiness
•	Develop and refine onboarding frameworks, rollout playbooks, and SOPs to prepare agencies and users for system transitions.
•	Support data migration planning and system transition and handover activities, coordinating across technical, operational, and business teams.
•	Conduct pre-go-live risk assessments and develop mitigation plans to ensure smooth operational launches with minimal service disruption.

4. Change Management and Stakeholder Engagement 
•	Design and execute change management (CM) strategies that address people, process, and technology dimensions for CaseCentral rollouts and enhancements.
•	Build, sustain and coordinate Change Champion networks across agencies to embed ownership, drive adoption, and enable peer-to-peer support.
•	Plan, coordinate and support communications, briefings, training, and engagement sessions tailored to diverse stakeholder groups.
•	Gather systematic user feedback through surveys, focus groups, and operational reviews; synthesise insights to inform product roadmap and system improvements.

5. Cross-Agency Coordination and Data Sharing
•	Develop, operationalise and maintain the consent framework to facilitate data sharing between MSF and partner agencies.
•	Advise on data governance considerations, including data standards and flows, to support interface and integration planning across CaseCentral and partner systems.

6. System Operations and Product Operations Management
•	Oversee or manage issue triage, escalation workflows, and resolution tracking to ensure timely and effective response to operational incidents.
•	Support system performance monitoring and service review processes, working with ICT partners to maintain service levels.
•	Identify recurring operational pain points and recommend systemic improvements to enhance system reliability and user experience.

7. Documentation and Knowledge Management 
•	Develop and maintain comprehensive SOPs, user guides, process maps, and governance documentation to support consistent system operations.
•	Establish and maintain knowledge transfer frameworks to ensure institutional knowledge is preserved and accessible across teams.

8. Project and Implementation Coordination
•	Contribute to project planning, milestone tracking, and delivery coordination across workstreams involving CaseCentral and related systems.
•	Manage project risks and issues, ensuring compliance with MSF and whole-of-government project governance frameworks.
jobRequirements:
•	Strong systems thinking with the ability to connect policy intent, operational realities, and technology enablers.
•	Analytical and structured, with a disciplined approach to problem framing, documentation, and decision-making.
•	Strong stakeholder engagement skills — able to communicate with clarity and influence across diverse audiences, from frontline workers to senior management.
•	Collaborative, adaptable, and comfortable operating in a complex, multi-stakeholder environment with competing priorities.
•	Proactive self-starter with a high degree of initiative and ownership over assigned workstreams.

Qualifications and Experience
•	Relevant qualifications in any discipline. Candidates with backgrounds in Public Policy, Social Sciences, Business, Information Systems, or related fields are welcome.
•	At least 3–5 years of relevant experience in policy development, operations management, change management, or ICT governance — preferably in a public sector or social services context.
•	Experience working with case management systems, social service platforms, or government ICT projects is an advantage.
•	Familiarity with WOG governance frameworks, IM8, or data governance practices is a plus.

Only shortlisted candidates will be notified within 4 weeks from the closing date of this position.

Established in 2015, the Cyber Security Agency of Singapore (CSA) seeks to keep Singapore’s cyberspace safe and secure to underpin our Nation Security, power a Digital Economy and protect our Digital Way of Life. CSA also engages with various stakeholders to heighten cyber security awareness, build a vibrant cybersecurity ecosystem supported by a robust workforce, pursue international partnerships and drive regional cybersecurity capacity building programmes. It also plays an important role in digital anti-scams, safeguarding the life savings of those who live and work in Singapore. 
This is more than just a technical role — it’s a national mission, a calling. You will play a pivotal role in keeping Singapore’s cyberspace safe and secure, watching out for cybersecurity threats, tailoring advice for constituents to protect themselves, and providing guidance to constituents who have encountered a cybersecurity incident.

As a HAS (ICA) Direct-Entry Sergeant, you are responsible for the implementation and enforcement of the laws, regulations and policies of the various work of the Department. Your duties and responsibilities include the screening of passports and passengers on arrival and departure, participation in operations against smugglers, investigations, and conducting of raids against illegal immigrants.
 
[ STARTING SALARY ]
Diploma holders (5 local polytechnics / NAFA / LASALLE) - $2,870 to $3,233
GCE ‘A’ Level holders (including pass in GP / KI), IB Diploma / NUS High School Diploma - $2,870 to $3,233
Higher Nitec, Nitec and GCE ‘O’ Level holders - $2,342 to $2,618
*Starting salary will vary according to assessment during interview, relevant work experience and completion of full-time National Service.
 
[ $30,000 SIGN-ON BONUS ]
Newly appointed Direct Entry Sergeant will receive a sign-on bonus of $30,000, with $12,000 paid upon signing on and $18,000 upon confirmation after a one-year probation.
 
[ RETENTION PAYOUTS ]
Attractive retention payouts of $5,000 paid every 4 years, up to a maximum of 28 years.
 
[ BENEFITS ]
•            14 - 18 days vacation leave
•            Medical & dental subsidies
•            Group Life insurance
•            Sponsorship for continuous education
•            Use of government holiday bungalows
•            Subsidies for sports and recreation activities
•            Performance and annual bonuses
•            Marriage / Child benefits
•            Birthday vouchers

You will undergo a 20-week non-residential ICA Basic Course (Sergeant) at the Home Team Academy, which will equip officers with the knowledge and skills to perform their duties. After your foundation posting, you will be deployed to other Checkpoints or Divisions where you will be given opportunities to perform specialised functions such as profiling, participation in operations against smugglers, investigation and conducting of raids against illegal immigrants.

We're looking for an AI Engineer working on LLM/LMM Operations to join our team working at the intersection of large language models and production systems. You'll help build and maintain the systems that powers our model fine-tuning workflows, RAG pipelines and deployment processes while partnering closely with application teams.

This setup gives our team the freedom to experiment and iterate quickly on R&D projects without cloud cost constraints or API rate limits. You'll work directly with this hardware to improve training runs, benchmark different approaches, and push the boundaries of what's possible with current models. 
 
We primarily work with open-source frameworks and in-house trained models, giving you the flexibility to choose the right tools for each challenge. Experience deploying models using Docker, Kubernetes, or cloud ML platforms 
 
Practice building or maintaining production ML systems 
 
Understanding of the operational challenges in keeping ML systems running reliably 
 
Nice to Have 
 
Experience with vector databases, embedding models, and retrieval systems 
 
Familiarity with model evaluation methods and metrics 
 
Experience with experiment tracking tools (MLflow, Weights & Biases, etc.) 
 
Knowledge of CI/CD practices for ML workflows 
 
You'll Thrive Here If 
 
You care about the details but don't lose sight of the bigger picture 
 
You can debug a failing deployment pipeline and think strategically about what metrics matter 
 
You communicate well with both technical and non-technical teammates 
 
You're comfortable working in an environment where requirements evolve as we learn

jobResponsibilities:

•	Architect data curation pipelines, including data curation and synthetic data generation, for textual and multimodal training datasets
•	Develop custom evaluation metrics and automated pipelines to assess model performance and alignment
•	Leverage SLURM for efficient job scheduling and compute resource management in high-performance computing environments
•	Implement advanced model optimisation techniques, including mixed-precision training and model parallelism 
•	Partner with cross-functional teams to integrate foundational models into agentic workflows and downstream applications
•	Co-author research publications and collaborate closely with academic and industry partners to push the frontier of Sovereign AI

You may specialise in one or more areas in the team:
•	Data: Build scalable data curation pipelines for large-scale textual, multimodal, and agentic training datasets. Perform data ablations, build synthetic generation engines, and design novel curation techniques
•	Training: Build robust distributed training pipelines. Run pre-training and post-training (e.g., SFT, DPO, GRPO) experiments for LLMs / LMMs, and design large scale Reinforcement Learning frameworks for agentic model development
•	Evaluation: Design custom LLM/LMM evaluation metrics. Build and integrate continuous evaluation pipelines into the training framework for testing model checkpoints
•	Alignment and Constitution: Develop frameworks for model alignment and safety. Research scalable oversight, constitutional AI, and preference tuning methodologies to align agentic models with human intent
•	Science: Drive foundational research on emerging topics, such as domain adaptation, language transfer, efficient AI architectures, and constitutional agentic AI

•	Bring excellent problem-solving skills and a low-ego, highly collaborative mindset to the team

jobResponsibilities:
As an AI Engineer (Infrastructure Automation), you will contribute to the next generation of autonomous infrastructure by developing intelligent agents that execute real-world engineering tasks across Cloud, Networking, and Site Reliability Engineering (SRE) domains. Working closely with senior architects and engineering teams, you will apply AI and software engineering principles to solve complex systems problems — from automated environment provisioning to self-healing infrastructure.

In this role, you will:
• Develop and test AI agents by writing clean, modular code that interfaces with infrastructure APIs across platforms such as AWS, Azure, Kubernetes, and Terraform.
• Implement safety-first validation logic and security filters to ensure agents operate predictably, securely, and within defined boundaries.
• Build and maintain orchestration tooling for agents, including custom functions, API wrappers, and connectors that extend agent capabilities.
• Monitor agent performance, troubleshoot execution failures, and refine agent logic based on real-world operational feedback.
• Collaborate across SRE and Networking teams to understand pain points and translate them into practical automated agent workflows.
jobRequirements:
We value the diverse talents and experiences that each individual brings to the table. While mastery of every requirement may not be necessary, familiarity and expertise in some of the following areas will position you for success within this team.
• Relevant experience in AI or software engineering, with a focus on automation, agent development, or infrastructure systems engineering.
• Proficiency in Python, including asynchronous programming and API integrations, with the ability to write clean and maintainable code.
• Experience in working with AI libraries and frameworks such as LangChain or LangGraph.
• Familiarity with at least one major cloud provider (AWS, GCP, or Azure) and working knowledge of containerisation tools such as Docker or Kubernetes.
• Knowledge of Infrastructure-as-Code tools such as Terraform or Ansible, as well as best practices in Git and CI/CD pipelines.
• Understanding of core networking concepts, including IP addressing, DNS, and firewalls.
• Knowledge of cybersecurity principles, including the least privilege principle, defensive coding practices, and exposure to Shift Left security approaches.
• Communicates effectively, both in writing and speaking, with the ability to explain technical logic clearly and document work thoroughly.
• Works independently and manages priorities effectively in a fast-paced engineering environment.
• Adaptable and resourceful in handling varied tasks and challenges, with the curiosity to navigate complex systems and understand their intricacies.

The seniority of appointment and actual corporate job title will commensurate with individual work experiences.

Position is on 2-year full time contract directly under the payroll of CPF Board with potential for emplacement into permanent position.

jobDescription: We are seeking a highly experienced and strategic candidate to join our Programme Management Team as a lead, overseeing the design development and implementation of critical high-security building facilities. jobResponsibilities:
(A)	Design Coordination and Management

agencyDescription:
Join Us at MSF for a Meaningful, People-Centric Career!

At MSF, our mission is to nurture and build resilient individuals, strong families, and a caring society. We offer meaningful and impactful people-centric careers in the design and delivery of policies, services and programmes. We are an all-inclusive and family friendly workplace where career growth is prioritised through a comprehensive suite of development opportunities to help our officers succeed today as well as be future-ready. We do this through various formal and informal learning and development programmes for officers to build different competencies and gain diverse work experiences within MSF, the Public as well as the Social Service Sectors.
jobDescription:
Description of Group:

You will be part of the Rehabilitation and Protection Group (RPG) that undertakes the statutory functions in the rehabilitation of adult and youth offenders, and the protection of children, families and vulnerable adults (VAs). Guided by our mission to prevent harm, protect and rehabilitate individuals, and strengthen families at risk, RPG strives toward its vision of transformed lives and safe, thriving families. 

At RPG, you will find a dynamic and supportive environment dedicated to your professional growth while being part of the broader MSF community that invests in career development. You will have access to resources to build essential capabilities and deepen your expertise, ensuring you are equipped to make a meaningful impact. 

Whether you are exploring different career paths within RPG or the wider MSF network, you will receive the resources and support needed to reach your full potential. With carefully curated programs and initiatives, we invest in your growth so you can thrive in a fulfilling and impactful career.

Description of Branch:

The People and Organisation Development (POD) branch is committed to placing people at the heart of the organisation, ensuring RPG’s workforce is not only equipped with the right skills and capabilities, but also enabled and empowered to thrive in a workplace that is healthy, engaged and aligned to the organisation’s vision, mission and values.  

POD maintains an overview of RPG’s learning and development needs, planning and implementing capability development programmes and talent management strategies to ensure that RPG’s workforce remains competent and future-ready. 

Through co-designing and co-delivering of facilitated dialogues, engagement platforms and workplan discussions, POD supports the organisation development needs of RPG. Working with RPG Divisions and leadership, POD diagnoses, designs and implements targeted interventions to improve workplace dynamics and organisational effectiveness. POD also sense-makes current climate by drawing on data from engagement surveys, using these insights to strategise, plan and implement staff engagement initiatives to strengthen RPG’s culture.
jobResponsibilities:
As part of the Organisation Development (OD) unit in POD, you will
•	Plan and implement staff engagement initiatives to strengthen engagement and build a healthy organisational culture 
•	Design ways to systematically collect data as a means to track ground sentiment on how staff are perceiving the workplace 
•	Analyse employee engagement and pulse survey data to identify organisational strengths, gaps, root causes, and translate insights into action plans
•	Support the design and delivery of small- and large-group engagements (e.g. townhalls, organisational events) to strengthen communication and staff engagement
•	Support the development and implementation of change management strategies to align to and support organisation-wide transformation efforts (e.g., partnering senior leadership to develop vision, mission, and change narratives that guide organisational direction)
•	Oversee and render secretariat support for relevant Group-level meetings

Responsibilities: 

Reporting to Senior Assistant Director, you will drive culture-building and staff engagement initiatives within RPG. You will work closely with stakeholders (including partner Divisions and senior leadership) to diagnose organisational challenges, design evidence-based interventions, and support large-scale change activities across multiple divisions.
jobRequirements:
Competencies required: 

Key Competencies

•	Basic understanding of organisation development and systems thinking
o	Able to appreciate how the external environment can impact the organisation and how different parts of an organisation are connected 
o	Understand how culture impacts an organisation’s business, and how it is expressed within organisations 
o	Possess foundations of OD theory and practice, with knowledge of relevant tools for diagnosis and change 
o	Ability to support the design and delivery of facilitated discussions 
•	Stakeholder engagement 
o	Able to relate and work with people from various backgrounds and seek relevant input from them for work tasks 
•	Employee experience and service design 
o	Able to design and enhance employee experience by analysing user needs, reviewing policies and programmes, and translating insights into meaningful service journeys and interventions that support organisational goals. 

Work Experience
•	Experience in organisational development, staff engagement, transformation, consulting, or related fields
•	Experience in supporting or leading staff engagement / change initiatives
•	Experience in working with range of stakeholders
•	Ability to be both a team player and work independently 

Preferred Background
•	Educational qualifications or professional background in psychology, human sciences or related disciplines
•	Relevant training in organisation development, change management and/or related fields 
•	At least 2 years of experience in the Public Service or large organisations would be an advantage

jobDescription: Families are the bedrock of our society. The goal of Family Life Group (FLG) is to build strong and resilient families, supporting them through all life stages. As the central division for FLG, the Operations Planning & Transformation (OPT) division is responsible for ops strategy, corporate planning, data and digitalisation, transformation as well as organisational development strategies for FLG.

You will be leading a team to drive digital and technology transformation plans across Family Life Group, to improve business outcomes such as user experience, service delivery and programme efficacy. Our aim is to strengthen access to FLG services and programmes and deliver MSF’s strategic outcomes of encouraging marriage and parenthood.

The role involves the following:

•	Identify and develop technology use cases that can transform core businesses/service delivery in FLG. This include working with key stakeholders to discover, design, prototype (e.g. proof-of-concepts) to scale up.

At least 8 years of experience in digital transformation, such as digitalisation of operations, leveraging digital tech to improve business outcomes, creating digital products or platforms or encouraging innovation and experimentation in digital-tech or AI. 

KEY TRAITS
-	Strong analytical and critical thinking, writing and communication skills.
-	Ability to analyse issues from a strategic and systems perspective, while having a good grasp of details and processes.
-	Strong stakeholder engagement and management skills.
-	Experience in leading teams in transformation related work.
-	Strong problem-solving skills with proven ability to deliver impact in greenfield environments
-	Strong interest in digital technology and emerging technologies (eg. AI) will be a plus

jobTitle: Manager, Strategy & Policy, National Space Agency of Singapore
agencyDescription: The Ministry of Trade and Industry (MTI) seeks to transform Singapore into a leading global city of talent, enterprise and innovation. Our mission is to promote economic growth and create good jobs to enable Singaporeans to improve their lives. In MTI, you can expect an exciting, challenging and rewarding career!
jobDescription: We are seeking a dynamic and strategic Manager (Strategy & Policy) to lead Singapore's space policy development and international engagement. This is a unique opportunity to shape Singapore's position in the global space economy and contribute to the development of international space governance frameworks.
jobResponsibilities:
As Manager (Strategy & Policy), you will spearhead critical initiatives that position Singapore as a responsible and innovative space nation. You will develop the National Space Strategy 1.0, establishing Singapore's comprehensive roadmap for space development across government, industry, and research sectors. This foundational strategy will guide Singapore's space ambitions and coordinate efforts across multiple agencies and stakeholders.

You will lead the development of national space legislation, crafting the legal framework that will govern Singapore's space activities whilst ensuring compliance with international obligations and supporting commercial space development. This includes analysing existing regulatory gaps, consulting with industry stakeholders, and designing legislation that balances innovation with responsible space governance.

Your role extends to developing Singapore's international policy positions on space matters, requiring deep analysis of emerging space technologies, geopolitical considerations, and economic opportunities. You will formulate policy recommendations that advance Singapore's national interests whilst contributing to global space governance.

On the international stage, you will represent Singapore in multilateral forums, particularly within the United Nations system, advocating for Singapore's positions whilst helping to shape international space law and norms. This includes participating in negotiations, building coalitions with like-minded nations, and contributing to the development of guidelines for responsible space activities.
jobRequirements:
•	The ideal candidate brings extensive experience in policy development, international relations, or space governance. You should have a strong understanding of international law, multilateral diplomacy, and the space sector's technical and commercial aspects. Experience in government policy work, international organisations, or space-related industries would be highly valued.
•	You possess excellent analytical and strategic thinking capabilities, with the ability to synthesise complex technical, legal, and political considerations into coherent policy recommendations. Strong communication and negotiation skills are essential, as you will engage with diverse stakeholders from government agencies, industry, academia, and international partners.
•	Familiarity with space technology, international space law, or UN processes would be advantageous.

jobDescription: In your role, you will be responsible for records compliance, audit and offsite storage and disposal functions. Ensures that restricted access reviews, audit checks and declassification activities are carried out in accordance with established schedules and standards, and that offsite records are accurately maintained, tracked and disposed of in an orderly manner.
jobResponsibilities:
Records Compliance & Audit
You will manage restricted folder access rights, ensuring they are updated promptly in line with staff movement notifications. You will coordinate file plan reviews with the respective department records management representatives, following up to ensure reviews are completed on schedule. You will also issue audit reminders, track responses, and maintain the non-compliance table with findings and follow-up actions. Beyond these review cycles, you will support the unit's digitisation programme for archival transfer by planning the scanning schedule and verifying scanned files against quality standards. You will also assist in the redaction of declassified files as part of the unit's declassification work.

Offsite Storage & File Disposal 
You will manage the unit's offsite records, including maintaining and updating the master listing, extracting carton listings and processing permanent-out of cartons in the vendor’s system portal. You will coordinate retrieval and collection requests through the vendor’s system portal and support file disposal exercises including the serialised cable ties exercise, ensuring all actions are properly documented and authorised.

Administrative & Vendor Support
You will support the unit's administrative and vendor management functions by preparing and submitting approvals for service maintenance of office equipment and service contracts.
jobRequirements:
•	Prior experience in a registry or records management environment would be an advantage
•	Familiarity with electronic document and records management systems and offsite records management portals 
•	Detail-oriented and organised, with the ability to manage operational processes and deadlines
•	Able to navigate IT systems with ease and pick up new digital tools and platforms readily

You will play a lead role in managing international contractors for the supply, design, manufacture, install, test and commission of the Signalling and Platform Screen Doors systems for both the new MRT Lines as well as extension/enhancement to Existing MRT Lines in Singapore.

You will be involved in design review, supervision of equipment delivery and installation, involves in overseas and on-site testing and commissioning. You are expected to be familiar with local safe work practices as well as to develop a good understanding of the system design. You are required to work closely with contractors to manage and monitor the project deliverables as well as in ensuring the safety, quality, and progress of the project works. You will be involved in reviewing and managing project risks and cashflows as well as issuance of engineering instructions and conduct assessment of projects variations/ payments/ claims. PRINCIPAL / SENIOR / EXECUTIVE ENGINEER
(SOLUTION ARCHITECT - INFRASTRUCTURE & SECURITY)
jobResponsibilities:
We are seeking a passionate and experienced Solution Architect to play a key role in the modernisation of Singapore’s Automatic Fare Collection (AFC) system, which supports Account-Based Ticketing & Card-Based Ticketing, to deliver seamless, secure, and scalable public transport experience. This is a high-impact opportunity to contribute to the digital transformation of Singapore's public transport infrastructure and help shape solutions that are seamless, secure, and built to scale.

As part of the System Architecture and Assurance Division, you will lead end-to-end solution design, architecture governance, and technical assessments across a complex landscape of payment systems, cloud services, and multi-vendor integrations — ensuring reliability and security at a national scale.

What You Will Do

  • Architect secure, scalable, and high-availability solutions for AFC and payment systems, including those built on EMV, open-loop standards, account-based ticketing, and card-based ticketing models in the GCC2.0 AWS environment.

  • Design and govern end-to-end system integration architectures across distributed, multi-vendor environments, leveraging event-driven patterns and message-oriented middleware including messaging protocols such as MQ and MQTT, communication protocols such as HTTP/S and WebSockets, and integration patterns such as REST APIs, webhooks, and pub/sub architectures, to support both real-time and asynchronous processing needs.

  • Lead security architecture design to ensure compliance with Govtech’s IM8 and security requirements to safeguard sensitive payment and commuter data.

  • Lead network infrastructure design, including the planning and governance of network topology, connectivity, and security controls across cloud and hybrid environments to ensure scalable, resilient, and secure deployments

  • Produce and maintain system architecture and networking infrastructure diagrams, API and interface specifications, and integration designs with clear documentation of network infrastructure components.

  • Translate business and system requirements into high-level and detailed technical specifications, interface designs, and integration patterns suited to complex multi-system environments. Perform technical impact analysis for change requests and system enhancements, ensuring minimal disruption to mission-critical AFC operations.

  • Conduct solution walkthroughs, architecture reviews, and technical presentations for internal and external stakeholders. Collaborate with internal stakeholders (project teams, software development, operations) and external partners (vendors, financial institutions) to develop robust and future-ready solutions.
jobRequirements:
• Knowledge in Engineering, Computer Science, Information Systems, or related field.

  • At least 5 years of experience in solution architecture, systems analysis/design, or complex enterprise IT infrastructure.

  • Networks and Protocols — working knowledge of common network and communication protocols such as TCP/IP, HTTP/S, FTPS, and SFTP, and the OSI model as applied to enterprise system design.

  • Enterprise Integration Patterns — experience designing solutions using APIs, webhooks, WebSockets, message queues, MQTT, and pub/sub or event-driven architectures across complex, multi-system environments.

  • Data and Interfaces — familiarity with data serialisation formats such as JSON and binary, and how these are applied across system integration touchpoints.

  • Network Infrastructure — understanding of IP addressing, CIDR, subnets, firewalls, routers, MPLS, and availability zone design in cloud and hybrid environments.

​Bonus Skills:

  • AWS certifications (e.g., AWS Certified Solutions Architect – Associate/Professional) are strongly preferred

  • Experience in Automatic Fare Collection (AFC) systems, open-loop payment architecture, or financial-grade transaction systems.

  • Strong knowledge of security architecture, including secure data flows, tokenisation, encryption, and compliance standards (e.g., PCI DSS).

  • Hands-on exposure to DevSecOps, CI/CD, containerisation (e.g., ECS, EKS), serverless architecture, or data streaming pipelines.

  • Security and Compliance — experience embedding a defence-in-depth approach across all layers of solution design, encompassing network security, identity and access management, data protection, encryption, vulnerability management, and threat detection and response, with a strong understanding of government and industry compliance standards such as IM8 and PCI-DSS.

  • GCC AWS — familiarity with Singapore's Government Commercial Cloud on AWS, including its governance requirements and deployment constraints.

agencyDescription: The Ministry of Trade and Industry (MTI) seeks to transform Singapore into a leading global city of talent, enterprise and innovation. Our mission is to promote economic growth and create good jobs to enable Singaporeans to improve their lives. In MTI, you can expect an exciting, challenging and rewarding career!
jobDescription:
What the role is
Singapore faces increasing constraints in manpower, land, energy and carbon. Research, innovation and enterprise policy therefore plays an important role in strengthening our economic competitiveness, developing new growth opportunities and creating good jobs for Singaporeans. This requires us to make strategic choices about the technological capabilities Singapore should build, and to translate our research strengths into economic and societal outcomes.
As Singapore embarks on the new Research, Innovation and Enterprise (RIE) 2030 tranche, MTI’s Innovation, Research and Development Division develops policies and strategies to strengthen Singapore’s innovation-driven economy. We work across government, industry and the research ecosystem to identify strategic opportunities, translate research into economic outcomes and ensure that public investments in R&D deliver value for Singapore.
jobResponsibilities:
What you will be working on

You will develop and implement policies and strategies, evaluate programmes and funding proposals and oversee agency and programme performance. The role involves engaging stakeholders across government, industry and the research ecosystem in Singapore and overseas. Your responsibilities may include: 

•	A*STAR Strategy and Governance. Shape MTI’s strategic oversight of A*STAR and work with the agency to align its research, innovation and corporate strategies with Singapore’s economic priorities. This includes reviewing and advising on strategic and resourcing proposals, strengthening the translation of research into economic outcomes, monitoring organisational and programme performance, and communicating the impact of A*STAR’s initiatives.

•	National Space Strategy and Agency Development. Develop and coordinate policies and strategies to advance Singapore’s national and economic interests in space, and oversee the development of NSAS as the national space agency. This includes working with NSAS and relevant stakeholders to ensure NSAS is sufficiently resourced to achieve their mandate, and measuring, tracking and communicating the outcome of NSAS’ initiatives. 

•	Innovation & enterprise. Assess emerging technologies and growth areas to identify where Singapore can build a competitive position, and develop policies and programmes to support their growth. This includes analysing industry and technology trends, reviewing Singapore’s innovation and enterprise landscape, monitoring RIE2030 initiatives, and working with agencies to strengthen Singapore’s position as an innovation and Intellectual Property (IP) hub.

•	Manufacturing, Trade and Connectivity RIE Domain. Work with economic agencies, industry and research stakeholders to develop R&D strategies for priority economic sectors. Evaluate programme and funding proposals, monitor portfolio performance, and recommend policy and resourcing decisions to ensure that public R&D investments support Singapore’s economic priorities and deliver intended outcomes.

•	International Relations. Advance MTI’s science, technology and innovation interests through bilateral and multilateral engagements, working across whole-of-government to further our interests. This includes monitoring and assessing global innovation and R&D policy trends and strategic directions, identifying collaboration opportunities, representing MTI on international science and technology platforms (e.g. G20, ASEAN), and developing partnerships that support Singapore’s economic and technological priorities, while taking into account of geopolitical considerations.
jobRequirements:

•	Strong analytical and critical thinking skills, with the ability to examine complex, economic and technical issues, synthesise information for different audiences, and support decision-making with rigorous analysis and well-considered recommendations. 

•	Experience or interest in public policy, economic strategy, programme or scheme design, strategic planning, programme evaluation, project management as well as international relations/engagements.

agencyDescription:
The Mission of Ministry of Transport is to develop Singapore's land, sea and air transport sectors so as to enhance our economic competitiveness and quality of life in a knowledge-based economy. MOT oversees the development and regulation of the following sectors:

• Civil Aviation and Air Transport
• Maritime and Ports
• Land Transport

Besides providing an efficient and cost-effective transportation in Singapore, it also strives to make Singapore an international civil aviation and maritime centre for the region.

The ministry sets the strategic and policy direction while operations and regulatory works are carried out by the statutory boards under its charge. There are four statutory boards which are established by Acts of Parliament: the Civil Aviation Authority of Singapore (CAAS), the Land Transport Authority (LTA), the Maritime and Port Authority of Singapore (MPA) and the Public Transport Council (PTC). The ministry also oversees the operation of the Transport Safety Investigation Bureau (TSIB).
jobDescription:
Singapore is internationally renowned for our transport infrastructure and for being a global aviation and maritime hub. At the Ministry of Transport (MOT), we spearhead developments in our air, land and sea transport sectors to advance Singapore’s economic competitiveness and Singaporeans’ quality of life. We seek dynamic, analytical and committed individuals to join our able MOT team in realising our vision of a global interconnected transport hub.

If you share our vision and possess the qualities we seek, do join us!
jobResponsibilities:
The Transport Safety Investigation Bureau (TSIB) is the independent investigation authority in Singapore responsible to the Ministry of Transport for the safety investigations of air, marine and rail accidents and incidents.  The TSIB is looking for motivated and versatile Singapore citizens with dedication, diligence, patience and perseverance to join.

As a Rail Safety Investigator with a focus on autonomous vehicles, you are responsible for carrying out TSIB investigations of accidents and incidents involving autonomous vehicle operations and rail operations.  The investigation tasks include accessing accident/incident site, planning the investigation, gathering evidence, interviewing witnesses, conducting investigation meetings, reporting on progress of investigation, identifying safety issues, determining the causal or contributing factors, making safety recommendations, and writing clear and robust investigation reports. 
 
You will also be involved in or responsible for operational planning, developing investigation procedures, updating investigation legislation, conducting investigation training, organising investigation logistics, procuring investigation equipment, researching into developments in investigation techniques, preparing discussion/policy papers and promoting safety to the autonomous vehicle  and rail industries.
jobRequirements:
•	Possess relevant qualification in Computer Engineering, Computer Science, Engineering or other related fields, with an understanding of systems and coding.
•	Possess experience in the development and implementation of autonomous vehicle systems and/ or rail sector related experience 
•	Candidates with relevant supervisory experience will be preferred.
•	You should have an open, inquisitive mind, and be capable of objective, analytical and critical thinking.  You need to be a team player and have good interpersonal, communication, leadership and planning skills.  You should have an interest in technical matters and safety issues that go beyond your specialty areas.
•	You should be familiar with word processing, spreadsheet and presentation software.  A reasonable level of IT literacy and understanding of PC architecture would be an added advantage.

jobResponsibilities:
[ LEADER IN BORDER SECURITY ]

As a HAS (ICA) Direct-Entry Inspector, you are responsible for the implementation and enforcement of the laws, regulations and policies of the various work of the Department; as well as the management and operation of the various branches/commands under the Department.

Leading a team of highly-skilled and well-trained ICA officers who are tasked with the duty of protecting Singapore's gateways, you play a critical role in ensuring the security of the nation. You have to possess leadership capability, be decisive, mentally agile, and display qualities of courage and integrity. You will be trained and developed to become a professional in border security, in-land enforcement and policy implementation.

[ REMUNERATION ]

First Class Hons / Second Class (Upper) Hons - $5,310 to $6,048
Second Class (Lower) Hons / Pass with Merit / Pass - $4,890 to $5,802
*Starting salary will vary according to assessment during interview, relevant work experience and completion of full-time National Service.

[ $15,000 SIGN-ON BONUS ]

Eligible newly appointed Direct Entry Inspector will receive a sign-on bonus, with $5,000 paid upon signing on and $10,000 upon confirmation after a one-year probation. Eligible Direct Entry Inspector will also be required to serve a 3-year sign-on bond.

[ BENEFITS ]

•	18 - 21 days' Vacation Leave
•	Medical & Dental subsidies
•	Group Life insurance
•	Sponsorship for Postgraduate Study
•	Use of Government Holiday Bungalows
•	Subsidies for Sports and Recreation Activities
•	Performance and Annual bonuses
•	Marriage / Child Benefits
•	Birthday Vouchers

[ TRAINING ]

Newly appointed officers will undergo a 26-week non-residential ICA Basic Course (Inspector) at the Home Team Academy, which will equip officers with the knowledge and skills to perform their duties. Officers will be required to don on designated training attire during their basic course, which will include approved attires for physical training. 

Training includes:
•	Document examination & forgery detection
•	People, goods and vehicle screening
•	Profiling and interview techniques
•	Law and legislation
•	Firearms training
•	Control and restraint techniques
•	Protective security
•	Personal effectiveness and soft skills 
•	On Job Training
•	Leadership Training and Development (includes residential training)

Direct-Entry Inspectors are required to serve a one-year bond upon completion of training. 

[ JOB DEPLOYMENT ]

- Foundational Posting
Upon graduation from the ICA Basic Course (Inspector), officers will be deployed to one of the Checkpoints e.g. at Woodlands, Tuas, or Singapore Cruise Centre. Officers deployed at the checkpoints work on three shifts. They are also required to wear uniform while on duty.

- Developmental Posting
As part of officers' career posting and exposure to ICA's line operations, officers with suitable aptitude may be deployed to perform enforcement-related work which includes the conducting of raids against illegal immigrants, participation in operations against smugglers, contraband detection and investigations. Officers may also be deployed to the Services Centres to assess applications for travel documents, permanent residence, citizenship, identity cards or other passes/permits. The posting deployment choices extend to development of officers in the areas of planning and review, operations management and policy administration. There are also opportunities for officers to go on overseas posting stints.

jobResponsibilities:
As an Infrastructure Operations & DevOps Consultant, you will design, implement and maintain resilient cloud infrastructure that supports CPF Board’s Data Platform, enabling secure, reliable and scalable digital services for members and external organisations. Through automated CI/CD pipelines, embedded security controls and monitoring solutions, you will support efficient and secure application development and deployment.

In this role, you will:
• Design, deploy and maintain scalable Government Commercial Cloud (GCC) and on-premise infrastructure using Infrastructure as Code tools such as Terraform, to support high-performing and reliable systems processing substantial data volumes.
• Build, enhance and manage end-to-end CI/CD pipelines that automate software build, testing, security checks and release processes, enabling secure and consistent delivery with reduced manual effort and risk.
• Partner cross-functional fusion/product teams to embed DevSecOps practices into day-to-day delivery, while working closely with Centre of Excellence team, infrastructure, and security teams to align departmental implementations with enterprise standards, architectures and operational guardrails.
• Monitor, troubleshoot and optimise infrastructure and application performance through observability tools such as Azure Monitor, Application Insights and Log Analytics, while supporting incident response, issue resolution, capacity planning and service resilience.
• Implement and strengthen security, compliance and governance controls in accordance with IT standards, and assess suitable DevSecOps tooling, infrastructure patterns and automation approaches to meet business needs and mitigate delivery risks.
jobRequirements:
We value the diverse talents and experiences that each individual brings to the table. While mastery of every requirement may not be necessary, familiarity and expertise in some of the following areas will position you for success within this team.
• Relevant experience in implementing and maintaining backend system infrastructure, with hands-on exposure to DevOps or DevSecOps and practical experience deploying applications on cloud platforms such as Azure or GCC.
• Good understanding of the end-to-end Software Development Life Cycle, with the ability to configure, maintain and troubleshoot CI/CD pipelines using tools such as Azure DevOps, and to support secure and reliable release practices.
• Proficiency in Infrastructure as Code and container technologies, such as Terraform or Azure Resource Manager (ARM) templates, Kubernetes (AKS) and Docker, for provisioning and managing scalable environments.
• Knowledge of observability, performance monitoring and operational support using tools such as Azure Monitor, Prometheus, Grafana, Application Insights and Log Analytics, with the ability to diagnose issues and improve system reliability.
• Familiarity with secure configuration, compliance requirements and embedded security controls within infrastructure and deployment pipelines, particularly in hybrid cloud environment.
• Strong documentation, stakeholder engagement and problem-solving skills, with the ability to work independently, adapt to new technologies and evolving requirements, collaborate across teams, and communicate clearly both verbally and in writing.
 
The seniority of appointment and actual corporate job title will commensurate with individual work experiences.

Position is on a 2-year full-time contract directly under the payroll of CPF Board with potential for emplacement into a permanent position.

What you can expect
Being part of #TeamCPF means embarking on a challenging and rewarding career in a progressive workplace that values productivity and growth. Here’s what awaits you:
• Opportunities to engage in a mix of formal and informal training, keeping your skills sharp in our ever-evolving technological landscape. 
• Promotion opportunities based on your capability and on-the-job performance. 
• A vibrant community of like-minded and friendly colleagues, where collaboration and creativity thrive.

• Flexible dress code that empowers you to choose your appropriate outfit for the day. 
• A comprehensive rewards package that includes annual leave, pro-family leave, medical and dental benefits, and access to recreational activities.

agencyDescription:
The Singapore Food Agency (SFA) is a new Statutory Board formed under the ‘Ministry of Sustainability and the Environment (MSE) to oversee food safety and security. The SFA will serve as the single point of contact for public feedback on food-related issues, and strengthen management of foodborne disease outbreaks to protect public health.

The SFA will also facilitate more business-friendly regulations with oversight of all food safety policies and consolidation of food laboratory capabilities to deepen competencies in food diagnostics, and research and development in food safety.
jobDescription:
The mission of SFA is to ensure and secure a supply of safe food for Singapore. The National Centre for Food Science (NCFS) supports SFA’s vision of ensuring safe food for all by being a national reference laboratory on food science, conducting food safety monitoring to generate scientific data for enforcement of food regulations, support of risk assessment and protection of consumer health. NCFS oversees the application of science and technology to enable an evidence-based approach for ensuring food safety in partnership with stakeholders across the entire food chain and research institutions to address emerging food safety and security concerns.

You will be part of a dynamic team of the Food Science Rapid Response Department (FSRRD) under NCFS to provide support to SFA’s food safety regulatory testing and market monitoring programs. This is a fantastic opportunity for you to learn and apply a wide range of cutting-edge testing and diagnostic techniques to solve real world problems and safeguard the food safety for Singaporeans. The Specialist Teams under FSRRD strive to continue developing our scientific knowledge and testing capabilities to keep pace with the challenges of emerging foodborne chemical, radiochemical and biological hazards. We collaborate with internal and external stakeholders to enhance food safety standards in the region, and support food security initiatives such as high-tech farming and novel food innovation.

You will be deployed to the Food Radioactivity Specialist Team under FSRRD, playing a key role in developing new analytical methods for strengthening and broadening the testing capabilities and for enabling risk assessment to support SFA’s operation needs for food safety regulatory function and market monitoring programs.
jobResponsibilities:
• Perform food radioactivity testing and all related functions to support SFA food safety monitoring and surveillance programs.
  • Develop, validate and implement analytical methods for determination of natural/artificial alpha, beta and gamma emitting radionuclides.
  • Lead the design, planning and implementation of radiological monitoring programs to establish representative baseline radioactivity levels in food.
  • Develop and implement advanced data analytics approaches, including statistical modelling and exploratory artificial intelligence and machine learning techniques, to support trend analysis, anomaly detection, and predictive insights from radiological monitoring data.
  • Develop data visualization tools, dashboards, and automated workflows to facilitate data interpretation and decision-making to support food safety surveillance and preparedness.
  • Implement laboratory quality assurance programs to ensure that laboratory practices are in full compliance with ISO/IEC 17025:2017 standards.

You will work alongside a team with varied skills and backgrounds, but with the common goals of (i) promoting good health and reducing illnesses; (ii) ensuring that Singaporeans have access to good and affordable healthcare; and (iii) pursuing medical excellence. jobDescription:
You will be part of the team which formulates, reviews and implements policies to develop Singapore’s healthcare financing framework, to keep healthcare affordable and sustainable for all Singaporeans. Specifically, this role will be focused on MediShield Life – Singapore’s national health insurance scheme. You will work collaboratively with policy and clinical groups within MOH, healthcare institutions and other public agencies to develop and implement MediShield Life policies. 

You will be working in a fast-paced and dynamic environment that would require the ability to manage multiple priorities and stakeholders at the same time.
jobResponsibilities:
As part of the MediShield Life team, you will contribute towards:

•	Ensuring that MediShield Life benefits provide sufficient protection against large medical bills and focuses coverage on high-value technologies. This may include:
       o	Reviewing MediShield Life benefits to ensure adequate protection against large healthcare bills and sustainable coverage of innovative high-cost technologies, balancing against impact on premiums.  This may require you to:
            	Analyse claims and utilisation data from a variety of sources to identify gaps and make recommendations to address them. 
            	Work with stakeholders such as the Agency for Care Effectiveness to understand approaches to clinical and cost-effectiveness evaluation, and calibrate financing based on evaluation outcome; 
            	Consult healthcare institutions and clinicians to understand the impact of changes in financing. 
      o	Overseeing the implementation of new or revised policies relating to MediShield Life benefits, including working with stakeholders to enhance claims systems and assessing appeals for coverage 

•	Ensuring that MediShield Life premiums are affordable for policyholders.  This may include:
      o	Reviewing premium support measures to ensure affordability of premiums for different groups of Singaporeans. This may require you to analyse the premium impact and MediSave adequacy of different segments and work closely with other teams to formulate measures such as MediSave top-ups or enhancements to premium subsidies.
      o	Overseeing the administration of MediShield Life premiums, including assessing appeals for premium support and designing premium recovery and enforcement measures 

Beyond the above, you will also:

•	Contribute to the policy-ops feedback loop, by addressing parliamentary questions and public queries
•	Work with partner agencies and stakeholders to enhance public communications of healthcare financing schemes
•	Provide secretariat support to the MediShield Life Council and its sub-committees in carrying out their functions
jobRequirements:

•	Learning & Putting Skills into Action - Possesses the drive and curiosity to learn and apply new skills, knowledge and new ways of working. 
•	Improving & Innovating – Ability to seek continual improvements, and to innovate and experiment while managing the risks involved. 
•	Working Effectively with Stakeholders – Ability to mobilise and rally partners and stakeholders towards a collective purpose.

•	Excellent writing, presentation and negotiation skills, experience in public policy formulation and/or scheme administration in the social sector would be an advantage

PASD establishes, implements and oversees the procurement policies and frameworks, as well as provide advisories in ensuring the standards of integrity are maintained throughout the procurement value chain.

You will be part of a team responsible for driving procurement policy reviews and digital transformation initiatives, procurement systems enhancement and development, as well as outreach and engagement to strengthen procurement capabilities across NEA.
jobResponsibilities:
You will support the procurement functions in NEA by carrying out the following activities:

  • Identify business needs and develop and implement digital solutions, including leveraging data and analytics to support procurement insights and process improvements
  • Administer and enhance existing procurement systems to meet evolving operational requirements and policy updates
  • Collaborate with internal and external stakeholders to develop, implement and facilitate the adoption of new procurement systems.
  • Conduct procurement policy, process and system reviews to improve operational efficiency while ensuring governance and compliance with the Instruction Manual (IM) on Procurement
  • Provide procurement advice to procurement teams across all stages of the procurement cycle
  • Conduct engagement sessions to facilitate knowledge transfer and build competencies within the NEA procurement community
jobRequirements:
Requirements:

  • At least 4 to 6 years of experience in government procurement
  • Experience in procurement systems, digitalisation and/or process improvement
  • Familiarity with the Instruction Manual (IM) on Procurement, GeBIZ and GeBIZ Management Console (GMC) is preferred.
  • Proficient in Microsoft Office and data visualisation tools
  • Strong analytical, interpersonal and communication skills (writing and presentation)
  • Ability to manage multiple priorities and stakeholders under tight timelines in a fast-paced environment

agencyDescription: The Accountant-General’s Department (AGD) plays an important role in making Singapore a better place through Finance. We do this through building a strong foundation in providing robust financial systems and processes that serve key stakeholders including our pensioners, vendors and the public sector. Our team of accounting professionals work at AGD and are deployed to the public agencies to deliver a wide range of financial and accounting-related services to the Public Service.
