jobDescription:
We are looking for a Senior Database Administrator to join our team to support the migration, administration and modernization of platforms supporting enterprise applications. You will play a key role in database migration to Government Commercial Cloud (GCC) (on AWS or Azure).

The successful candidate will be responsible for the full database lifecycle, including installation, configuration, upgrades, patching, performance tuning, backup and recovery, high availability, disaster recovery and operational support. The role also involves evaluating and adopting the latest AI Database capabilities to support future platform modernization. The successful candidate will also work closely with existing vendors and internal stakeholders to ensure successful delivery of database migration, upgrade and operational support activities.
jobResponsibilities:
• Lead the migration of Oracle Database 19c environments to Government Commercial Cloud (GCC) on AWS and Azure, ensuring minimal disruption to business operations.

  • Design, implement and maintain database replication between on-premises and cloud environments.

  • Plan and execute Oracle database installations, configuration, upgrades and database lifecycle management.

  • Perform proactive database administration, including performance tuning, SQL optimization, capacity planning, health monitoring and preventive maintenance to ensure database availability, reliability and performance.

  • Design, implement and maintain backup, recovery, High Availability (HA) and Disaster Recovery (DR) solutions.

  • Apply database patches, security updates and configuration changes while ensuring compliance with organisational security policies and industry best practices.

  • Collaborate with application, infrastructure, cloud and DevOps teams to support application deployments, system integration and cloud migration initiatives.

  • Troubleshoot complex database and infrastructure issues, perform root cause analysis, automate operational tasks using scripting where appropriate, and maintain comprehensive technical documentation.

  • Collaborate with existing vendors and cross-functional teams, including application, infrastructure and cloud teams, to deliver database migration, implementation, maintenance and operational support.
jobRequirements:
• Knowledge in Engineering, Computer Science or equivalent degree.

  • Minimum 7 years of experience in Oracle Database design, implementation and administration in enterprise environments.

  • Strong hands-on experience administering Oracle Database 19c, including installation, configuration, upgrades, patching, performance tuning, backup & recovery and database security.

  • Proven experience planning and executing Oracle database migrations from on-premises infrastructure to cloud platforms, preferably Government Commercial Cloud (GCC) on AWS or Azure.

  • Strong hands-on experience with Oracle High Availability, Disaster Recovery and migration technologies, including Oracle GoldenGate, Data Guard, RMAN and Zero Downtime Migration (ZDM)

  • Familiarity with Oracle AI Database technologies, including Oracle AI Database 26ai, Oracle APEX, Select AI and related database capabilities.

  • Experience administering Oracle databases on Linux platforms and deploying database workloads to cloud environments (AWS and/or Azure).

  • Proficiency in scripting and automation using Shell, Python or equivalent scripting languages to improve database administration and operational efficiency.

  • Relevant Oracle Database, Oracle Cloud and cloud platform certifications are preferred.

  • Team player with strong analytical, troubleshooting and interpersonal skills.

jobDescription:
GovTech supports various Government Agencies in carrying out ICT delivery services and appoints Agency Chief Information Security Officers (ACISO) to oversee information security management within these agencies. The ACISO is a leadership role that requires technical proficiency demonstrated in multiple cybersecurity domains. The role demands knowledge and/or practical experience in most of the domains below:

  • Cybersecurity Governance frameworks,
  • Security Operations including incident response,
  • Architecture design and threat risk assessment,
  • Security Testing.

The ACISO must possess technical understanding of both on-premises infrastructure security and cloud security architectures across major platforms (e.g., AWS, Azure, and GCP), including their native security features, identity management systems, and security control implementations.

[What you will be working on]

Emplaced in public agencies and reporting to the agency’s Chief Information Officer (CIO) and Ministry Family CISO, you will collaborate with various stakeholders (GovTech HQ teams, Agency management, Agency project teams, and outsourced vendors) and will be responsible to:

  • Lead the agency-level cybersecurity function in supporting agency digital transformation initiatives whilst ensuring digital resilience of agency systems.
  • Formulate and implement agency cybersecurity strategies, policies and work plans, ensuring continuous alignment with Ministry Family's business strategic goals
  • Review and enhance risk management through threat-based risk assessments, risk mitigations, risk monitoring and reporting.
  • Provide consultation and endorse risk management and mitigation plans from agency’s project teams.
  • Govern and enhance the agency's security posture by maintaining visibility and oversight of ICT assets, security architectures, and cybersecurity operations code of practices.
  • Develop and maintain incident response plan and playbooks. This involves planning, designing and conduct of security incident response workshops and exercises (table-top exercises, simulation and drills) as well as lead the investigation and management of ICT security incidents.
  • Provide advisory and recommendations on appropriate cybersecurity technologies to be deployed that meets agency’s business requirements and aligned with WOG-wide advisories and practices.
  • Ensure secure by design ICT product development, and that security controls implementations comply with the defined security policies, standards and guidelines.
  • Develop and maintain effective cybersecurity awareness and training programmes


[What we are looking for]

  • Degree in Computer Science, Information Systems, Engineering or related Technology field
  • At least 8-10 years of management experience related to information security and solid grasp of ICT operations, security policies, business processes and the relationship between them.
  • Ability to work with multi-functional, multi-disciplined teams to formulate, institute real time awareness of security posture and baseline among end users.
  • Good interpersonal and partner/executive leadership skills.
  • Demonstrate knowledge and experience in security by design implementations, review of system architecture, devsecops practices, Infrastructure as Code (IaC) tools and securing CI/CD pipelines 
  • Demonstrate understanding of cloud service models (IaaS, PaaS, SaaS), coupled with a strong understanding of core cloud services and modern cloud-native architectures (serverless, containers, microservices)
  • Identify on-premises and cloud-specific cybersecurity risks and threats, demonstrating skills to thoroughly assess their impact and likelihood. This assessment encompasses, but is not limited to, secure configurations, insider threats, vendor risks, data leakage, malwares including ransomware, account hijacking, and compliance risks.
  • Evaluate the effectiveness of existing controls and recommending appropriate mitigation strategies for on-premises and cloud-related cybersecurity and data security issues.
  • Display understanding of emerging threats and technologies, and the ability to translate risk into business impact
  • Strong understanding of compliance requirements and the ability to identify potential violations in on-premises or cloud environments.
  • Able to communicate cyber security topics effectively to senior stakeholders.
  • Minimally possess CISSP certification, preferably with other related certifications, e.g. CISM, CCSP, GCIH that demonstrates continuous learning and knowledge of industry best practices.
  • We believe in being Agile, Bold and Collaborative, and are looking for people who identify with these values.
  • Singaporeans only.

What you'll do

Architecture & technical direction

  • Set the overall system architecture for the TradeNet platform — service decomposition, data architecture, API contracts, infrastructure patterns.

  • Design for resilience: fault isolation, blast-radius containment, defensive API contracts, and graceful degradation across a system that cannot go down.

Legacy modernisation

  • Lead the technical strategy for decomposing and replacing the legacy monolith, including where to strangle, where to rewrite, and where to leave alone.

  • Write architecture documents, design specs, and technical RFCs that teams implement against.

  • Review code and designs across squads — particularly at integration boundaries and in foundational components.

  • Prototype and prove out critical technical approaches before committing teams to them.

  • Lead root-cause analysis on hard production and programme-level technical problems.

AI-assisted engineering

  • Pioneer and refine AI/LLM-assisted approaches to legacy analysis, code generation, test creation, and documentation.

  • Set the technical standards for how AI-generated output is evaluated, attributed, and held to quality.

  • Push the programme's use of agentic AI beyond basic code completion into architectural and analytical workflows.

  • Resolve technical disputes across squads. People will disagree on approach, and you are the one who makes the call and gets buy-in from both sides.

  • Balance technical debt against migration timelines. Know when to take a shortcut to hit a delivery date and when to say no because the long-term cost is too high. Make these tradeoffs explicitly and visibly.

  • Experience with data-governance and compliance constraints that shape architecture (data residency, classification, audit trails).

  • Familiarity with the Java/J2EE legacy ecosystem you'd be migrating away from.

GovTech Data Practice

The Data Practice drives innovation and sets best practices for the effective and responsible use of data across the Whole-of-Government (WOG). We work at the intersection of data engineering, AI, privacy, and governance - developing standards, platforms, and tools that enable agencies to build high-quality data products and unlock the value of data for public good.

A core focus of our work is advancing responsible data use. As data sharing and AI adoption accelerate, we develop both the frameworks and technologies needed to ensure sensitive data can be used safely; including in AI systems, where interactions with sensitive data are becoming more widespread and risks will scale further with more autonomous, agentic workflows.

A core focus of our work is to make responsible data use practical and scalable. This includes developing technical guardrails, privacy-preserving workflows, evaluation methods, and reusable standards that help agencies use data safely for analytics, AI, and digital services. Our work spans areas such as AI privacy, context-aware anonymisation, synthetic data generation, federated AI / computing, encrypted computation, differential privacy, and confidential computing. We bridge the gap between policy, research, and real-world deployment by experimenting with new approaches, validating them through agency pilots, and operationalising them into standards, implementation guides, and central government tools.

We are seeking a Data Scientist at the intermediate to senior level. At the baseline, you will (a) conduct rigorous research and experimentation to evaluate emerging privacy solutions, (b) design scalable, implementable workflows tailored for government adoption, and (c) translate these into practical tools, guidelines, and systems used across agencies. Depending on experience and seniority, you may also take on broader ownership in shaping the team’s direction; identifying emerging technology opportunities, working with stakeholders across policy and engineering, and driving initiatives from problem definition through to scaled deployment.

What you will be working on

  1. Applied Research & Development
    a. Design and execute rigorous experiments to evaluate emerging PETs and AI-enabled solutions
    b. Develop proof-of-concepts that demonstrate real-world applicability and measurable impact
    c. Stay current with academic research and translate findings into practical, deployable solutions
    d. Contribute to the broader community through publications and knowledge sharing with government and international partners
  2. Agency Partnership & Pilot Implementation
    a. Collaborate directly with government agencies to deeply understand their unique privacy challenges and operational constraints
    b. Design and execute pilot programmes to test PET solutions
    c. Systematically gather user feedback and iterate on solutions based on practical deployment experiences and lessons learned
    d. Provide ongoing technical consultation and hands-on support to agencies throughout their privacy technology adoption journey
  3. End-to-End Solution Innovation & Development
    a. Identify opportunities where PETs can address current common data challenges across government
    b. Architect and develop scalable solutions designed for widespread adoption across the Whole of Government ecosystem
    c. Establish clear implementation pathways and adoption frameworks for new privacy technologies

  4. Cross-Functional Collaboration
    a. Work as a collaborative team player alongside data scientists, data engineers, software engineers, and product managers
    b. Partner strategically with government agencies to align technical solutions with the evolving landscape of regulatory requirements and governance frameworks

  5. Strategic Direction & Technical Leadership (for more senior hires)
    a. Identify and evaluate emerging technologies and their relevance for government use cases
    b. Shape the team’s direction by defining high-impact problem areas and prioritising initiatives
    c. Scope and drive projects end-to-end, from early exploration through to scaled deployment across agencies
    d. Engage stakeholders across policy, engineering, and vendors to align on problem framing and solution design
    e. Mentor team members and contribute to building a strong, high-performing team

GovTech's Anti Scam Products Team builds tech to detect, disrupt, and deter scammers at scale.   • Willingness to understand the fraud/scam domain
  • Effective and critical use of LLMs: able to leverage AI tools to move fast, while exercising judgment on output quality.
  • Basic statistical data analytics (A/B test significance, rolling window analysis, confounder analysis)
  • Experience in data wrangling, model development (e.g. classification, regression, outlier detection on tabular data, relational/graph data, embedding or a combination) and deployment (e.g. Sagemaker, TensorFlow)
  • Foundational coding experience in Python (e.g. Git, package management/venv)

Preferred requirements:

  • Experience in Spark

  • Experience in Neo4j or any graph database
  • Experience in on-device ML

jobTitle: Deputy Director, Government Incident Reporting Ops
jobDescription:
Role Purpose

The Deputy Director (DD), Government Incident Reporting Ops, leads a high-performing operational team responsible for centralizing, assessing, and managing the full spectrum of Whole-of-Government (WOG) incident reports across all Singapore Government agencies.

The scope of coverage is multi-disciplinary, encompassing cybersecurity/data incidents, physical security breaches, public-facing service disruptions, and general operational failures. The DD ensures swift severity assessment, accurate fact-gathering, and seamless leadership escalation, while driving a WOG continuous learning culture to prevent systemic recurrence.

Key Responsibilities

Multi-Domain Operational Leadership

  • Lead daily operations for the WOG Incident Reporting framework, ensuring all submissions across cyber, physical, and operational domains are triaged and validated accurately.
  • Demonstrate sharp acumen to make critical judgment calls on complex, multi-domain incidents, ensuring appropriate escalation and containment strategies are triggered according to SOPs.
  • Review and refine high-quality, high-stakes incident summaries and assessments for senior leadership presentation under tight timelines.

Process Optimization & Culture Building

  • Drive continuous improvement initiatives to streamline the reporting workflow, leveraging technology to make reporting frictionless and encourage timely submissions from all agencies.
  • Foster a "Just Culture" across the public service, prioritizing psychological safety so agencies report incidents transparently without fear of blame.

WOG Knowledge Management & Continuous Learning

  • Transform diverse incident data into actionable insights, identifying trends and cross-domain vulnerabilities.
  • Develop effective mechanisms (e.g., cross-agency sharing sessions, post-incident reviews, systemic playbooks) to ensure lessons are institutionalized WOG.

Talent Development

  • Mentor and develop team officers, uplifting their technical literacy across different incident domains and honing their analytical capabilities.

Requirements & Qualifications

Technical & Domain Knowledge (Critical)

  • Cross-Domain Literacy: Strong foundational knowledge across IT infrastructure, Cybersecurity operations, and Physical Security frameworks. Must be able to speak the language of both tech engineers and physical security teams.
  • Incident Triage Expertise: Familiarity with incident classification models, threat landscapes, and standard risk matrix frameworks across both digital and physical environments.

Professional Experience

  • Experience in Large-Scale Operations: At least 8 years of professional experience managing complex operations, incident response, crisis management, or operational risk.
  • Organizational Scale: Proven track record of navigating and operating effectively within large, complex organizations (e.g., Multi-National Corporations (MNCs), major financial institutions, critical infrastructure operators, or public sector agencies).
  • Stakeholder Management: Demonstrated ability to manage diverse, high-level stakeholders and navigate matrixed organizational structures or multi-party ecosystems.
  • Public Sector Familiarity (Preferred but not mandatory): Prior experience within the Singapore Public Service, or a strong conceptual understanding of Whole-of-Government (WOG) governance structures and inter-agency dynamics, is highly advantageous. Private sector candidates with a strong adaptability to public sector governance are welcome to apply.

jobTitle: Deputy Director, ICT & SS Risk Specialist
jobDescription:
GovTech is the lead agency driving Singapore’s Smart Nation initiatives and public sector digital transformation. As the Centre of Excellence for Infocomm Technology and Smart Systems (ICT & SS), GovTech develops the Singapore Government’s capabilities in Data Science & Artificial Intelligence, Application Development, Smart City Technology, Digital Infrastructure, and Cybersecurity.

At GovTech, we offer you a purposeful career to make lives better where we empower our people to master their craft through robust learning and development opportunities all year round.

Play a part in Singapore’s vision to build a Smart Nation and embark on your meaningful journey to build tech for public good. Join us to advance our mission and shape your future with us today!

Learn more about GovTech at tech.gov.sg.

The challenge

What happens when technology, delivery and threats move faster than an organisation’s ability to see and respond to risk?

And what could become possible if risk management moved just as quickly?

Every organisation needs a way to detect warning signs, connect the dots and act before problems spread.

That is the role of governance, risk and control.

Think of it as the organisation’s nervous system. It picks up signals from across the organisation, helps leaders make sense of them and enables a timely response.

When that system works well, teams can move faster, take smarter risks and deliver with greater confidence. When it does not, warning signs are missed, decisions slow down and governance becomes a barrier rather than an enabler.

GovTech has strong platforms, talented people and an important mission. As our role and public impact grow, the risks we manage are becoming more interconnected, fast-moving and consequential.

We are looking for Deputy Directors and Assistant Directors in Enterprise Risk Management who want to help build what comes next.

You will have the opportunity to challenge established practices, experiment with data and AI, influence senior decisions and shape how one of Singapore’s most important technology organisations manages risk.

[What you will be working on]

This is a role for people who want more than a steady portfolio. It is for those who want to build, push boundaries and leave the system better than they found it.

What you will have the chance to change. We want to move enterprise risk management:

  • from periodic reporting to more continuous risk visibility

  • from manual collation to data and AI-enabled insight

  • from risk registers to clearer decisions and action

  • from unclear accountability to risks with active owners

  • from retrospective assurance to earlier intervention

  • from compliance activity to practical support for delivery


This is not simply a reporting role. You will help shape how risk is understood, discussed, owned and acted upon across GovTech.

Your mandate

Your job is to make enterprise risk management useful.

You will work with senior leaders, risk owners and teams across GovTech to identify what matters, make trade-offs visible and support action before issues become incidents.

Depending on your experience and appointment level, you will lead or take ownership of significant ERM portfolios and initiatives.

You will have room to test ideas, challenge established practices and build better approaches. You will also need to influence people you do not manage and create clarity where risks, priorities or accountabilities are contested.

That is part of the job.

Break the Frame

Modern risk management cannot rely only on inherited frameworks, templates and periodic reporting.

We want people who are prepared to question established practices, test better approaches and rethink how risk management should work in a technology organisation.

You will explore how data, AI and automation can help GovTech:

  • detect weak signals and emerging risks earlier

  • connect information across the organisation

  • reduce manual reporting and administrative work

  • give leaders more timely and useful risk insight

  • strengthen judgement without removing human accountability

This requires an experimental mindset. You should be comfortable testing ideas, learning from what does not work and turning successful experiments into practical capabilities.

The aim is not to use AI to perform old processes faster. It is to ask whether those processes are still needed and design better ones where they are not.

We call this Break the Frame: looking beyond established ways of working, pushing boundaries responsibly and building an ERM function that can keep pace with modern technology.

What you will do

Strengthen our ERM approach

Develop and improve GovTech’s enterprise risk framework, methodology and governance arrangements.

Clarify who owns each risk, how issues should be escalated and where decisions should sit.

Make sure the approach works for a modern technology organisation rather than forcing teams into processes that add little value.

Build a forward-looking view of risk

Maintain a current view of GovTech’s key risks across strategy, technology, operations, delivery, vendors, regulation, data, reputation and organisational capability.

Look beyond known issues and past incidents. Identify emerging threats, dependencies and concentrations of risk before they become larger problems.

Keep GovTech’s enterprise risk profile, register and monitoring approach relevant and useful to decision-makers.

Support better leadership decisions

Provide clear and practical advice to senior leadership, Board-level committees, auditors and oversight bodies, including SNDGO and relevant central agencies.

Turn complex risk issues into straightforward choices, trade-offs and recommendations.

Help leaders understand what matters most, what needs to be done, who should act and where attention is required.

Modernise how risk management is done

Improve processes that are too manual, retrospective or disconnected from day-to-day operations.

Use data, AI, automation and emerging technologies to improve the timeliness and quality of risk information.

Run practical experiments, test new approaches and turn successful ideas into reusable capabilities.

Develop tools and guidance that help teams manage risk as part of their work, not as a separate compliance exercise.

Work across GovTech

Partner with product, engineering, cybersecurity, operations, policy, procurement and corporate functions.

Help leaders balance delivery speed, resilience, governance and risk appetite.

Build trusted relationships and support honest conversations, especially where risks or accountabilities are unclear or contested.

Represent GovTech in relevant cross-agency risk and governance forums.


What good looks like

Success will not be measured by the number of reports produced.

You will know the role is making a difference when:

  • leadership has a clearer view of GovTech’s most important risks

  • risks are surfaced earlier and acted on faster

  • ownership and accountability are clear

  • risk insight improves strategic and operational decisions

  • governance supports responsible delivery rather than slowing it down

  • manual reporting is reduced

  • successful experiments lead to better ways of working

  • teams see ERM as a practical partner

  • GovTech is better prepared for disruption and emerging risks

[What we are looking for]

We are looking for people who want to improve how things work, not simply maintain existing processes. You should bring:

  • relevant experience in enterprise risk, governance, assurance or a related field

  • experience in a technology-intensive, operationally complex or regulated organisation

  • a strong understanding of risk appetite, governance, accountability and assurance

  • sound judgement and the confidence to challenge constructively

  • the ability to turn complex issues into clear choices and actions

  • credibility with senior leaders, auditors, regulators and technical teams

  • experience influencing across organisational boundaries

  • curiosity about how data, AI and automation can improve risk management

  • a willingness to experiment, learn and challenge the status quo

Candidates considered for the Deputy Director level should have substantial leadership experience, enterprise-wide influence and the confidence to advise senior leaders and oversight bodies on complex risk matters.

Candidates considered for the Assistant Director level should have strong delivery capability, sound risk judgement and the ability to lead significant portfolios and stakeholder engagements.

What would be useful

Experience or strength in one or more of the following would be valuable:

  • government technology

  • critical digital infrastructure

  • large-scale platforms or digital services

  • technology or operational resilience

  • digital transformation

  • risk analytics, automation or AI-enabled risk management

  • systems thinking, including the ability to see dependencies, feedback loops and second-order effects

  • narrative competence, including the ability to turn complex risk issues into clear and persuasive stories that support decisions


You do not need to tick every box. Relevant experience matters, but so do judgement, curiosity and the ability to make change happen.

What we offer you:

GovTech is an equal opportunity employer committed to fostering an inclusive workplace that values diverse voices and perspectives, as we believe that diversity is the foundation to innovation.   

Our employee benefits are based on a total rewards approach, offering a holistic and market-competitive suite of perks. These include leave benefits to meet your work-life needs and employee wellness programs. 

We champion flexible work arrangements (subject to your job role) and trust that you will manage your own time to deliver your best, wherever you are, and whatever works best for you.

Role Purpose
This role is built for a technical leader who can orchestrate and scale high-concurrency red team engagements, managing multiple distinct victim operations simultaneously. The Director ensures the continuous development of sophisticated custom malware and resilient Command and Control (C2) architecture, while serving as the primary operational coordinator who translates active attack campaigns into clear, actionable risk insights for diverse stakeholder groups.

Key Responsibilities

High-Concurrency Operational Management

  • Directly manage multiple offensive teams executing simultaneous, distinct victim operations across separate target networks or business entities.
  • De-conflict operational resources, timelines, and personnel to ensure high-fidelity, continuous testing across multiple concurrent environments.
  • Handle the inherent ambiguity of shifting variables across multiple live runs, ensuring every operation maintains rigid operational security (OPSEC).

C2 Architecture & Advanced Malware Development

  • Oversee the design, deployment, and operational management of complex Command and Control (C2) frameworks capable of supporting multi-tenant, simultaneous operations.
  • Enforce best practices in C2 server segregation, obfuscation, and traffic routing to prevent defensive detection across various target environments.
  • Drive the engineering lifecycle for custom, evasive malware and custom tooling to ensure operations bypass modern enterprise controls (EDR/NDR).

Threat-Aligned Operation Execution

  • Maintain an expert, up-to-the-minute understanding of real-world threat actor behaviors, actively applying global threat intelligence to live operational scenarios.
  • Ensure that simultaneous red team campaigns realistically mimic the specific Tactics, Techniques, and Procedures (TTPs) of modern Advanced Persistent Threats (APTs) targeting the respective victims.

Stakeholder Interface & Operational Coordination

  • Act as the primary interface for all affected stakeholders, providing regular, precise updates on active exploitation paths and findings during live runs.
  • Coordinate complex, multi-stakeholder rating exercises, ensuring seamless collaboration and communication before, during, and after a specific operational run.
  • Translate highly technical, multi-stage attack paths into risk-based executive briefings for non-technical leadership.



Job Requirements

Technical Experience & Qualifications

  • Multi-Team Operational Leadership: Proven experience directly managing multiple technical offensive units or red teams, with a track record of executing concurrent attack campaigns.
  • Live Operations Mastery: Expert-level knowledge in running routine, high-velocity red team operations, including post-exploitation, lateral movement, and data exfiltration.
  • Malware & C2 Infrastructure Engineering: Deep technical background in developing custom malware and managing robust C2 server environments tailored for stealth and resilience.
  • Threat Landscapes: Mastery of modern adversarial TTPs and a precise understanding of what real-world threat actors are currently exploiting in the wild.

Soft Skills & Core Competencies

  • Stakeholder Diplomacy: Outstanding capability to interface with, update, and manage expectations across a wide array of stakeholders during high-stakes operational runs.
  • Crisis & Ambiguity Management: Calm under pressure; able to switch contexts rapidly between multiple live victim operations and make split-second operational decisions.
  • Clear Articulation: Ability to synthesize complex technical execution chains into concise, impactful operational reports and executive summaries.

Cultivating Technical Camaraderie & Shared Team Spirit

  • Culture & Team Builder: Proven ability to build camaraderie and high esprit de corps among eccentric, highly specialized technical professionals, transforming isolated experts into a cohesive, mission-driven unit.
  • Forge a Collaborative "Crew" Identity: Cultivate a tight-knit, high-trust team culture where multi-team silos are broken down. Encourage a collaborative environment where vulnerability researchers and red team operators actively swap insights, techniques, and tools to win operations together.
  • Drive Shared Technical Victories: Build deep team spirit by establishing peer-review structures, collaborative hackathons, and collective post-operation debriefs. Ensure that a breakthrough by one operator (e.g., a novel C2 bypass or custom malware variant) is celebrated and adopted as a collective win for the entire unit.
  • Foster an Environment of Mutual Respect: Lead with the technical credibility required to earn the respect of deeply analytical engineers, creating a flat, open culture where the best technical argument wins, regardless of hierarchy.
  • Unite Around a Common Adversary: Foster high morale and collective purpose by aligning the team against a clear, shared mission—outsmarting real-world threat actors and securing complex ecosystems through elite, unified offensive tradecraft.

We are seeking a dynamic individual to be part of the journey in transforming governance, risk, and compliance (GRC) from a traditional oversight function into an integrated and scalable capability that keeps in step with modern IT delivery practices. This role bridges GRC and engineering. The objective is not to become a software engineer who works in compliance, but to become an effective practitioner who leverages engineering thinking to embed GRC seamlessly into DevOps practices and prepare frameworks for emerging AI-driven systems. By bridging regulatory requirements with technical innovation, you will help position Singapore at the forefront of responsible digital government, enabling faster and safer technology deployment that directly benefits citizens in our increasingly AI-integrated future.

Responsibilities

• Work directly with operational units to understand their challenges, constraints, and needs within their operating context before implementing control requirements.

• Apply systems thinking to understand how controls interact across processes, platforms, and teams, moving from “this is the control requirement” to “this is how it should operate in practice.”

• Design and embed GRC practices into system and process development from inception, ensuring governance mechanisms feel natural within product and engineering workflows rather than burdensome.

• Translate GRC requirements into practical, actionable solutions with stakeholder experience as a primary consideration, ensuring appropriate governance is in place without hindering operational velocity.

• Analyse delivery workflows, decision latency, and control friction across digital products and platforms to identify systemic risk, operational complexity, and value leakage.

• Architect reusable control patterns and implement real-time risk and control telemetry using data pipelines, APIs, and analytics platforms to enable continuous automated monitoring and assurance-by-design.

• Replace retrospective compliance validation with embedded, continuous assurance mechanisms that demonstrate measurable risk outcomes.

• Implement governance for AI-enabled systems, including model lifecycle controls, decision accountability, data provenance, and human-in-the-loop assurance.

• Champion the cultural shift toward proactive GRC engineering. Manage key stakeholder relationships across product engineering teams, legacy policy units, and executive leadership to align governance initiatives with broader product roadmaps.

8+ years' experience with either of the two backgrounds:

• GRC practitioner who understands how GRC can be embedded into systems and workflows to make it practical, operational and scalable; OR

• Former engineer (security, DevOps, platform, or similar) who are interested in applying structured, systems thinking to modernize GRC processes.

• Systems thinking across business, technology, and risk.

• Structured problem-solving.

• Pragmatic controls design.

• Comfort operating in imperfect integration environments.

• Strong translation skills; clear communication between deep-technical engineering teams, non-technical stakeholders, and policy makers.

• Strong leadership capability to drive systemic change and influence without relying solely on direct authority.

• Strong foundation in GRC principles with practical understanding of how they apply in modern technology environments.

• Solid grasp of cloud fundamentals and DevSecOps practices (e.g., CI/CD, Infra as-Code, Policy-as-Code).

Data and AI help us detect fraud, understand product performance, make better decisions, automate operations and develop new capabilities.

This is not traditional analytics or reporting role.

You will lead Singpass’ Data Science and AI function across:

Singpass is Singapore’s national digital identity platform, enabling citizens and businesses to securely access digital services across government and the private sector.

As part of Singapore’s critical digital infrastructure, Singpass must remain trusted, resilient and well-governed. As Singpass evolves in scale and complexity, our approach to governance and risk management must evolve alongside it. At Singpass, we believe governance should enable delivery, not slow it down. It should be embedded into how we design, build and operate our products and systems, rather than imposed as a final gate.

We are looking for a Head of Governance & Risk to build and lead this capability.

The Opportunity

This is not a traditional Governance, Risk & Compliance (GRC) role.

You will lead Singpass’ governance, enterprise risk and operational resilience capability, partnering closely with Product, Engineering, Security and Operations teams to help Singpass move fast with confidence.

Your mission is to ensure Singpass is:

  • Well-governed.
  • Operationally resilient.
  • Continuously audit-ready.
  • Crisis-prepared.

You will champion a shift from reactive compliance to continuous assurance, where governance is embedded into delivery, risks are identified and monitored early, and audit readiness is an outcome of strong daily practices rather than periodic preparation.

You will also help shape the future of governance by using automation, data and AI to modernise how risk, compliance and assurance are managed.

What you will be working on:

1. Governance & Enterprise Risk.

  • Develop and continuously improve Singpass’ governance frameworks, decision rights and enterprise risk management practices..
  • Maintain a holistic view of Singpass’ risk posture across operational, technology, vendor, policy, regulatory, compliance, data, delivery and reputational domains..
  • Ensure risks are identified early, clearly understood, actively managed and owned by the appropriate leaders..
  • Support leadership in making informed decisions where risk, control and delivery priorities must be balanced..

2. Operational Resilience & Crisis Management

  • Lead Singpass’ business continuity, operational resilience and crisis management programmes..
  • Develop and maintain business continuity plans, crisis playbooks, escalation structures and recovery strategies..
  • Plan and conduct crisis simulations and resilience exercises to strengthen organisational readiness..
  • Ensure lessons from incidents and exercises are translated into sustained operational improvements..

3. Continuous Assurance & Governance Transformation

  • Build an organisation that is continuously audit-ready rather than periodically audit-prepared..
  • Establish near-real-time visibility into risks, compliance status and control effectiveness through automation, data and modern tooling..
  • Use AI and emerging technologies to improve risk detection, control monitoring, assurance and operational oversight..
  • Reduce manual processes and recurring compliance effort through automation and reusable controls..

4. Governance Enablement

  • Partner with Product, Engineering, Security and Operations teams to embed governance and risk management throughout the product lifecycle..
  • Drive a shift-left approach where governance, controls and compliance requirements are considered from design through operations..
  • Build governance capability through practical guidance, coaching, standards and reusable patterns..
  • Develop a forward-deployed governance model that keeps governance close to delivery while maintaining consistency with GovTech-wide standards

5. Stakeholder Assurance

  • Provide clear and credible governance and risk reporting to senior leadership, auditors, regulators and oversight bodies..
  • Translate complex risk matters into practical options and recommendations for technical and non-technical stakeholders..
  • Build confidence that Singpass is responsibly governed, operationally resilient and managing its risks effectively.

Who We’re Looking For:

We are looking for a builder who believes that a modern governance and risk team should enable innovation rather than constrain it.

You should have:

  • Significant experience leading governance, enterprise risk, operational resilience or related functions within a technology-driven organisation..
  • Experience working with large-scale digital platforms, critical services or infrastructure..
  • Strong understanding of enterprise governance, risk management, business continuity, crisis management and assurance..
  • The ability to communicate complex governance and risk matters effectively and accurately with executives, engineers, auditors and regulators..
  • Strong judgement and the ability to balance rigour, pragmatism and delivery speed..
  • An interest in modernising governance through automation, data and AI..

Experience in government technology, digital identity, cloud platforms, agile development or continuous compliance will be an advantage.

Why Join Us

This is an opportunity to build a modern governance and risk capability for one of Singapore’s most important digital platforms.

You will do more than write policies or coordinate audits.

You will help redefine how governance is practised by embedding it into everyday delivery, strengthening operational resilience, and enabling Singpass to innovate with confidence while maintaining the trust placed in it by its users and partners.

If you are excited by the opportunity to build the next generation of governance and risk capabilities for critical digital infrastructure, we would like to hear from you.

Government Commercial Cloud (GCC) is a key platform within Singapore Government Technology Stacks that enables government agencies to build and operate digital services on commercial cloud. The GCC Engineering team develops platform automations, landing zones, and security tooling across AWS, Azure, and GCP — serving thousands of government systems and thousands of public officers.

Security at GCC is not a side function — it's core to the platform's value proposition. Government agencies trust GCC to be secure by default.

You are the single named owner of security outcomes across all engineering teams in GCC. You define how security works — the standards, processes, escalation paths, and technical approaches — and drive adoption through influence, not authority. You operate through a Security Champions network: persistent, named engineers in each product team who own security judgment locally, coordinated by you. Your accountability is whether GCC is actually secure — measured through process health, incident response quality, and security posture metrics you define.

This role is part of the organisation's domain leadership structure — you join alongside Engineering Managers as a peer, not as a report to any EM. The Security domain is being stood up fresh. The previous model (centralised security team gatekeeping all decisions) has been retired. You inherit a Champions network in early stages, documented runbooks, and interim coverage from a senior security advisor. Your job is to take it from "interim bridge" to "sustainable, scalable security function."

The domain scope will evolve. Today it centres on the areas listed above — but we expect the role to grow into adjacent areas (AI security, detection engineering) as the organisation's needs develop. Adaptability and willingness to define your own frontier matters more than deep expertise in every area on day one.

[What you will be working on]

Security Architecture & Posture

  • Own the organisation's security posture across all product teams and cloud environments
  • Architect security frameworks that integrate into engineering workflows without creating bottlenecks
  • Design and evolve threat modelling methodologies adapted to the organisation's multi-cloud, multi-tenant context
  • Define escalation paths, severity frameworks, and incident response playbooks
  • Own the relationship with GCSOC, shaping how external security signals translate into internal action
  • Drive security tooling strategy — selecting, configuring, and setting alert thresholds that distinguish signal from noise

Standards & Process Design

  • Define security standards, runbooks, and compliance approaches that teams can self-serve against
  • Design the Security Champions model: training curriculum, forum cadence, escalation criteria, and what "good" looks like for a champion
  • Replace gatekeeping with enablement — move from "security reviews everything" to "teams self-certify against clear criteria, you spot-check and consult"
  • Own security decision records: all posture choices documented, auditable, and transferable
  • Reform compliance processes (e.g. IMR8) to reduce ceremony while maintaining assurance

Cross-Org Influence

[What we are looking for]

Must-Have

  • Deep security engineering expertise (architecture, not just operations) — you've designed security frameworks, not just followed them

Technology Landscape

| Area | Technologies |

Developer Productivity and Service (DPS) is building a Central Product Marketplace, the single platform through which agencies subscribe, provision, and manage GovTech's central products. Console is the engine at its core, with a clear organisational mandate: every GovTech platform product should be fully subscribable, billable, and operable through it. This is a product with real momentum, a clear mandate, and a large pipeline of central products to bring on board fully.

What you'll own:

Console is the command centre for agencies: where they subscribe, get billed, provision access, and manage GovTech products. Right now, most central products are only partially integrated. Your job is to change that: making Console the complete operational home for agencies and the default go-to-market platform for product teams, rather than one of many portals they have to deal with.

You are expected to:

  • Own the Console product roadmap and drive central products through the full integration journey, from being listed, to subscribable, to billed, to fully operable, at scale.

  • Consolidate various Console surfaces into one, so agencies deal with one subscription surface.

  • Reduce the time it takes for an agency to go from starting onboarding to being ready to use a product. This is Console's most important outcome.

  • Make Console genuinely valuable to product teams, not just a mandate they comply with. Surface demand signals, reduce their GTM overhead, and make integration worth their while.

  • Work closely with the Product Portal and Developer Portal PMs so the agency journey holds together across the full funnel.

You do this by:

  • Shipping and iterating on onboarding, approvals, billing, and management plane workflows with your engineering and design team.

  • Running structured engagement with central product teams across GDP to unblock integrations and build a repeatable playbook for getting products fully live on Console.

  • Defining and tracking the metrics that reflect whether agencies and product teams are actually getting value, not just whether products are listed.

  • Partnering with TMO to align integration timelines with product teams' own priorities.

  • Building the instrumentation needed to trace agency journeys end-to-end, so the team can see where things stall and fix them.

You will ultimately be responsible for Console becoming the operational backbone of the Central Product Marketplace.

[Summary of the Role]
We are looking for an experienced Lead Product Manager to drive a large-scale Human Capital Management (HCM) transformation and modernisation initiative. This role will lead discovery, strategy, and experimentation efforts to rethink how HR services, employee experience, and workforce operations should evolve for the future.
You will work across product, design, engineering, policy, and business teams to shape future-state HR journeys, validate ideas through rapid prototyping and POCs, and guide strategic decisions on modern HCM platforms and architecture.

[What the Role Needs to Do]

  • Lead discovery and transformation efforts across the employee lifecycle, from recruitment to exit.

  • Prioritise opportunities and guide hypotheses testing through prototypes and experimentation.
  • Facilitate alignment across senior stakeholders, HR teams, engineers, designers, and policy partners.
  • Translate discovery findings into actionable roadmaps, recommendations, and POC plans.

  • Strong systems thinking and ability to navigate ambiguity and organisational complexity.
  • Experience working with multidisciplinary teams across product, UX, engineering, and business domains.

  • Experience in public sector, workforce transformation, or regulated environments is advantageous.

  • Shape the future of workforce transformation and employee experience at scale.

[About the product]

Digital Access is a core IMDA initiative that supports digital inclusion by providing low-income households and seniors with affordable connectivity and digital devices.

[About the role]

We are looking for a Lead Product Manager to take ownership of a complex product area within Digital Access and to build the product function around it. This includes setting the operating model, the ceremonies, and the bar for product craft, and bringing the methodology and rigour of a modern product company to an IMDA core platform. You would also need to coordinate with multiple WOG product teams to bring a best of class delivery to IMDA.

This is a forward-deployed role: you will be a GovTech product leader embedded within Infocomm Media Development Authority (IMDA), working day-to-day alongside agency stakeholders, policy owners, and design and engineering teams. The role blends deep, hands-on product ownership with leadership of a small and growing team of product managers. You will operate with a high degree of autonomy, shape the direction of your area, and invest meaningfully in the people around you.

[What you will be working on]

Building the product function
You will establish how product is done on Digital Access — the operating model, the ceremonies, the discovery and delivery rhythm, and the standards for prioritisation and product craft. You will lead and grow a small team of product managers, set the bar for product thinking and execution, and create genuine opportunities for them to stretch. Just as importantly, you will partner with the existing business analysts and engineers as the team builds its product practice together — identifying those with product-management potential and coaching them toward it. You will contribute to raising hiring and assessment standards as the team scales.

Product strategy & execution
You will own the strategy and roadmap for your product area — translating complex business, regulatory, and technical inputs into a sequenced, measurable plan. You will set OKRs and success metrics, drive discovery, and make clear, well-documented prioritisation trade-offs. Drawing on user research, industry feedback, and platform data, you will validate or rule out ideas before development begins, and lead end-to-end execution to a high standard of quality, security, accessibility, and compliance. You will champion speed and simplicity within a large problem space while remaining clear-eyed about technical debt.

Agency partnership
Embedded within IMDA, you will help strengthen the product partnership between GovTech and IMDA. This means partnering with business and policy stakeholders to translate needs into well-framed product outcomes, and helping shape a sustainable operating model for how the two organisations collaborate on Digital Access. You will role-model the standards — prioritisation rigour, evidence-based decisions — that raise the bar for how the work is done.

Stakeholder management & organisational influence
Digital Access spans several government agencies, industry players, and vendor partners. You will build alignment through evidence, trust, and well-earned relationships — resolving complex dependencies, navigating competing requirements, and securing senior-management support for product strategy and investment. When stakeholder conflicts arise, you will be expected to facilitate solutioning toward strategic outcomes.

[What we are looking for]

  • 8+ years of product management experience, with a track record of shipping outcomes on enterprise, platform, or grants products
  • Experience establishing product practice — operating models, ceremonies, ways of working — in a team building or scaling its product capability
  • Experience leading PMs and cross-functional teams in complex, multi-stakeholder environments
  • Strong product craft: discovery, prioritisation, metrics, writing, and stakeholder influence
  • Comfort operating in ambiguity and leading without formal authority, holding yourself accountable to outcomes over outputs
  • Technical literacy to work effectively with engineers on platform, data, and integration trade-offs

Good to have:

  • Domain knowledge in the ICT and grant-based systems
  • Government or public-sector digital transformation experience
  • Experience modernising or re-platforming complex legacy or grant systems
  • Experience building or scaling a product team

As a Lead Product Manager, you will shape the strategy and roadmap of the fCMS. This role is not about managing a fixed set of requirements. It is about helping the Judiciary modernise critical systems in a way that delivers value incrementally, reduces delivery risk and creates long-term adaptability. You will help the platform respond to new legislation, policies and judicial processes, while improving the experience of those who use and operate the courts.

Shape the future of justice in Singapore

Justice is one of Singapore's most important public services. Every year, almost 200,000 cases pass through our courts, involving individuals, families, businesses, lawyers and public agencies. Behind every case is someone seeking a fair, timely and accessible resolution.

The Judiciary's transformation into One Judiciary brought together the Supreme Court, State Courts and Family Justice Courts under a shared vision of delivering justice that is trusted, accessible and ready for the future.

Realising this vision requires more than organisational change. It requires rethinking the digital systems, processes and services that underpin how justice is delivered.

The Future Courts Management System (fCMS) is the Judiciary's flagship digital transformation programme, developed in close partnership with GovTech. You will join GovTech's product management community while working deeply with the Judiciary to shape products that support the administration of justice across Singapore's Courts.

This is not simply a like-for-like replacement of legacy systems. It is an opportunity to reimagine how court services should work: making them easier to use, more responsive to changing legislation and policies, and better able to serve everyone who depends on them.

This is a rare opportunity to help shape how justice will be delivered in Singapore for years to come.

In this role, you will:

  • Shape product strategy for fCMS domains, translating Judiciary priorities, user needs, operational complexity and legislative changes into clear roadmaps and measurable outcomes.

  • Work in a product trio with Engineering and Design leads to discover, prioritise and deliver solutions that are valuable, usable, feasible, secure and scalable.

  • Understand users and court operations by working with judges, judicial officers, lawyers, court administrators, partner agencies and members of the public to identify where digital products can make the greatest difference.

  • Deliver value incrementally using modern product and engineering practices that reduce delivery risk, support learning from real usage and avoid big-bang replacement.

  • Shape a secure and adaptable platform that can support evolving court processes, new government policies, integrations, data needs and long-term operational resilience.

  • Build alignment and product capability by communicating product direction clearly, influencing through evidence, and coaching or guiding Product Managers where appropriate.

You'll Thrive in This Role If...

  • You bring clarity to ambiguity — framing complex user, operational, legal and policy problems into clear product opportunities.

  • You think strategically and systemically — understanding how court processes, technology, legislation, data and organisational change connect across One Judiciary.

  • You make thoughtful product trade-offs — balancing user value, operational needs, technical sustainability, security, compliance and delivery risk.

  • You lead through influence — building alignment across senior stakeholders, court operations, legal, policy, design, engineering and technology partners.

  • You are comfortable with modern digital delivery — working with multidisciplinary teams, Agile delivery, cloud platforms, APIs, integrations, enterprise systems, product analytics and secure-by-design practices.

  • You raise the bar for product practice — coaching Product Managers where appropriate, contributing to GovTech's product community and strengthening a culture of discovery, evidence and continuous improvement.

Experience leading complex digital products, platforms or enterprise workflows is important. Experience in government, justice, regulated environments or large-scale transformation programmes will be advantageous, but not essential.

What Success Looks Like

In this role, you will help the Judiciary:

  • Improve access to justice by shaping digital services that are easier to use, more inclusive and better aligned to the needs of court users.

  • Modernise critical court operations by streamlining workflows across courts, case types and user groups.

  • Respond faster to change by enabling new legislation, policies and judicial processes to be implemented more quickly and consistently.

  • Build a resilient, adaptable platform that is secure, scalable and able to evolve with the Judiciary's long-term needs.

  • Strengthen product maturity across fCMS by helping teams make better decisions through discovery, data, outcome measurement and continuous improvement.

Why This Role Is Different

Few product management roles offer the opportunity to redesign digital systems that underpin an entire national institution.

As part of GovTech, you will bring modern product, design and engineering practices to one of the Judiciary's most important transformation programmes. As part of the fCMS, you will help shape how justice is delivered in Singapore — not just by building better technology, but by helping create a Judiciary that is more accessible, more responsive and better prepared for the future.

Having knowledge of Judiciary domain is an added advantage.

As a Lead Product Manager, you will hold significant ownership over your product domain, driving it from concept to reality while aligning with the broader programme goals. The role blends deep, hands-on product ownership with leadership of a small and growing team of product managers, working day-to-day alongside agency stakeholders, policy owners, and design and engineering teams.

What you will be working on

Lead Product Manager — Access to Justice & Regulation, Ministry of Law (MLAW)

As Lead Product Manager for Access to Justice and Regulation at the Ministry of Law (MinLaw), you will lead the product strategy and transformation of two of MinLaw's major business verticals.

Your portfolio will span four product domains:

Assess to Justice

  • Legal — helping people who need legal assistance obtain and navigate representation.
  • Community — helping people resolve disputes early and turn legal outcomes into real-world resolution and compliance.

Regulation

  • Licensing — enabling legitimate operators to receive timely permission to operate without compromising regulatory safeguards.
  • Enforcement — helping regulatory teams detect and address risks before they cause serious harm.

Together, these products touch important moments for individuals, businesses and professionals — from seeking legal help and resolving disputes to entering and operating within regulated sectors.

You will help MinLaw rethink how these services should work, organise technology around enduring user problems and policy outcomes, and build the product teams and common capabilities required to deliver them.

In This Role, You Will

  • Own the product strategy across two domains: Access to Justice and Regulation, translating MinLaw's policy outcomes, user needs, operational challenges and technology opportunities into a coherent portfolio direction.
  • Lead and coach Product Managers, giving teams sufficient autonomy to solve their respective problems while ensuring that product strategies reinforce the outcomes of the wider vertical.
  • Define and use outcome measures, establishing meaningful measures of product success and using evidence to understand whether interventions are improving outcomes rather than simply delivering features.
  • Drive the transition from projects to products, establishing enduring ownership and continuous discovery and development instead of treating digitalisation primarily as a sequence of fixed-scope system implementations.
  • Partner deeply with policy and operations, understanding the intent behind legislation, regulation and government programmes while challenging historical processes that unnecessarily constrain user experience or operational effectiveness.
  • Work in close partnership with Engineering and Design leadership, ensuring that product strategy is desirable for users, feasible to build, operationally viable and technically sustainable.
  • Navigate complex product trade-offs, balancing accessibility, regulatory safeguards, policy intent, operational realities, security, cost, delivery risk and long-term sustainability.

You'll Thrive in This Role If...

  • You can lead at multiple levels of abstraction. You are comfortable moving from a conversation about MinLaw's strategic outcomes to a product strategy, an investment decision or a specific user problem — without losing sight of how they connect.
  • You think in portfolios, not just products. You understand that good product leadership sometimes means investing in one product, sharing capabilities across several, consolidating existing solutions or deciding not to build something at all.
  • You are an experienced product leader. You have led complex digital products or platforms and can coach Product Managers rather than needing to personally make every product decision.
  • You bring clarity to ambiguity. You can take complex policy, operational and user problems and turn them into clear product choices that multidisciplinary teams can act on.
  • You think in outcomes rather than systems. You naturally ask what problem we are solving and how we will know whether people's lives or regulatory outcomes have improved, rather than starting with a system, feature or predetermined solution.

Experience in government, legal services, regulation or similarly complex domains is advantageous, but not essential. We value demonstrated product leadership, judgement and the ability to learn complex domains over familiarity with a particular industry.

What Success Looks Like

You will have succeeded when:

  • MinLaw is managing Access to Justice and Regulation as products, not collections of systems and projects. Teams have clear ownership of enduring problems and outcomes, with strategies that persist beyond individual initiatives or technology refreshes.
  • There is evidence that the products are making a difference. Teams have meaningful measures of success and can demonstrate how their work is improving outcomes for the people, businesses and officers who rely on MinLaw's services.
  • MinLaw makes better portfolio choices. Investment decisions are increasingly driven by user and policy outcomes, evidence and strategic priorities — including deliberate decisions about what to build, reuse, consolidate, change or stop.
  • The portfolio becomes simpler over time. Common needs across products and regulatory regimes are solved through shared capabilities and platforms where appropriate, reducing unnecessary duplication and fragmentation.
  • Product teams can respond more quickly to change. New policies and emerging needs can increasingly be addressed by evolving existing products and capabilities rather than starting new technology projects from scratch.

Why This Role Is Different

This role sits at an unusual intersection of product leadership, law, regulation, public policy and technology.

You will not be responsible for a single application or transformation programme.

You will lead product strategy across two major areas of MinLaw's mission and work with multiple Product Managers and multidisciplinary teams to transform how those outcomes are delivered.

Some of the problems will require excellent individual products. Others will require common platforms or capabilities spanning several products. Some may be solved through data or AI. And sometimes the right product decision will be to simplify a process or change an operating model rather than build more technology.

The challenge is to see these connections and make deliberate choices about where product teams and technology can create the greatest public value.

The product portfolio, teams and practices you establish will shape how MinLaw delivers access to justice and regulation for years to come.

[About CCYC]

GovTech's Culture, Community and Youth Cluster (CCYC) partners with the Ministry of Culture, Community and Youth (MCCY) and its statutory boards, including the National Arts Council (NAC), People's Association, Sport Singapore, and MUIS, to deliver digital products that strengthen community life across Singapore. Our products serve millions of Singaporeans across community engagement, cultural participation, youth development, and sports and active lifestyle.

This role sits within CCYC and will be working on NAC products, specifically AHEAD (Arts & Heritage Evaluation, Analytics and Data Portal).

NAC (National Arts Council) is Singapore's lead government agency for the arts, championing the development of a vibrant arts and cultural ecosystem. AHEAD is NAC's centralised data platform, used by NAC and partner agencies, that aggregates fragmented arts datasets to enable holistic sector insights, evidence-based funding decisions, and data-driven planning for Singapore's arts and cultural sector.

We are seeking an experienced Lead Product Manager to own the end-to-end reimagination of AHEAD, across its web portal and the full suite of data pipelines and analytics capabilities that serve NAC and its partner agencies.

GovTech is seeking a strategic and mission-driven Lead/Senior Product Manager to spearhead the AI Safety and Governance pillar within PlatformAI. As AI adoption scales across the public sector, your mission is to ensure that every AI-enabled application is secure, fair, and accountable by design.

You will own a dual-track roadmap:

  • For Developers: Building the "Safety Stack"—a suite of automated Evals, Guardrails, and Red-teaming tools that allow teams to deploy LLMs with speed and confidence.
  • For Governance and Observability: Architecting the "Governance Layer"— observability tools and risk-posture dashboards that provide a unified view of AI compliance across the whole-of-government (WOG) ecosystem.

Key Responsibilities

  1. Defining the Sovereign Safety Standard
    • Define the long-term strategy for AI Safety-as-a-Service, transitioning governance from a manual checklist to an automated platform feature.
    • Synthesize emerging global frameworks and local AI governance policies into platform features that make compliance "invisible" for developers.
    • Establish the government’s standard for AI risk levels, determining the safety benchmarks required for different use cases (e.g., citizen-facing vs. internal productivity).

  2. Building the Guardrails & Audit Trails
    • Lead the development of automated evaluation engines that stress-test products and models for prompt injection, PII leakage, toxicity, and hallucination before and after deployment.
    • Partner with Engineering to integrate safety checks directly into CI/CD pipelines, ensuring that "Safety-by-Design" accelerates rather than hinders deployment.
    • Build real-time monitoring tools to detect "jailbreak" attempts and model drift, ensuring rapid mitigation of live AI risks.

  3. Bridging Policy & Code
    • Act as the primary liaison between Policy/Legal teams and Engineering teams to ensure technical tools meet policy and legal intent.
    • Cultivate a culture of safety across GovTech by publishing playbooks, standardizing red-teaming exercises, and educating teams on the evolving LLM vulnerability landscape.

  4. Trust-Centric Metrics & Accountability
    • Define and track KPIs such as Mean Time to Detect (MTTD) vulnerabilities, Policy Coverage %, and Guardrail Efficacy Rates.

[What we are looking for]

  • Senior Product Leadership: Proven experience managing complex technical products, specifically those focused on Security, Governance, or AI/ML infrastructure.
  • AI Safety Domain Expertise: Deep understanding of Generative AI risks (e.g., prompt injection, training data poisoning, algorithmic bias) and the current state of AI safety research.
  • The "Translator" Skillset: Exceptional ability to distil abstract ethical principles into concrete technical requirements and APIs.
  • Analytical Rigor: A background in using data-driven evaluation frameworks (e.g., RAG evaluation, perplexity scoring, or model benchmarking) to measure performance and risk.
  • Developer Empathy: A deep understanding of developer workflows and a commitment to making safety tools an "accelerant" rather than a "roadblock."

jobTitle: Lead / Senior Software Engineer, Data Programme
jobDescription:
The Government Technology Agency (GovTech) aims to transform the delivery of Government digital services by taking an "outside-in" view, putting citizens and businesses at the heart of everything we do. We also develop the Smart Nation infrastructure and applications, and facilitate collaboration with citizens and businesses to co-develop technologies.

Join us as we support Singapore's vision of building a Smart Nation - a nation of possibilities empowered through info-communications technology and related engineering.

Learn more about GovTech at tech.gov.sg.

[What you will be working on]

Who we are

The mission of GovTech's Data Program is to deliver fit-for-purpose data assets and services for policy making, service delivery and operations across Whole-of-Government (WOG). Our programme creates value through enablement - reducing friction for agencies so they can move faster and make better decisions in their work with existing government datasets.

Key Technical Responsibilities:
You will contribute to the development of one or more of our four strategic technical initiatives:

Standardised Data Platform

  • Build and maintain unified data platform infrastructure for government agencies

  • Develop APIs and services that standardise data ingestion, processing, and storage

  • Create reusable components and templates for agency data platform implementation

  • Implement data connectors and integration tools for legacy systems

Unified Frontend / DataHive

  • Develop the central data discovery and access request platform

  • Build intuitive user interfaces for data catalogue browsing and metadata search

  • Implement request management workflows and approval systems

  • Create responsive web applications that serve both data consumers and providers

Unified Serving Backbone

  • Design and implement standardised data delivery APIs and microservices

  • Build robust data serving infrastructure that can handle high-volume requests

  • Develop authentication and authorisation systems for secure data access

  • Create monitoring and alerting systems for data delivery pipelines

Observability & Governance Infrastructure

  • Build central observability systems for data quality monitoring and lineage tracking

  • Develop dashboards and analytics tools for data usage patterns

  • Implement automated data quality checks and validation frameworks

  • Create audit trails and compliance reporting systems

What the role is

You will work on both small and large scale projects, building and maintaining the infrastructure behind them. We are fully aligned with the Government's cloud-first policy and you will bring capability to help us realize this. The role includes:

  • Managing the development, deployment, orchestration and maintenance of data pipelines for our products

  • Ensuring the scalability, performance, and reliability of Cloud-based applications

  • Providing DevOps architecture implementation and operational support

  • Architecture and planning for cloud deployments (Private and Public cloud)

  • Developing and managing processes, automation, best practices, documentation

  • Development and operation of continuous integration and deployment pipelines.

What it is like working here

We build products that serve a variety of agency users, who use them to solve highly meaningful problems pertinent to our society, from transportation, to education, to healthcare. The public sector is full of opportunities where even the simplest software can have a big impact on people’s lives. We are here to improve how we live as a society through what we can offer as a government.

  • Rapid Prototyping - Instead of spending too much time debating ideas we prefer testing them. This identifies potential problems quickly, and more importantly, conveys what is possible to others easily.

  • Reliable Productization - To scale an idea, a prototype or a Minimum Viable Product to a software product, we scrutinize and commit to its usability, reliability, scalability and maintainability.

  • Ownership - In addition to technical responsibilities, this means having ideas on how things should be done and taking responsibility for seeing them through. Building something that you believe in is the best way to build something good.

  • Continuous Learning - Working on new ideas often means not fully understanding what you are working on. Taking time to learn new architectures, frameworks, technologies, and even languages is not just encouraged but essential

[What we are looking for]

The customers for our products are normally agency users, which means that breadth of knowledge in government IT infrastructure and experience in government networks will help. Since our direction is cloud-first, you will likely have some experience in patch/update scheduling, and knowledge of security incident response procedures. A disciplined approach and strong problem-solving instincts are fundamental to succeed. Your aptitude for completing the tasks and attitude to continuous learning are more valued than any formal certification. To succeed, you will need to possess some of the following:

  • Excellent problem solving and methodical troubleshooting skills

  • Strong knowledge and experience in DevOps automation, containerization and orchestration using tools eg. Ansible, Airflow, Docker, Kubernetes, Terraform, Artifactory/Nexus Sonatype

  • Cloud computing deployment and management experience in AWS, GCP

  • Strong scripting skills e.g. Python, Bash, JavaScript, Scala, Rust, Go

  • Strong understanding of Apache Spark/Flink, Hadoop, distributed file systems and resource scaling/scheduling, streaming message queues (RabbitMQ, Kafka)

  • Strong understanding of virtualization and networking concepts

  • Experience with patch maintenance, regression testing and security incident response

  • Experience with interactive workloads, machine learning toolkits and how they integrate with cloud computing e.g. Databricks, KX

  • Experience with highly scalable distributed systems

  • Experience with on-premise deployments, government application and networking infrastructure/routing

  • Breadth of knowledge - OS, networking, distributed computing, cloud computing

jobDescription:
