At MOE, our mission is to empower every learner to achieve their fullest potential and to build a future-ready nation through a dynamic and inclusive education system. We are dedicated to cultivating an environment that nurtures innovative teaching practices, critical thinking, and lifelong learning. Our mandate is to shape policies and drive initiatives that not only enhance the quality of education but also integrate digital advancements and global best practices—ensuring that our educators and students are well-prepared to navigate and excel in an ever-evolving world.

Joining MOE DXD’s Tf(x) team will place you at the forefront of transforming education through technology. As part of our innovative unit, you will create bespoke tools tailored specifically for educators, empowering them to streamline processes, enrich classroom experiences, and inspire the next generation of learners. In this role, your technical expertise will intersect with visionary educational goals. This is an opportunity to drive meaningful change in a dynamic environment where creativity, collaboration, and cutting-edge technology converge to shape the future of education.

Expect yourself to collaborate with experienced educators, product/ops managers, software engineers and designers to rapidly prototype innovative solutions that tackle key challenges in the education sector. You will be working in an environment that encourages continuous learning through hands-on guidance and mentorship. Be prepared to utilise a continuous integration engineering pipeline and an iterative design process to streamline both development and testing.

[What you will be working on]

You will work in Tf(x), a team of product/ops managers, software engineers and designers (formerly Transform): “We're a dynamic team, equally driven by our passion for making a positive impact and our dedication to our craft. Whether we're developing robust software or designing user-centric experiences, we ensure that everything we do is delivered at our best.”

Your job scope with our team is as follows:

  • Develop bespoke digital tools to help schools and teachers address their operational and administrative pain-points. You will join a team of software engineers, product managers and designers to establish a digital product team with the broad objective of building bespoke products for MOE officers and educators. This includes data analytics tools for analysing student results, profiling tools to identify at-risk students, and even an ops-readiness digital product to ready schools for emergencies such as COVID-19. Much of the work will be synthesised from hackathons, user discovery sessions, workshops and rapid prototyping.
  • Modernise the School Cockpit IT system and reorganise the engineering team structure. The School Cockpit is a critical system used by schools and educators for school administrative tasks and aggregating student information across Singapore. The vision is for MOE to re-conceptualise this long-standing system into a collection of applications with potential reuseability across the entire MOE ecosystem. Aside from engineering work, there will be an opportunity to work with MOE’s engineering partners in the private sector, and transform the way public-private engineering partnerships have traditionally worked in MOE.
  • Facilitate the transfer of central engineering knowledge from GovTech to MOE. You will be working with a product team who has previously built central products (e.g. SafeEntry, TraceTogether and OurSG Grants Portal) and Artificial Intelligence products that look into the extraction, synthesis and usage of data in government agencies. You will work with the team to actively transfer such intellectual property and know-how gradually into the MOE IT ecosystem, through strategic placement in apps.

[What we are looking for]

  • Demonstrate a solid understanding of responsive web application development and a willingness to enhance your skills.
  • Experience with continuous integration tools is a plus (added advantage). (Note: On-the-job training will be provided if needed.)
  • Possess working knowledge of at least one of the following—or show a willingness to learn:
    • JavaScript (added advantage: experience with React, TypeScript, Next.js, NestJS)
    • Go
    • Python
  • Exposure to any of the following areas is an added advantage, and our team is here to help you grow in these areas:
    • ML/AI/GenAI frameworks
    • Testing methodologies and troubleshooting techniques
    • Cloud application development/deployment fundamentals
    • Common IPC/RPC methods and patterns
    • OS/networking basics
  • Show curiosity in DevSecOps (added advantage).
  • Thrive in a collaborative, high-performing team environment.

jobTitle: Principal / Lead Product Manager, TradeNet, DEP
jobDescription:
GovTech is Singapore's lead agency for digital government and the Smart Nation initiative. We build and deploy technology that meaningfully improves lives — for citizens, businesses, and the public sector.

Digital Economy Products (DEP) is a division within GovTech that operates with the pace and rigour of a modern product company. Our teams tackle high-stakes problems across Singapore's public sectors — Healthcare, Manpower, Trade and Finance, National Development, Sustainability, and more — and build digital products that serve millions.

Many of Singapore's most critical government systems were built decades ago — pioneering for their time, but now running on aging technology, tightly bound to vendor dependencies, and struggling to keep pace with evolving policy and industry demands. We are bringing these platforms in-house and rebuilding them from the ground up — rethinking not just the technology, but the operating models, user experiences, and regulatory workflows they underpin.

Two flagship programmes are currently underway:

TradeNet — Singapore's National Single Window for trade permit processing. Launched in the late 1980s, it processes over 9 million permit applications annually across import, export, and transshipment, contributing to approximately 10% of national tax revenues. Designated as critical IT infrastructure, TradeNet is being brought in-house to secure Singapore's technology sovereignty over one of its most consequential trade systems.

CoreNet X — Singapore's national digital platform for regulatory approval of building works. It unifies eight regulatory agencies into a single BIM-based submission and processing system, transforming how the built environment sector interacts with government.

Both programmes sit at the intersection of complex regulation, enterprise-scale technology, and high public-sector impact. As a Principal Product Manager at DEP, you will be at the centre of this transformation — working at the frontier of how government systems are redesigned, rebuilt, and reimagined for the future.

Responsibilities

  • Define and own the product strategy for modernisation of your key system(s).
  • Translate complex business, technical, and policy insights into clear roadmaps that align teams and drive measurable outcomes.
  • Establish success metrics (OKRs, KPIs) and ensure alignment with the policy, business, and operational objectives.
  • Build strong stakeholder alignment through evidence, trust, and well-earned relationships — resolving complex dependencies and securing senior management support for product strategy and investments.
  • Develop deep system and domain expertise, serving as the subject-matter expert for your product(s) — bringing informed perspective to agency escalations, regulatory tradeoffs, and decisions that shape product approach across government and industry stakeholders.
  • Champion adoption of emerging technologies and industry best practices to improve team effectiveness and impact.
  • Lead and mentor a team of talented product managers, setting the bar for product thinking, execution rigour, and professional development of each team member.
  • Lead hiring of other product leaders for your team and outside, identify and coach future leaders
  • Lead end‑to‑end product execution of a major product —from ideation to launch to iteration—ensuring high standards of quality, security, accessibility, and compliance.
  • Collaborate with engineering, design, research, operations, and data teams to deliver cohesive, scalable user experiences.

Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree and 10+ years of product management or equivalent experience with strong demonstrated impact in the consumer/enterprise/platform ecosystem.
  • Track record of delivering complex products at scale with measurable business impact.
  • Excellent communication and leadership skills, capable of inspiring teams and influencing senior leaders.
  • Strong stakeholder management skills — ability to navigate complex, multi-agency environments and build alignment across government agencies, vendor partners, and industry players.
  • Strong analytical skills with the ability to leverage data to inform product decisions.
  • Proven experience hiring, managing, mentoring, and coaching a team of product managers.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience modernising or re-platforming complex enterprise systems, B2B applications, or legacy platforms.
  • Domain expertise in trade/customs or building/construction industries.
  • Experience in process optimisation, regulatory technology, or government digital transformation.
  • Prior engineering experience working on complex web applications or enterprise systems.

The Developer Productivity Programme equips thousands of government engineers with the platforms, tools, and practices they need to ship faster, more safely, and with greater confidence. This is a platform product role. The programme's product suite spans CI/CD, Managed Runtimes, AI tooling and enablement, as well as surfacing data, insights and productivity metrics to stakeholders. We serve close to 100 government agencies and thousands of developers, including vendors who build and maintain government systems.

A key part of the programme's direction is deepening AI usage for developers, from running experiments and building agentic workflows to ensuring the right security guardrails are in place for AI-assisted development at scale. We are seeking a Principal Product Manager who combines strong product leadership with a genuine understanding of developers and how they work. The best person for this role has a feel for what makes developer tools great, cares deeply about the developer experience, and can bring both strategic vision and practical credibility to the role.

[What you will be working on]

Product Strategy, Portfolio Health and New Product Development

  • You will own the product strategy across the programme's full portfolio. This means building strategy grounded in user insights, market trends, and organisational goals, translating them into OKRs and long-term roadmaps, and driving execution within and across teams.
  • You will define the right success metrics across the programme and products, track them consistently, and follow up to ensure the insights are being acted on. Products must not just be built and launched but actively used, delivering genuine value to users, and financially sustainable.
  • You will also be expected to envision what comes next. This means identifying opportunities the programme has not yet addressed, staying close to where the developer landscape is heading, and working with the Product Managers to develop and execute on new product ideas.

Whole-of-Government Adoption and Stakeholder Engagement

  • You will drive adoption of developer productivity tools across the Whole of Government. Government agencies are at different stages of digital maturity and the approach must account for that, meeting agencies where they are while progressively raising the bar. You will work with counterparts from engineering, policy, security, and operations to unblock challenges in product rollouts, whether navigating policy constraints, meeting security and compliance requirements, or building the guardrails that allow teams to move forward.

AI Product Leadership

  • You will define how the programme's products evolve to support an AI-native software development lifecycle. The programme works with and integrates AI developer tools, including building components and workflows that extend their capabilities for the government context. You will shape the product vision for AI-enabled developer tooling at scale, ensuring the portfolio helps government engineering teams adopt AI across how they write, review, test, and ship code.

Go-to-Market Leadership

  • You will own the go-to-market function for the programme's products, including platform pricing strategy and working with Comms and Marketing on positioning and communications. You are accountable for ensuring that what gets built also gets adopted.

Team Leadership and Talent Development

  • You will lead and grow a team of Product Managers, setting high standards for product craft and mentoring individuals on analysis, strategy, and execution. You will actively develop future leaders within the team.

[What we are looking for]

  • Significant experience in product management, with a proven track record of owning product strategy for complex, multi-product portfolios and driving outcomes across multiple teams.

  • A developer or engineering background, or deep experience working alongside engineering teams. Someone who has used developer tools, has strong opinions about what makes them good, and can speak with authority on what great looks like. The kind of person who tinkers, experiments out of curiosity, and instinctively understands the difference between a tool that empowers developers and one that gets in their way.

  • Deep empathy for developers as users and a clear understanding of what enterprises and government agencies need from developer tooling at scale, including how to navigate policy constraints and compliance requirements without blocking adoption.

  • Demonstrated ability to build product strategy from user insights and market trends. Experience owning go-to-market strategy including pricing, positioning, and communications.

  • Strong cross-organisational skills. Able to work with counterparts from engineering, policy, operations, and other product teams, influence at the executive level, and build the relationships needed to get things done in a complex organisation.

  • Proven ability to cultivate high-performing teams, mentor product managers, and actively develop future leaders.

  • Actively experimenting with AI tools and thinking about what they mean for the developer experience.

jobDescription:

About the Role
AI is being adopted across government at pace — and with that comes real risk. Models hallucinate. Prompts get injected. Outputs can be unsafe. And AI-generated media is getting harder to spot and easier to produce at scale.

We’re looking for a product manager to contribute to our work in making AI safer and more accountable across government. You’ll be part of AssuranceAI — the AI Programme’s function focused on AI behaviour and AI risk — and you’ll own an assigned product area spanning evaluation, runtime safeguards, assurance reporting, and AI manipulation detection.

You’ll work within a team led by a lead product manager, and you’ll be expected to operate with a high degree of independence within your scope. This means getting into the details with engineers and policy teams, translating direction into concrete requirements, and seeing things through to delivery.


[What you will be working on]

1. AI Evaluation

  • Execute on the product roadmap for AI evaluation — covering groundedness, citation quality, safety and adversarial testing, and regression evaluation.

  • Work with engineering to build and maintain reusable evaluation sets that product teams across the AI Programme can rely on, reducing duplicated effort.

  • Use AI observability data to support groundedness evaluation, unsafe output analysis, and AI risk reporting.

2. Runtime Safeguards

  • Contribute to the development of runtime safeguarding capabilities — including unsafe prompt and output detection, sensitive-content controls, prompt-injection indicators, and policy-based AI controls.

  • Work with engineering to embed safeguards into development workflows, following the assurance-by-design approach established by the team.

  • Support real-time monitoring for model drift, unsafe outputs, and prompt-injection attempts — flagging issues and working with engineering to resolve them.

3. Assurance Reporting

  • Maintain and improve AI assurance reporting — evaluation history, risk and remediation records, and assurance status — contributing to the team’s overall view of AI risk posture.

  • Track and report on defined KPIs: evaluation coverage, guardrail efficacy, mean time to detect vulnerabilities, and policy coverage.

4. AI Manipulation and Online Safety

  • Execute on the product roadmap for a whole-of-government platform that benchmarks and integrates AI detection solutions across image, video, and audio.

  • Support continuous evaluation as the deepfake threat landscape evolves — gathering performance data, surfacing findings, and contributing to decisions on which detection capabilities to onboard, refresh, or retire.

  • Work with capability developers and partner agencies to keep the platform operationally effective as a shared government service.

  • Participate in the Community of Practice across government — sharing benchmarking lessons, datasets, and evaluation insights.

5. Translating Policy into Product

  • Translate defined policy direction and requirements into concrete product specifications, evaluation criteria, and platform features.

  • Work with the AI Practice to keep teams current on the evolving AI risk and vulnerability landscape, and contribute to playbooks and guidance materials.


[What we are looking for]

  • Product experience — You’ve owned products or feature areas end-to-end and know what it takes to ship things that actually work for users.

  • AI domain curiosity — You don’t need to be an AI safety expert on day one, but you should be genuinely interested in AI risk, evaluation, safeguards, or online safety — and willing to go deep quickly.

  • Analytical approach — You’re at ease working with evaluation metrics, benchmarking results, and usage data to make decisions. You test assumptions before committing to development and use evidence to navigate trade-offs.

  • Policy-to-product translation — You can read policy direction and translate it into something concrete — requirements, features, platform decisions.

  • Stakeholder range — You can work effectively with engineers, agency users, capability developers, and policy teams — and keep them aligned without losing momentum.

  • Execution discipline — You’re organised, proactive, and can manage multiple workstreams without dropping the ball.

[About the role]

GovTech's CIO's Office builds products that improve how GovTech operates and that can, where relevant, serve as useful models for the wider public sector. The Hiring to Productivity workstream covers the full workforce journey: translating manpower plans into hiring needs, running effective recruitment processes, equipping people with the tools and access they need, and helping them become productive as quickly as possible. Throughout this journey, we aim to maintain sound security, data and operational controls.

As a Product Manager (II), you will own a product, substantial feature area or defined problem within this journey. Depending on workstream priorities, this could involve products supporting manpower planning, recruitment, workforce records, onboarding, equipment and access provisioning, or workforce administration. The current domain includes products such as Manpower Nexus, Greenhouse, T-rex, Equip and Punchcard.

You will work with users, business owners, product operations, design and engineering to understand problems, decide what matters most and deliver improvements from discovery through launch and iteration. You will be expected to operate independently within your product area, while working closely with the PM Lead to ensure that your roadmap supports the wider Hiring to Productivity strategy.

You will be accountable for the outcomes and day-to-day product decisions within your assigned area. The PM Lead owns the end-to-end workstream strategy and portfolio trade-offs across multiple products; you will work together on cross-product dependencies, material risks and decisions that affect the wider journey.

This is an individual-contributor role for a PM who is ready to independently own a product area. The PM Lead will provide coaching, organisational context and direction on workstream priorities, while giving you room to exercise judgement and grow your product craft.

This role suits someone who enjoys making sense of ambiguous operational problems, is comfortable working across organisational boundaries and wants to use technology to improve the everyday experience of public officers and the teams that support them.

[What you will be working on]

The journey from manpower planning to productivity spans multiple teams, policies and systems. Today, users and operational teams may need to navigate fragmented workflows, repeated data entry, manual coordination and unclear hand-offs between stages. Decisions made in one part of the journey can also create downstream effects—for example, the quality of manpower and recruitment data affects how smoothly a person can be onboarded, equipped and supported.

You will work with an established cross-functional group of engineers, designers and product operations colleagues, as well as business partners across GovTech. Your challenge will be to improve an assigned part of this journey while understanding how it connects to the whole. This may involve creating a new product, modernising a legacy service, improving an existing product or joining up workflows and data across products.

Own product outcomes and direction

  • Own the success of an assigned product, substantial feature area or defined problem from discovery and prioritisation through delivery, launch and continuous improvement.
  • Define clear user and organisational outcomes, and develop a product strategy and roadmap that align with the Hiring to Productivity workstream.
  • Prioritise opportunities based on user needs, expected impact, evidence, effort, risk and dependencies—not simply the volume or seniority of requests.
  • Focus the team on the work with the greatest expected value, adapting plans independently as new evidence or constraints emerge.

Understand users and define the right problems

  • Conduct user research and analyse operational data to understand the needs of workforce planners, recruiters, hiring managers, employees and external workforce members, as well as HR, security and operational teams.
  • Map end-to-end journeys and identify where fragmented processes, unclear ownership or poor data hand-offs create delays, rework or control risks.
  • Turn research, feedback and operational insights into clear problem statements, product requirements and measurable hypotheses.
  • Validate or reject ideas early through data analysis, prototypes and lightweight experiments before committing significant engineering effort.

Deliver effectively with a cross-functional team

  • Work closely with engineers, designers and product operations colleagues to shape solutions, clarify requirements and deliver useful increments.
  • Make practical trade-offs between speed, quality, scope and simplicity, with a clear understanding of implementation constraints and operational consequences.
  • Keep delivery on track by surfacing dependencies and risks early, resolving issues proactively and engaging the PM Lead or relevant specialists when needed.
  • Ensure that privacy, cybersecurity, reliability and accessibility needs are considered throughout product development rather than only at launch.

Build connected, measurable services

  • Partner with the owners of related products—including Manpower Nexus, Greenhouse, T-rex, Equip and Punchcard—to improve end-to-end workflows, strengthen data flows and reduce duplicated data entry or manual coordination.
  • Remain accountable for the outcomes, interfaces and dependencies within your assigned product or problem area, while working with the PM Lead on trade-offs that span the wider portfolio.
  • Partner with technical teams on system integrations, data ownership, error handling and the controls needed for sensitive workforce information.
  • Define success measures before launch, establish appropriate product analytics and use the resulting evidence to decide whether to iterate, scale or stop an initiative.
  • Track outcomes such as time to productivity, processing time, data quality, task completion, adoption, user satisfaction and reduction in manual effort.

Drive adoption and contribute to the team

  • Partner with product operations and business teams to plan and deliver the communications, training, documentation and transition support needed for successful adoption.
  • Build trusted relationships with stakeholders, communicate decisions and trade-offs clearly, and influence outcomes without relying on formal authority.
  • Share research, data, lessons, successes and failures openly so that other product teams can benefit from the work.
  • Contribute to a constructive team culture, help peers where useful and suggest improvements to the team's ways of working.

[What we are looking for]

  • Experience owning a digital product, substantial feature area or service improvement from discovery through launch and iteration.
  • Experience with zero-to-one products, product modernisation or ambiguous operational problems would be beneficial.
  • A data-focused approach, using qualitative and quantitative evidence to prioritise work, test assumptions and evaluate outcomes.
  • Ability to work closely with engineers, designers and business owners, understand their respective needs and trade-offs, and make sensible decisions about speed, quality and simplicity.
  • Technical fluency in areas such as APIs, system integrations, data models, security and privacy would be useful; deep software engineering expertise is not required.
  • Strong written and verbal communication, with the ability to work through differing stakeholder needs and influence across organisational boundaries.
  • A high degree of ownership: you identify and address issues with minimal guidance, while recognising when to seek help or escalate a material risk.
  • Interest in public service and in improving the systems and experiences that help government teams do their best work.

[About This Role]

We are looking for a Product Manager to work on the development and adoption of a centralised data discovery platform that serves as the single authoritative entry point for public officers across the whole of government to find, evaluate, and request access to government data.

Today, data discovery is fragmented across multiple platforms, each with its own go-to-market effort, onboarding process, and user experience. This creates confusion, duplication, and missed opportunities for data reuse. Your role is to change that — by building a product that becomes the definitive "first stop" for any public officer looking for government data, and by driving the ecosystem-level coordination needed to make that vision real.

This role that sits at the intersection of product, data governance, and cross-agency coordination. You will be responsible for both the strategic positioning of the platform and the day-to-day execution of product improvements — from search experience and catalogue coverage, to request workflows and integration with downstream delivery systems.

[What you will be working on]

As a Product Manager, you will hold significant ownership over your product domain, driving it from concept to reality while aligning with the broader programme goals. Your core responsibilities include:

Establishing and Communicating a Clear Product Vision

  • Execute Own and articulate the product vision for a centralised data discovery platform, ensuring alignment across engineering, design, policy, and senior stakeholders

  • Contribute to Define and maintain a coherent product strategy that positions the platform as the single entry point for government data discovery, replacing fragmented multi-platform behaviour

  • Collaborate with programme leadership and agency partners to secure buy-in and drive adoption at scale across government

Driving Catalogue Growth and Coverage

  • ExecuteLead the strategy to expand the platform's central catalogue by working with agency data owners and platform teams to surface more government data in one place — without necessarily requiring agencies to migrate their underlying systems

  • Identify and resolve the technical, operational, and incentive barriers that prevent agency datasets from being discoverable centrally, and develop scalable approaches to address them

  • Work with agency data owners to improve metadata completeness and quality so that datasets are genuinely useful to discover, not just listed

Improving Search, Discovery, and Request Experience

  • Own the end-to-end user experience for data discovery, from search and browse to dataset evaluation, access request, and approval

  • Use search analytics and user research to identify where the discovery journey breaks down — and drive iterative, evidence-based improvements

  • Explore how emerging technologies, including AI, might fundamentally reimagine how users find and evaluate data relevant to their needs — going beyond conventional search to ask what a great discovery experience could look like

  • Ensure that data consumers can assess dataset fitness-for-purpose directly within the discovery experience, without needing to contact data owners separately

Streamlining the Request and Approval Workflow

  • Drive consolidation of the inter-agency data request process into a single, trackable workflow within the platform, reducing fragmentation and improving visibility for both requestors and approvers

  • Work with policy and governance teams to digitalise and simplify approval processes, reducing time from request creation to first data access

  • Enable data providers to manage their sharing obligations — including approvals, rejections, and monitoring — through a single console experience

Reducing Friction Between Discovery and Data Use

  • Investigate and address the gap between a user finding a dataset and being able to actually use it in their work — understanding where friction exists in how data is accessed, integrated, and consumed across different working environments

  • Define and validate approaches that reduce the effort required for users to go from discovery to productive use, without prescribing a fixed technical solution upfront

Driving Adoption and Go-to-Market

  • Develop and execute a go-to-market strategy that consolidates user mindshare around a single discovery platform, replacing fragmented awareness across competing products

  • Build and maintain relationships with key agency stakeholders — both data providers and data consumers — to drive onboarding, usage, and feedback loops

  • Use consolidated user activity data to generate insights that improve the product and demonstrate value to programme leadership and agency partners

Monitoring, Measuring, and Iterating

  • Define and track product metrics that reflect real discovery success (e.g. search success rate, time from request to first access, catalogue coverage) rather than vanity metrics

  • Run structured experiments and user studies to validate product decisions and prioritise the roadmap

  • Maintain a clear, well-reasoned product backlog and communicate trade-offs transparently to stakeholders

Compliance and Governance

  • Ensure the platform meets security, performance, and data governance requirements applicable to a whole-of-government system handling sensitive metadata and access workflows

  • Adhere to compliance requirements and audits (IM8, AGO, QMS, etc.)

[What we are looking for]

The customers for our products are normally agency users, which means that prior public service experience will help. A disciplined approach and strong problem-solving instincts are fundamental to succeed. Your aptitude for completing the tasks and attitude to continuous learning are more valued than any formal certification.

We look for product managers with:

  • Product management experience, with a demonstrated track record of owning and shipping products used at scale by diverse user groups

  • Experience driving adoption of a platform or tool in a multi-stakeholder environment where you did not have direct authority over all users or contributors

  • Strong product sense — ability to translate ambiguous strategic goals into concrete, prioritised product decisions

  • Proven ability to work directly and effectively with engineers, designers, and data or platform specialists (at least 3 years in cross-functional product teams)

  • Strong analytical skills — comfortable using data to diagnose problems, validate hypotheses, and communicate product performance

  • Excellent communication and stakeholder management skills, including the ability to influence senior decision-makers and drive alignment across organisations

  • Prior experience with data cataloguing, metadata management, search/discovery products, or developer/analyst-facing platforms

  • Experience working in or with government agencies, or in other large, federated organisations where adoption requires ecosystem coordination rather than top-down mandates

  • Familiarity with data governance concepts (e.g. data stewardship, data classification, access control workflows)

  • Experience designing or improving approval and workflow automation features

  • Exposure to AI-assisted product features, particularly in search or recommendation contexts

  • Specific government data policies, classification frameworks, and inter-agency data sharing processes

  • Technical details of the underlying data infrastructure and delivery mechanisms

  • The specific agency landscape, stakeholder map, and political dynamics of the programme

Requirements

  • Diploma/Degree in Computer Science, Infocomm Technology, Engineering, or a related subject area, with a minimum of 5 years of relevant experience. Candidates with more experience will be considered for more senior roles.

  • Prior working experience in product management, IT business analysis, or application solutioning design and testing

  • Experience in modern product development and management practices such as Agile, Design Thinking, and Product-Centric Development will be strongly preferred

  • Relevant certifications such as CITPM, COMIT, PMP, or Certified Scrum Master are advantageous

jobDescription:

[What you will be working on]

As a Product Manager, you will hold significant ownership over your product domain, driving it from concept to reality while aligning with the broader programme goals. Your core responsibilities include:

Product Manager (Future Courts Management System)

Shape the future of justice in Singapore

Justice is one of Singapore's most important public services. Every year, almost 200,000 cases pass through our courts, involving individuals, families, businesses, lawyers and public agencies. Behind every case is someone seeking a fair, timely and accessible resolution.

The Judiciary's transformation into One Judiciary brought together the Supreme Court, State Courts and Family Justice Courts under a shared vision of delivering justice that is trusted, accessible and ready for the future.

Realising this vision requires more than organisational change. It requires rethinking the digital systems, processes and services that underpin how justice is delivered.

The Future Courts Management System (fCMS) is the Judiciary's flagship digital transformation programme, developed in close partnership with GovTech. You will join GovTech's product management community while working deeply with the Judiciary to shape products that support the administration of justice across Singapore's Courts.

This is not simply a like-for-like replacement of legacy systems. It is an opportunity to reimagine how court services should work: making them easier to use, more responsive to changing legislation and policies, and better able to serve everyone who depends on them.

This is a rare opportunity to help shape how justice will be delivered in Singapore for years to come.

The Role

As a Product Manager, you will be close to these problems and the people experiencing them. You will turn that understanding into product decisions and work with your team to make those decisions real.

You will work as part of a product trio with Engineering and Design, you will own a product problem space within fCMS — understanding the people and processes involved, discovering what should be built, prioritising what matters most, and working with your team to deliver measurable improvements.

As part of GovTech, you will be supported by a wider product, design and engineering community while working deeply with the Judiciary to build long-term digital capability.

In this role, you will:

  • Discover what problems are worth solving, working directly with judges, judicial officers, lawyers, court administrators, partner agencies and members of the public to understand their needs and pain points.

  • Prioritise based on evidence and outcomes, making decisions about what to build now, what to learn more about and what not to build.

  • Deliver value incrementally using modern product and engineering practices that reduce delivery risk, support learning from real usage and avoid big-bang replacement.

  • Measure whether the product is working, defining meaningful measures of success and using qualitative and quantitative evidence to understand where the product should improve.

  • Build alignment around product decisions, communicating the problem, evidence, priorities and trade-offs clearly to stakeholders and your delivery team.

You'll Thrive in This Role If...

  • You are curious about users and their problems. You want to understand why something works the way it does before deciding what should be built.

  • You think beyond requirements. When someone asks for a feature, you naturally want to understand the underlying problem and whether there might be a better way to solve it.

  • You use evidence to make decisions. You are comfortable combining user research, operational knowledge, product data and technical input rather than relying only on stakeholder opinion.

  • You make thoughtful product trade-offs — balancing user value, operational needs, technical sustainability, security, compliance and delivery risk.

  • You communicate clearly. You can explain a complicated problem, the evidence behind a decision and the trade-offs involved in a way that different audiences can understand.

  • You want to develop your product craft. You actively seek feedback, learn from more experienced Product Managers and reflect on how you can make better product decisions.

You should have experience working on digital products or services and have participated meaningfully in activities such as product discovery, user research, prioritisation, delivery or product analytics. Experience in government, justice, legal services or other complex domains is advantageous, but not essential.

What Success Looks Like

You will have succeeded when:

  • You understand your problem space deeply — not only the system, but the users, court processes and outcomes it exists to support.

  • Your team is solving problems rather than processing requirements, with clear reasoning behind what it chooses to build and what it chooses not to build.

  • You make increasingly independent product decisions, using evidence and good judgement while knowing when to seek guidance or escalate wider strategic decisions.

  • Your product improves through learning, with user feedback, product data and operational evidence influencing what the team does next.

  • Your team delivers useful improvements incrementally, creating value and reducing uncertainty throughout the transformation rather than only at the end.

  • People trust you as the product owner for your space, because you understand the problem, communicate decisions clearly and follow through on outcomes.

Why This Role Is Different

Few product management roles offer the opportunity to be part of the team that redesigns a digital system that underpin an entire national institution.

As part of GovTech, you will bring modern product, design and engineering practices to one of the Judiciary's most important transformation programmes. As part of the fCMS, you will help shape how justice is delivered in Singapore — not just by building better technology, but by helping create a Judiciary that is more accessible, more responsive and better prepared for the future.

Job Summary

GovTech is seeking a strategic and mission-driven Lead/Senior Product Manager to spearhead the AI Safety and Governance pillar within PlatformAI. As AI adoption scales across the public sector, your mission is to ensure that every AI-enabled application is secure, fair, and accountable by design.

You will own a dual-track roadmap:

  • For Developers: Building the "Safety Stack"—a suite of automated Evals, Guardrails, and Red-teaming tools that allow teams to deploy LLMs with speed and confidence.
  • For Governance and Observability: Architecting the "Governance Layer"—observability tools and risk-posture dashboards that provide a unified view of AI compliance across the whole-of-government (WOG) ecosystem.

Key Responsibilities

1. Defining the Sovereign Safety Standard

  • Define the long-term strategy for AI Safety-as-a-Service, transitioning governance from a manual checklist to an automated platform feature.
  • Synthesize emerging global frameworks and local AI governance policies into platform features that make compliance "invisible" for developers.
  • Establish the government’s standard for AI risk levels, determining the safety benchmarks required for different use cases (e.g., citizen-facing vs. internal productivity).

2. Building the Guardrails & Audit Trails

  • Lead the development of automated evaluation engines that stress-test products and models for prompt injection, PII leakage, toxicity, and hallucination before and after deployment.
  • Partner with Engineering to integrate safety checks directly into CI/CD pipelines, ensuring that "Safety-by-Design" accelerates rather than hinders deployment.
  • Build real-time monitoring tools to detect "jailbreak" attempts and model drift, ensuring rapid mitigation of live AI risks.

3. Bridging Policy & Code

  • Act as the primary liaison between Policy/Legal teams and Engineering teams to ensure technical tools meet policy and legal intent.
  • Cultivate a culture of safety across GovTech by publishing playbooks, standardizing red-teaming exercises, and educating teams on the evolving LLM vulnerability landscape.

4. Trust-Centric Metrics & Accountability

  • Define and track KPIs such as Mean Time to Detect (MTTD) vulnerabilities, Policy Coverage %, and Guardrail Efficacy Rates.

What You Will Bring

  • Senior Product Leadership: Proven experience managing complex technical products, specifically those focused on Security, Governance, or AI/ML infrastructure.
  • AI Safety Domain Expertise: Deep understanding of Generative AI risks (e.g., prompt injection, training data poisoning, algorithmic bias) and the current state of AI safety research.
  • The "Translator" Skillset: Exceptional ability to distil abstract ethical principles into concrete technical requirements and APIs.
  • Analytical Rigor: A background in using data-driven evaluation frameworks (e.g., RAG evaluation, perplexity scoring, or model benchmarking) to measure performance and risk.
  • Developer Empathy: A deep understanding of developer workflows and a commitment to making safety tools an "accelerant" rather than a "roadblock."

[What you will be working on]

SEED (Security Suite for Engineering Endpoint Devices) is the Singapore Government's endpoint security and zero trust platform for engineering devices. It is already live across thousands of engineering endpoints, supporting a growing range of builders — from traditional software engineers to teams developing AI-powered and agentic solutions. With an expanding product surface — secure remote access, managed productivity tools, AI-assisted security operations — and a clear mandate: keep it secure, make it seamless, and evolve it to stay ahead of both threats and user expectations.

As the Product Manager for SEED, you will own the product roadmap and run SEED as a live platform — keeping it stable, secure, and frictionless enough that engineers can focus on shipping.

What you'll own:

  • SEED is the security foundation for government engineering. SEED needs to be fast, reliable, and frictionless enough that engineers can focus on shipping. Your job is to run SEED as a live platform: keep it stable, reduce operational overhead, improve the user experience at every touchpoint, and evolve the capability surface as threats and engineering needs change.

​You are expected to:

  • Own the SEED product roadmap and drive ongoing improvement of a live platform serving thousands of engineering endpoints — balancing security outcomes with engineering velocity.

  • Reduce the time and friction it takes for an agency engineer to go from device assignment to fully compliant and productive on SEED.

  • Drive consolidation so SEED and adjacent products (e.g. TechPass, GCC, M365) work together as a coherent experience for engineers. Own the integration roadmap and clarify where boundaries sit.

  • Systematically reduce friction. Surface where security controls slow engineers down and invest in making compliance invisible — automated onboarding, self-service remediation, clear error states, AI-assisted analysis that saves time rather than generating noise.

  • Anticipate and support emerging engineering workflows, including AI-assisted development and agentic systems, ensuring SEED evolves to meet new security and productivity needs.

  • Work closely with adjacent product teams so the full engineering device lifecycle — identity, device management, and security — holds together as a coherent experience for agencies.

You do this by:

  • Running continuous improvement cycles on enrolment, policy enforcement, monitoring, and self-service workflows with your engineering and design team.

  • Engaging agencies across WOG to understand where SEED creates friction in real engineering workflows, and building repeatable playbooks for onboarding new device types, security profiles, and agency operating models.

  • Defining and tracking operational metrics — time-to-compliance, exception request volume, false-positive rates, support ticket patterns — that tell you whether SEED is getting better or worse for the people who have to use it.

  • Partnering with cybersecurity stakeholders to align SEED's evolution with the government's broader security posture strategy.

  • Building the instrumentation needed to trace the user journey end-to-end — from device enrolment to policy compliance to active threat monitoring — so the team can see where things stall and fix them before users raise tickets.

  • Driving the rollout of new SEED capabilities across a diverse WOG landscape with varying levels of engineering and cybersecurity maturity.

  • You will ultimately be responsible for SEED being a platform that sustains engineering productivity — because it's secure by default and invisible by design.

[What we are looking for]

  • We are looking for an independent person with strong product management fundamentals and a desire to continuously develop their craft.

  • 4 to 8 years in product management. Years of experience are a rough guideline. We are also open to exceptional early-career candidates who demonstrate strong product thinking, ownership, and learning agility.

  • Has shipped impactful products, projects, or initiatives in complex organisations, with multiple stakeholder groups and a mix of top-down mandates and bottom-up adoption to navigate.

  • Can run structured product thinking in ambiguous spaces and shift into execution mode without losing sight of the strategy.

  • Communicates clearly in writing and in person, comfortable presenting to senior leadership and working with engineers in the same week.

  • Prior experience with security products, zero trust architecture, endpoint management, or enterprise platform products is a plus.

Who We Are & Our Vision

At GovTech, we don’t just build apps and technology; we build the digital infrastructure of an entire nation. Our mission is to transform the delivery of public services through technology that is seamless, secure, and—above all—human-centric.

The Product Marketing Team is the bridge between world-class engineering and millions of users. We don’t just "launch" products; we drive adoption, build trust, and ensure that every digital touchpoint improves a life. Our end goal is that through our work, Singapore becomes a model of how governments can use technology to improve the public good, and that GovTech products are loved and have a positive impact across Singapore.

The Portfolio: Impact at Scale

You will oversee a diverse ecosystem of products that have redefined the Singaporean digital experience, examples include:

  • Singpass: The trusted digital identity of every Singaporean.
  • GovWallet: Revolutionizing how government payouts and credits reach citizens.
  • BookingSG: Making bookings seamless for public officers and citizens.
  • Oobee: Making digital accessibility a reality for all.
  • Ownself Gather: Simplifying case management for public service

About the Role

As Senior Manager, Product Marketing, you will own the end-to-end GTM strategy for a portfolio of GovTech's most impactful whole-of-government products. You will drive adoption at scale, translate complex technical capabilities into compelling narratives for technical and non-technical stakeholders, and build the measurement frameworks that prove what's working. This is a rare opportunity to shape how the entire nation of Singapore experiences government services.

What You'll Own:

  • Own end-to-end GTM strategy and execution for assigned GovTech products, from positioning and messaging to launch and post-launch adoption tracking.
  • Define and drive product positioning, user segmentation, and value proposition development for B2B and B2B2C audiences.
  • Identify product discovery channels and user touchpoints to drive adoption, activation, and retention.
  • Analyse product funnels and engagement data to surface friction points and direct intervention strategies.
  • Build and maintain sales enablement and stakeholder enablement assets, translating technical roadmaps into value-based narratives for policy makers, agency directors, and product teams.
  • Partner with Product, Engineering, Data, and Policy teams cross-functionally to align GTM plans with product roadmaps.
  • Define and track success metrics, plus build feedback loops that inform product and marketing decisions.
  • Function as an Individual Contributor within a team of PMMs

Requirements & Qualifications

Experience

  • Seniority: Minimum 6–8 years of experience in Product Marketing or Growth roles.
  • Seasoned Marketer: Have a demonstrated ability to plan and execute marketing or product marketing strategies. Prior work and personal projects count for much more than specific degrees.
  • SaaS Expertise: Minimum 2 years in Enterprise SaaS. You must demonstrate experience managing complex B2B or B2B2C product lifecycles, API-led ecosystems, and platform adoption.
  • People Management: Proven experience working in teams and influencing across multi-levels of stakeholders. Having managed a small team or reports will be a plus.

Skills

  • Go-to-market Fluency: Expert-level knowledge of Go-To-Market (GTM) strategy and a proven track record of executing on plans proficiently and managing budgets efficiently. An ability to work and influence across different product teams to scale adoption and grow users, plus improve retention rates of GovTech products.
  • Market & User Intelligence: Proven ability to turn research on user behaviour and adjacent product ecosystems into insights that sharpen product positioning and identify adoption opportunities.
  • Data & Analytics: Have exceptional ROI-tracking skills, able to prove what is, or isn’t, working. You must be able to perform independent data deep-dives to validate marketing decisions and create feedback loops. A proficiency in a GA4, Mixpanel, or Amplitude is ideal.
  • The SaaS "Lens": You bring a "Product-Led Growth" mindset. You view B2B2C and B2B products like GovWallet or BookingSG through the lens of user friction, activation, and retention while managing them as an integrated ecosystem rather than a collection of features.
  • Narrative Excellence: You are a world-class writer and presenter. You can take a 50-slide technical deck and distill it into a 3-slide "Vision Pitch" that inspires action, as well as crafting a message that resonates with every end user. Proven ability to build enablement assets, one-pagers, ROI narratives, pitch frameworks, and training programmes, that equip non-marketing stakeholders to drive product adoption on your behalf.
  • Stakeholder Diplomacy: The ability to navigate the "Gov" in GovTech. You can translate complex technical roadmaps into value-based narratives for non-technical policy makers and technical product team members alike.
  • AI & Emerging Tech Awareness: Familiarity with how AI is transforming digital service delivery and user experience. Ability to translate AI-driven product capabilities into plain-language value propositions for non-technical audiences, and an interest in applying AI tools to improve marketing efficiency and content quality.

Because in most companies, "Product-Market Fit" means a better quarter. At GovTech, it means a better country. With us, you’ll have the opportunity to shape and improve the lives of everyone in Singapore.

[What you will be working on]

The DV module is a centralised, reusable document verification capability built within the Work Pass Integrated System (WINS). It consolidates what was previously fragmented verification logic spread across independent systems for Employment Pass, S Pass, Work Permit, and Migrant Domestic Worker applications into a single, shared module.

The key goals of the module are to eliminate duplication of verification workflows and maintenance effort, standardise and harmonise DV processes across pass types, and enable verified documents to be shared across applications so that applicants do not need to resubmit the same documents for different pass types. This improves efficiency for both MOM officers processing applications and applicants going through the work pass application journey.

Understanding and Defining Requirements

Product Ops is responsible for deeply understanding the current state of Document Verification across the various pass types and documenting the pain points — such as duplicated verification logic, workflow discrepancies, and the need for applicants to resubmit the same documents across different pass applications. They translate these into clear, structured business and functional requirements for the centralised DV module, ensuring it meets the needs of all pass types without compromising on pass-type-specific rules or validations.

Stakeholder Engagement and Alignment

Product Ops acts as the bridge between MOM policy owners, operations teams, and the technical development team. This involves facilitating workshops and interviews with stakeholders from each pass type domain to surface existing workflows, identify divergences, and agree on a common, harmonised process. Given that DV currently exists independently across multiple systems, managing stakeholder alignment and buy-in for a shared module is a significant part of the role.

Process Mapping and Gap Analysis

A core responsibility is mapping out the as-is DV workflows for each pass type and conducting a thorough gap analysis to identify where processes diverge and where they can be standardised. Product Ops would document these in process flow diagrams and use them to define the to-be state — a unified DV workflow that is flexible enough to accommodate pass-type-specific requirements while eliminating unnecessary duplication.

Defining the Shared Document Repository Logic

One of the key features of the new DV module is the ability to share verified documents across pass type applications, so applicants do not need to resubmit the same documents. Product Ops is responsible for defining the business rules around this — for example, what constitutes a valid previously verified document, how long a verified document remains valid, and under what conditions a document must be re-verified. These rules need to be clearly articulated before development begins.

User Stories and Acceptance Criteria

Product Ops translates requirements into well-defined user stories and acceptance criteria that the development team can work from. For a reusable module like DV, this includes stories covering document upload, verification workflows, document sharing logic, exception handling, and integration touchpoints with the various pass type systems.

Integration and Dependency Management

Since the DV module needs to integrate with multiple existing systems across the different pass types, Product Ops plays a key role in mapping out integration requirements and dependencies. This includes working with technical architects to understand API contracts, data flows, and how the centralised module will be consumed by each downstream system.

Supporting UAT and Change Management

Product Ops supports user acceptance testing by preparing test scenarios that cover the full range of pass types and document verification scenarios, including edge cases. They also play a role in change management — helping operations and policy teams understand how the new centralised module changes their workflows, and ensuring that training and communication materials accurately reflect the new processes.

Metrics and Success Criteria

Product Ops helps define what success looks like for the DV module — for instance, reduction in duplicate document submissions, reduction in maintenance overhead across systems, and improvement in processing time. Tracking these metrics post-launch also falls within the Product Ops remit, helping the team iterate and improve the module over time.

[What we are looking for]

  • Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Information Technology, or a related field.
  • Proven experience in software development, system analysis, or a similar technical role.
  • Proficiency in at least one modern programming language (e.g., Java, Python, Go, C#).
  • Experience with cloud platforms (e.g., AWS, Azure, GCP) and containerization technologies (e.g., Docker, Kubernetes) is highly desirable.
  • Strong understanding of database concepts and experience with SQL/NoSQL databases.
  • Familiarity with API design and development principles.
  • Excellent problem-solving, analytical, and critical thinking skills.
  • Strong communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to collaborate effectively with diverse stakeholders.
  • Ability to work independently and as part of a team in a fast-paced environment.

We are looking for a Product Ops specialist to support STARS2.0's Phase 2 delivery squads and the parallel discovery into the platform law firms use to submit property transactions. This role sits at the intersection of business analysis and product delivery: you will analyse existing business processes, translate business and regulatory requirements into clear product requirements, and help the delivery squads avoid simply replicating STARS1's existing business rules where those rules can instead be rationalised and simplified.
This is a forward-deployed role: you will be embedded within the Singapore Land Authority (SLA), working day-to-day alongside Registration Officers, business stakeholders, and the engineers, designers and Product Managers across both Phase 2 squads.
You will be shared across both delivery squads and into the parallel discovery workstream, giving you visibility into how requirements and business logic connect across the whole programme rather than being scoped to a single team's backlog.

[What you will be working on]

About the programme
STARS2.0 is the programme to modernise STARS, Singapore's Land Titles Registry system, which has been in operation since 1993 and today manages approximately 2 million live titles. It is operationally critical infrastructure: it processes 500,000 property transactions a year and is the single source of truth by which the Government records and guarantees land ownership in Singapore.
STARS2.0 is not a standalone technology project. It sits at the centre of a wider Land Titles Registry transformation that extends beyond the registry itself - to the digital platform through which law firms submit property transactions, the Digital Conveyancing Portal, and adjacent systems. This role spans both the core registry modernisation and a parallel discovery into that wider ecosystem.

Business process analysis
You will analyse how STARS1's existing business processes and rules actually work today, identifying which are genuinely load-bearing regulatory logic and which are legacy implementation artefacts that can be simplified in STARS2.0. This is central to the programme's approach: STARS1's business rules were, in places, hardcoded for implementation convenience rather than reflecting the underlying regulation, and a key goal of STARS2.0 is to rationalise rather than replicate that logic.

Requirements translation
You will work with Registration Officers, policy stakeholders and Product Managers to translate business needs, operational realities and regulatory requirements into clear, actionable product requirements that engineering and design can build against. You will help ensure requirements are documented with enough precision that squads can build from defined criteria rather than discovering constraints mid-delivery.

Cross-squad and cross-track support
Because you sit across both Phase 2 squads and the parallel platform-discovery workstream, you will help surface where requirements, business rules or dependencies in one area affect another, so decisions are made with the full picture rather than in isolation.

[What we are looking for]

  • Experience in business analysis, business process re-engineering, or a similar requirements-focused role, ideally on enterprise, platform, or legacy-modernisation programmes
  • Ability to read and interpret complex, rules-heavy legacy business logic and distinguish genuine regulatory requirements from legacy implementation artefacts
  • An open, curious mind, with a genuine drive to spot inefficient processes and challenge them - whether through automation, AI, or simply better-designed workflows
  • Strong requirements-writing and documentation skills; comfort translating ambiguous stakeholder input into clear, buildable requirements
  • Comfort working across multiple concurrent workstreams and squads without losing rigour or consistency
  • Effective stakeholder communication, particularly with operational staff (Registration Officers) and policy owners
  • Basic technical literacy sufficient to work effectively with engineers on how requirements translate into system design.

  • Government or public-sector experience, particularly in regulatory or licensing domains
  • Domain knowledge in land administration, conveyancing, or legal/regulatory systems
  • Familiarity with agile delivery practices and working within cross-functional squad

[About the role]

The Product Policy function sits at the critical intersection of government policy and digital product delivery. It enables tech teams to succeed in a complex public sector environment by:

  • Guiding product teams through regulatory and policy considerations / constraints; and
  • Supporting public agencies to understand how technology can improve public service delivery

As a Product Policy Specialist (Individual Contributor), you will play a key role in shaping policy approaches that enable good technology outcomes. You will work directly with internal product teams and public agencies to identify blockers, develop pragmatic policy strategies, and help align digital products with regulatory, operational, and public interest needs.

Join us if you are excited about working in the nascent tech policy space and to strategically influence how tech, policy and ops are effectively deployed in the public service.

[What you will be working on]

Policy-Product Integration

  • Translate policy constraints / intent into actionable guidance for product teams
  • Help agencies understand how product design choices intersect with public policy goals
  • Advise on trade-offs between user experience, compliance, and government outcomes

Strategic Problem Solving

  • Identify systemic barriers to effective digital delivery (e.g. outdated policies, fragmented approvals)
  • Co-develop solutions with internal and external stakeholders that balance compliance with innovation
  • Use systems thinking and backcasting to assess long-term implications of policy-product decisions

Stakeholder Engagement

  • Work closely with product managers, designers, engineers, legal, and policy teams
  • Collaborate with public agencies to align on project objectives and delivery conditions
  • Communicate clearly across technical and non-technical audiences

Writing & Communication

  • Craft memos, policy notes, and communications that frame product issues in clear, policy-aligned terms
  • Present recommendations to internal leads and external partners with clarity and persuasion

[What we are looking for]

  • Government Acumen: Understands how regulations, governance processes, and public accountability shape digital delivery. Familiarity with Singapore’s public sector or similar operating contexts is a plus.
  • Product Orientation: Comfortable working with digital product teams, understanding product life cycles, and prioritising user needs. Able to assess how tech decisions can drive or hinder policy outcomes.
  • Systems Thinker: Able to anticipate downstream impacts, navigate ambiguity, and identify root causes in complex systems.
  • Initiative & Ownership: Self-starter who can independently scope and drive initiatives. Comfortable making progress in unclear or fast-evolving contexts.
  • Strong Communicator: Excellent written and verbal communication. Able to synthesise complexity and convey compelling recommendations.
  • 6–10 years of experience in public policy, product strategy, regulatory affairs, or related fields
  • Demonstrated experience in roles requiring cross-functional alignment, policy interpretation, or product delivery
  • A background in public sector work, management consulting, policy & strategy, or technology policy is advantageous
  • SADs/DDs (MX11, MX11A, MX10-equivalent) from the Singapore Public Service are welcome to apply; remuneration will be commensurate with relevant experience.

GovTech is an equal opportunity employer committed to fostering an inclusive workplace that values diverse voices and perspectives, as we believe that diversity is the foundation to innovation.   

Our employee benefits are based on a total rewards approach, offering a holistic and market-competitive suite of perks. These include leave benefits to meet your work-life needs and employee wellness programs.

  • Prepare regular reports and dashboards for recruiters, hiring managers, and leadership teams.
  • Analyze scheduling trends, interviewer utilization, candidate throughput, and operational efficiency.
  • Ensure data accuracy and integrity within recruitment systems and reporting tools.
  • Support workforce planning and recruitment forecasting through scheduling and pipeline data insights.

Process Improvement

  • Identify opportunities to streamline scheduling workflows and improve recruitment operations.
  • Develop and maintain standard operating procedures (SOPs) and documentation.
  • Partner with recruiters and stakeholders to implement scalable scheduling and coordination practices.
  • Support projects related to recruitment technology, automation, and operational excellence.

  • Candidates for this position should ideally possess a Bachelor’s degree in Human Resources, Business Administration, or a related field.

  • Strong attention to detail and commitment to data accuracy.

As the Senior AI Security Consultant for the BusinessSG initiative, you will be the primary security architect guiding our transition to a proactive AI-driven platform. You will be embedded within a 10-man Discovery Squad, working alongside AI engineers and product leads to ensure that autonomous AI workflows—operating via messaging interfaces and a unified data hub—are secure, transparent, and resilient.

Your mission is to ensure every AI action is auditable and non-repudiable, protecting multi-agency data sources while maintaining the highest standards of public trust.

Key Responsibilities

  1. Security Architecture & Threat Modeling
  • System Design: Lead the design of security guardrails for AI agents to prevent them from taking unauthorized legal or financial actions.
  • Threat Modeling: Map out potential risks for autonomous AI, such as users trying to "hijack" the agent's intent or tricking it into accessing data it shouldn't.
  • Human-in-the-Loop: Design workflows that ensure high-stakes AI decisions (like grant recommendations) cannot proceed without explicit, authenticated human approval.
  1. Reliable Audit & Explainability
  • Audit Trails: Build a "Chain of Custody" for AI decisions by logging what the agent "thought," what specific data it retrieved, and which model version was used.
  • Reproducibility: Ensure that AI actions are documented well enough to be reconstructed and explained to auditors or stakeholders.
  • Data Governance: Ensure the AI only accesses integrated agency data on a strict "need-to-know" basis.
  1. Testing & Advanced Privacy (Preferred)
  • Security Testing: Conduct proactive testing to find vulnerabilities in how the AI processes instructions or uses external tools.
  • Advanced Privacy: Implement specialized privacy technologies to protect sensitive business information within our unified data hub.

Required Competencies & Experience

Experience Profile

  • 6–10 years of experience in Cybersecurity, with at least 2–3 years focused on AI/ML systems or securing LLM-based applications.
  • Proven track record in Cloud Infrastructure Security, specifically securing serverless compute, API gateways, and cloud-native databases.

Core Technical Foundations

  • Agentic System Design: Experience architecting or securing systems where AI moves beyond "chat" to performing actions through APIs.
  • LLM Security Foundations: Strong understanding of current LLM/ASI security risks, including prompt injection and data privacy in RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation) setups.
  • Regulatory Knowledge: In-depth knowledge of Singapore’s public sector security standards, including:
  • IM8.
  • Model AI Governance Framework.

Strategic & Soft Skills

  • Discovery Squad Collaboration: Ability to thrive in a high-velocity "sandbox" environment where you must balance rapid prototyping with security rigor.
  • Adversarial Mindset: Ability to anticipate how users might try to "game" the system to gain unfair advantages.
  • Risk Communication: Translating complex technical AI risks into clear, actionable advice for senior leadership.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience with Policy-as-Code or logic-based authorization systems (e.g., ABAC).
  • Knowledge in Digital Forensics or building immutable logging architectures.
  • Prior experience in a Public Sector or "Smart Nation" project context.

Why this role?

This is a unique opportunity to join a specialized squad at the ground floor of agentic AI adoption in government. You will move from defending static applications to securing autonomous intelligence that directly impacts the Singapore business community.

Our multidisciplinary team comprises product managers, engineers, designers professionals passionate about delivering secure digital services for the Singapore Public Service.

You will work closely with CISOs, business owners, GovTech, technology partners and government agencies to build secure-by-design capabilities while shaping cybersecurity practices across the GeBIZ X ecosystem.

We are looking for an experienced Senior Cybersecurity Engineer who is passionate about designing secure, resilient, and scalable digital platforms across cloud, SaaS, and enterprise environments.

In this role, you will lead the design, implementation, and continual improvement of cybersecurity controls across the GeBIZ X ecosystem, encompassing the Ivalua SaaS platform, integrated Whole-of-Government (WOG) agency systems, and the Singapore Government Tech Stack (SGTS), connected through the MOF Orchestrator—the common integration platform.

Beyond engineering, you will play a pivotal role in cybersecurity governance, risk management, audit readiness, and security assurance. Working closely with GovTech, WOG agencies, business stakeholders, and technology partners, you will champion secure-by-design principles, strengthen cyber resilience, and ensure compliance with Singapore Government ICT security policies, standards, and regulatory requirements.

You will apply Singapore Government ICT security policies, standards, and industry best practices, including IM8, the GovTech Cybersecurity Playbooks for Software-as-a-Service (SaaS) Security and Large Language Model (LLM) Applications, as well as ISO/IEC 27001 and ISO/IEC 27018, to drive secure SaaS configuration, vendor risk management, protection of Personally Identifiable Information (PII) in cloud environments, and compliance with AI governance and security directives issued by the Smart Nation and Digital Government Office (SNDGO) and the AI Governance Division (AIDG).

Technical Leadership Expectations

  • Lead the design, implementation, and continual improvement of cybersecurity controls across the GeBIZ X ecosystem, ensuring secure-by-design principles are embedded throughout the solution lifecycle.

  • Define cybersecurity requirements and provide technical consultancy on application, cloud, and system security architecture, ensuring compliance with IM8 and prevailing Government ICT security policies and standards.

  • Lead security architecture reviews, threat modelling, security design reviews, and VAPT remediation planning for cloud-native, SaaS, COTS, and enterprise integrations.

  • Drive cybersecurity risk assessments and recommend appropriate security controls to address emerging threats and evolving business requirements.

  • Strengthen GeBIZ X's cybersecurity posture by applying Singapore Government ICT security policies, standards, and industry best practices, including IM8, the GovTech Cybersecurity Playbooks for Software-as-a-Service (SaaS) Security and Large Language Model (LLM) Applications, as well as ISO/IEC 27001 and ISO/IEC 27018, to drive secure SaaS configuration, vendor risk management, protection of Personally Identifiable Information (PII) in cloud environments, and compliance with AI governance and security directives issued by the Smart Nation and Digital Government Office (SNDGO) and the AI Governance Division (AIDG).

Ownership

  • Take ownership of the end-to-end cybersecurity delivery for complex and ambiguously scoped initiatives, making sound technical decisions and driving workstreams through to successful implementation.

  • Lead the development and maintenance of cybersecurity governance artefacts, including System Security Plans (SSPs), System Criticality Assessments (SCAs), Security Risk Assessments (SRAs), Risk Treatment Plans, and audit remediation reports.

  • Lead and coordinate internal and external cybersecurity audits, including GIROC and IM8 audits, ensuring audit readiness, timely evidence submission, effective stakeholder engagement, and closure of audit findings.

  • Lead cybersecurity incident response and coordinate investigation, containment, recovery, root cause analysis, and implementation of preventive measures for security incidents.

  • Drive continuous improvement of cybersecurity controls, operational processes, and governance practices across the GeBIZ X ecosystem.

Strategic Alignment

  • Translate organisational cybersecurity objectives into actionable implementation plans, ensuring security initiatives support GeBIZ X product delivery and Whole-of-Government digital transformation goals.

  • Identify cybersecurity risks, technology trends, and improvement opportunities, proactively recommending solutions that enhance security resilience while balancing delivery, operational, and business needs.

  • Evaluate emerging technologies, including Frontier AI and AI-enabled capabilities, assessing associated cybersecurity risks and recommending appropriate security controls for secure adoption within Government systems.

  • Support strategic planning by providing cybersecurity insights, technical recommendations, and risk-based advice to IT and business stakeholders.

Culture and Organisation Influence

  • Foster a culture of security, collaboration, continuous learning, and engineering excellence by promoting knowledge sharing, innovation, and secure engineering practices.

  • Build trusted partnerships across GovTech, Government agencies, vendors, and multidisciplinary teams to deliver secure and resilient digital services.

Champion continuous improvement by challenging existing processes, sharing lessons learnt from projects and security incidents, and driving improvements to engineering and cybersecurity practices.
