AI Practice is the AI R&D and capability development arm of GovTech's Government Technology Office (GTO). As a Senior Data Scientist (Multimodal AI) on the Multimodal AI Squad, your work will span two broad areas:

Frontier Exploration and Evaluation
Systematically scanning, experimenting with, and interpreting the latest AI developments across vision, video, audio, and document modalities. This includes producing fast-response technical explorations when meaningful new capabilities emerge, as well as deeper assessments of maturing areas. The emphasis is on getting your hands dirty. This is empirical work, not editorial.

Agency Engagement and Transformation
Translating frontier AI capabilities into real outcomes for government agencies. The squad builds AI capabilities through rapid experimentation and works with agencies to identify and test promising capabilities against their own data and use cases, with viable solutions graduating onward for productisation. You will support the journey from discovery through experimentation and prototyping, often as the squad's technical point of contact with an agency.

Day to day, you can expect to:

  • Experiment with state-of-the-art multimodal models (VLMs, MLLMs, diffusion models, speech and audio models) and evaluate their applicability to government use cases and strategy
  • Design, build, and run evaluations and benchmarks for AI models on real-world Singapore government tasks — including constructing the underlying datasets, defining metrics and scoring, and standing behind results that inform agency and vendor decisions
  • Build functional prototypes and proof-of-concept solutions for agency engagements spanning smart city video analytics, document intelligence, generative media, and content authentication
  • Stay current with the latest developments in applied AI and assess what translates from research settings to practical government applications
  • Support the development of our multimodal AI showcase and prototyping platforms, and advise on deployment considerations such as on-premise vs cloud, hardware, and cost
  • Produce technical write-ups and contribute to knowledge artefacts such as handbooks, reports, and evaluation findings

  • Degree in Computer Science, Data Science, AI/ML, Engineering, or a related field
  • 5+ years applied ML/data science, with meaningful depth in at least one non-text modality — computer vision, video understanding, audio/speech, or generative image/video
  • Solid understanding of machine learning fundamentals, including model training, evaluation methodology, and experiment design — comfort with sampling, uncertainty, and metric selection is a strong plus
  • Foundational knowledge of computer vision concepts and/or hands-on experience working with image, video, or audio data
  • Exposure to multimodal AI systems, vision-language models, and generative AI — including fine-tuning (e.g. LoRA) and synthetic data generation
  • Practical sense for running models: GPU/VRAM constraints, open-weight vs commercial API trade-offs, and the cost implications of each
  • Working knowledge of cloud solution architecture on GCP and/or AWS — able to stand up and structure prototypes using managed compute, storage, and model-serving services
  • Comfortable using AI-assisted development tools (e.g., Claude Code, Cursor, OpenAI Codex) to accelerate your work
  • Treats AI as a collaborator, using it to learn new libraries, debug, and move faster — and re-tests frontier model capability first-hand rather than relying on secondhand claims
  • Curious and outcome-oriented. You enjoy going deep on a problem but ultimately care about whether it works in practice
  • Comfortable with ambiguity. Government AI work means scoping problems that aren't always well-defined, running several workstreams at once, and accepting that not every prototype ships
  • Comfortable leading a small team of junior data scientists — setting technical direction, breaking down problems, giving feedback, and growing capability alongside your own delivery.
  • Strong communicator. You can explain what you built and why it matters to both technical peers and non-technical agency stakeholders — including turning a metric into a recommendation someone can act on

NEA works closely with its partners and the community to develop and spearhead environmental and public health initiatives and programmes. It is committed to motivating every individual to care for the environment as a way of life, in order to build a liveable and sustainable Singapore for present and future generations.

We are seeking a Senior Data & Platform Engineer to lead the build-out of NEA's Weather Data Lake, a Databricks-based analytics platform replacing the legacy Climate Data Management System (CDMS) and serving as the single source of truth for meteorological and climate data across the Meteorological Service Singapore (MSS).

As a forward-deployed engineer, you will own the MSS data platform architecture on the Government Commercial Cloud (GCC 2.0) Azure stack, design and deliver production data pipelines, and mentor junior engineers. This role sits at the intersection of data engineering, software engineering, and cloud platform architecture.

As a Senior Data & Platform Engineer, you will be working on:

  • Design and build the Weather Data Lake on Databricks (Unity Catalog, Delta Lake, Structured Streaming) running on ADLSv2 within GCC 2.0. Make and document platform architecture decisions covering compute, storage tiering, governance, and cost management.
  • Architect production data pipelines ingesting from GTS, ADES, AirViro, IWXXM, and WIS 2.0 sources. Build these using Spark (PySpark) on Databricks with CDC patterns and full data lineage.
  • Own the data quality framework. Implement QC pipelines serving both the real-time forecasting path and the post-correction analytics path from a common Azure Blob landing zone.
  • Own the infrastructure as code layer, defining all platform resources (Databricks workspaces, storage, networking, IAM) in Terraform with modular configurations. Establish staging and production environment separation with appropriate retention policies and CI/CD pipelines.
  • Define integration contracts between the Azure Landing Zone (ingestion) and the Weather Data Lake (analytics), ensuring operational systems do not take direct dependencies on the lake.
  • Mentor junior data engineers and software engineers. Conduct code reviews, run architecture workshops, pair on complex pipeline work, and build a culture of engineering rigour.
  • Partner with MSS to translate domain requirements into technical designs meeting the April 2027 CDMS end-of-support deadline, including historical data migration and downstream consumption patterns.
  • Implement data governance using Unity Catalog: access policies, classification, audit logging, and lineage tracking compliant with IM8 and NEA standards.
  • Evaluate platform evolution opportunities including serverless compute, Lakebase, and integration with the Weather Data Hub (Azure APIM) for API distribution.

  • Deep familiarity with Azure — ADLSv2, Blob Storage, Data Factory, and networking fundamentals (VNet, Private Endpoints, ExpressRoute).
  • Strong Terraform experience for data platform infrastructure: provisioning Databricks workspaces, storage, networking, and IAM in a modular, version-controlled manner. Comfortable with CI/CD in regulated cloud environments.
  • Proficiency in Python and SQL. Solid hands-on Spark (PySpark or Scala) experience building and optimising large-scale data processing on Databricks.
  • Demonstrated ability to make platform architecture decisions, write ADRs, and present trade-offs to technical and non-technical stakeholders.
  • Track record of mentoring junior engineers and raising the engineering bar across a team.
  • Experience with data governance frameworks, data quality tooling, and lineage tracking in production.

  • Solid understanding of OpenUSD layering, composition arcs, and schemas.

As a Technology Associate in Cybersecurity, you'll begin your career protecting the digital services and infrastructure that millions of people in Singapore rely on every day.

This is a challenging and rewarding opportunity for a highly analytical and meticulous individual to join the Threat Intelligence Research & Analysis (TIRA) team within the Cyber Security Group (CSG). As a TIRA analyst, you will play a critical role in identifying, analysing, and tracking advanced and emerging threats that may impact the Singapore Government. You will be responsible for developing actionable intelligence from your findings to inform WoG detection and response capabilities.

[What you will be working on]

  • Conduct in-depth research of advanced threat actors to analyse their tactics, techniques and procedures (TTPs), victimology and motivations to provide operational teams with behavioural elements to develop detection rules and adversary simulations
  • Support investigations by contextualising identified indicators and performing sensemaking of findings to derive intel assessment
  • Correlate data from multiple intelligence sources to identify patterns and trends to recommend how defenders can mitigate against pertinent threats
  • Produce timely and accurate intelligence briefings, reports and other intel products to disseminate findings to technical and executive audiences
  • Evaluate and recommend tools and methodologies to improve research and analysis capabilities
  • Stay informed about the evolving cyber threat landscape by continuously monitoring threat intelligence feeds and attending industry conferences

[What we are looking for]

  • Highly developed research and analytical skills, including critical thinking and contextual analysis
  • Possess strong communication and interpersonal skills
  • Degree in Information Security, Computer Science, Engineering or Cybersecurity or related fields strongly preferred
  • Cybersecurity certifications (e.g. GCIH, GCTI, GREM, CISSP) are an advantage
  • Proven experience in processing, handling, and analyzing large-scale datasets
  • Practical knowledge or hands-on experience in leveraging AI and automation tools
  • Relevant experience in various cybersecurity domains (e.g. threat intelligence, incident response, malware analysis, risk assessment) and data analysis strongly preferred
  • Good understanding of cyber threat analysis models (e.g. cyber kill chain, diamond model, MITRE ATT&CK) preferred
  • Applicant must be a Singapore Citizen

GovTech is the lead agency driving Singapore's Smart Nation initiative and public sector digital transformation. We harness the power of technology to make lives better for citizens, businesses, international audiences and the public service sector.

Digital Economy Products (DEP) is a division within GovTech run like a modern product company, solving important underserved problems spanning across Healthcare, Manpower, Trade-Industry-Finance, National Development, and Sustainability sectors.

Designers at DEP are key to our success. They work closely with product managers, researchers, software engineers, and public sector stakeholders, bringing purposeful ideas to life with excellent visual and interaction design, skillfully shaping how users feel when using our services.

About the product

Through the GreenGov initiative, the government has committed to the public its aim to achieve net-zero emissions by approximately 2045. Furthermore, it has established clear and measurable milestones to facilitate progress across all agencies. Since the year 2021, agencies have utilised the eGreenGov portal, which is housed within the National Environment Agency’s Waste and Resource Management System (WRMS), to report various environmental data of their respective premises.

The Public Sector Sustainability Office (PSSO) reviews the progress of agencies, provides updates to the Cabinet, and produces the annual GreenGov report championing the GreenGov initiative. They intend to help agencies identify opportunities to improve resource efficiency and climate resilience, and partner them to streamline the process of implementing these improvements.

Responsibilities

  • Understand PSSO’s mission and users’ needs

  • Create mockups and intuitive user flows that drive climate action at scale

  • Test early designs with users; iterate with feedback

  • Create detailed user interface specifications

  • Guide engineers in implementing your designs

  • Execute overall aesthetics that align with branding and design principles

  • Help progressively build and adapt a design system, that scales and flexes across a variety of user groups for the product

As a designer on this product, you’ll also get to learn and experiment with green design practices, taking a truly systemic approach towards responsible design and tech for public good.

We’re looking for a designer with:

  • Demonstrated ability in interaction and visual design — ideally 5+ years of experience in digital design

  • Great visual design sense and eye for detail

  • User- and data-focused design mentality

  • Proficiency in Figma and Adobe Creative Suite

  • Experience building responsive and accessible designs

  • Communicate well with users and engineers

  • A “can-do” attitude

  • Want to work for public good — respectfully pushing back if something is not in the public’s interest, including that of the environment.

These will be a plus:

  • Experience creating a simple and elegant design system

  • Interest in continually growing your visual design craft

  • Strong belief and drive for sustainability is a plus!

Overall, we look for people who are collaborative, value open communications, and take initiative to improve things.

[What you will be working on]

The Government Digital Products (GDP) Team aims to spearhead the digital transformation of government. We are a team of technologists in GovTech that aims to design and develop software applications that help government agencies better serve the needs of Singaporeans. We adopt an Agile development approach and work towards adopting tech best practices and cutting edge tools. Our team in GDP aims to improve lives by empowering change with the right technologies and better user experience.

How do we work

Job overview

We have built a scrum team of technologists who have developed digital products to improve citizen's experience of using the agency's e-services.

As a UX designer, you will work with our scrum team and other government agencies to inform product and design decisions. You will get to influence the digital experience of the agency’s e-services. This will involve having good interpersonal skills, sharp analytical mind, and astute design judgement. You will work closely with our designers, engineers, business analysts and product managers to continuously deliver features for transforming citizen experience and improving agency efficiency.

You will sit with the project scrum team, as a member of the UX team in GDP. The office will be located at the Punggol Digital District (PDD).

What to expect

Within your first month...

You have understood the overall product strategy, did a stock take on the UX status of the project, and contributed design screens for concurrent active sprints.

By the end of 3 months...

You should have run an inception, gathered requirements, co-create with stakeholders and scrum team, tested, prototyped, and shipped at least one new feature to the product backlog.

After 6 months...

You will have led research efforts to identify at least one opportunity for the product to grow or proposed enhancements for the existing tracks, in collaboration with designers, engineers, and product managers.

Beyond that...

You will continue to solve problems such as:

How can we...

  • create a seamless experience for citizen across e-services
  • help citizen complete the service with ease
  • resolve the agency pain point and improve ops efficiency
  • use data to improve government services
  • design for reusability across products

What we are looking for

How to succeed

Product and user-centric mindset

  • A desire to serve the public through the use of technology

  • You need to be able to grasp the use case and come up with the task flows in a short span of time

  • You are able to drive product solutions that service the goals of both the users and stakeholders

  • You are collaborative and understand that co-creating a product with the team
    and stakeholders will have a higher chance of it being the best product

  • You find the quickest route to design, test, and ship a design prototype to 'prove'
    a concept. Be agile and lean

  • You are data-driven yourself, with experience in user research, in order to use data to justify design decisions

  • You yearn to analyse user feedback and activity, and iterating the design to enhance user experience

Technologist at work

  • You are able to translate user research into design recommendations and findings

  • You are able to tackle complex tasks and transform them into intuitive, accessible, and easy-to-use designs

  • You are meticulous and possess good problem solving skills

  • Frontend development knowledge is a bonus

Strategist at heart

  • Strategists hardly work alone. You have to work well with your scrum team and agencies to strategise the product direction together.

  • Good organisational, presentation and listening skills

  • Be flexible, be a team player, solve problems, and contribute to the UX and product team’s success.

Preferred (Additional Requirements)

  • At least 4-5 years of professional experience in product design, working on end-to-end delivery. That would include experience in facilitating workshops, gathering requirements, usability testing, envisioning flows, and delivering hi-fidelity mockups.

  • Experience in Agile and UX development environment will be an added advantage

  • Previous experience leading a team in UX design will be an added advantage. You may be considered for a senior position if applicable.

What We Offer:

  • Collaborative and creative work environment
  • Competitive salary and benefits package, including opportunities for professional growth and development
  • Work environment that is fully supportive of self-improvement and personal/professional development

jobTitle: HR Policy Analyst (Lead/Senior) Performance Management and Organisational Design
agencyDescription:
The Public Service Division (PSD) stewards a trusted Singapore Public Service for a successful and vibrant Singapore. Our 4 key roles include:

  • Developing a flourishing and diverse workforce by supporting our public officers' continual growth of skills and creating meaningful careers
  • Developing a forward-looking and inspiring community of leaders who are united, resilient, and anchored in public service values and ethos
  • Building future-ready public sector organisations by steering and supporting transformation of our organisations and catalysing innovations for organisations to work more effectively
  • Driving good governance, values and excellence to safeguard the integrity and reputation of the Public Service and uphold the trust of citizens

Why Join Us

When you join PSD, you become part of a community that learns together and cares for one another. We look out for your well-being and partner you in your career growth. Being in the business of developing People and driving transformation makes our work deeply Purposeful. What you do will impact our public officers and agencies, and in turn make a difference to Singapore and Singaporeans.

If you share our passion in reimagining Possibilities and pushing boundaries to shape a first-class Public Service, we welcome you to join us!

People, Our Pride | Service, Our Pledge | Integrity, Our Core | Excellence, Our Quest
jobDescription:
The Public Service Division (PSD), a Centre of Government agency, shapes people and organisation strategies across Singapore's Public Service. As the steward of Public Service-wide HR policies, PSD is reimagining how performance is recognised, organisations are designed and managers lead — building an agile, future-ready people system for an AI-enabled, competency-based and multi-generational workforce.

Performance management and organisation design are two sides of the same coin. High-performing organisations are built not only through how work is organised, but also through how people are recognised, developed and enabled to perform. In this role, you will design HR policies, people systems and organisational structures that enable the Public Service to deliver for Singapore today and into the future.

Join a team shaping the future of Singapore’s largest employer — with more than 150,000 public officers — and the people systems and policies that enable it to deliver for Singapore. If you are excited by solving complex workforce challenges and reimagining HR policy, operations and technology to deliver lasting impact at scale, we would love to hear from you.

What You Will Do

You will be part of a high-performing team responsible for shaping Public Service-wide performance management and organisational design policies that strengthen both individual performance and organisational effectiveness.

Shape the Future of Performance Management

  • Lead the review, design and continuous evolution of Public Service-wide performance management frameworks, including appraisal, ranking and promotion.
  • Design policy, operational and digital solutions that keep performance management simple, effective and future-ready, supporting competency-based careers, diverse career pathways and a future-ready workforce.
  • Reimagine the employee and supervisor experience across the appraisal and development journey, strengthening manager capability, performance conversations and employee growth.
  • Partner across HR policy domains to build a coherent, integrated workforce policy ecosystem.

Design High-Performing and Future-Ready Organisations

  • Partner agencies to design organisation structures, job evaluation and workforce models that strengthen organisational effectiveness and build future-ready capabilities, aligned with strategic workforce plans.
  • Develop organisation structure review guidelines and processes which are agile and fit-for-purpose.
  • Design and enable diverse career roles and pathways across generalist, leadership and specialist tracks, empowering officers with different aspirations to grow and contribute meaningfully across the Public Service.
  • Integrate organisation design and performance management policies to ensure organisation structures, jobs and people systems reinforce one another and drive organisational performance.

Drive Evidence-Based Policy Across Government

  • Work with HR practitioners, data specialists and technology teams to develop HR data products, digital capabilities and analytics that improve policy design, implementation and user experience.
  • Use workforce, organisational and performance data to generate insights, evaluate policy effectiveness and inform strategic workforce decisions.
  • Build trusted partnerships across Ministries, Statutory Boards and the HR community to co-create scalable workforce solutions.
  • Lead cross-functional initiatives spanning policy, operations, data and technology to deliver Public Service HR transformation.
jobRequirements:
What We Are Looking For

This role offers the opportunity to solve some of the Public Service's most strategic workforce challenges while working with senior leaders across Government to design the policies, people systems and organisational foundations that enable more than 150,000 public officers to perform at their best. Your work will help build a high-performing, future-ready Public Service for Singapore.

We are looking for curious, analytical and purpose-driven individuals who enjoy solving complex problems and creating meaningful impact at scale.

You Bring

  • Strong analytical and critical thinking skills, with the ability to navigate ambiguity and translate complex challenges into practical policy solutions.
  • A data-driven mindset and confidence in interpreting quantitative and qualitative evidence to inform decision-making.
  • Excellent written, verbal and presentation skills, with the ability to communicate complex ideas clearly and influence diverse stakeholders, including senior leaders.
  • Strong stakeholder management skills and the ability to influence and collaborate across diverse groups.
  • Initiative, resilience and a bias for action, with the drive to take ideas from concept to implementation.
  • High integrity, a collaborative mindset and pride in delivering high-quality outcomes.

Experience

  • Experience or demonstrated interest in public policy, HR policy, organisation design, organisational development, workforce strategy, job evaluation, workforce analytics or HR transformation will be advantageous.

jobDescription:
PSD’s HR Policy cluster is reimagining HR policies for Singapore’s biggest employer – the public service and its 153,000 officers. We’re rethinking how policies, operations and tech could look like for a multi-generational workforce, against the backdrop of career tour-of-duties and tech disruption. Play a driving role in enabling a diverse, flourishing public sector workforce that continues to deliver great policies, initiatives and services, for the next 60 years.

You’ll be part of a dynamic team of policy analysts from various agencies and specialists with experience at organisations such as Accenture, PWC and Kantar, to ensure that our benefits policies (such as medical, leave and awards) don’t just keep pace – they lead the way, balancing innovation with inclusivity to cater to the diverse needs of agencies and a multi-generational workforce. The short feedback loop means that you will land tangible impact, quickly, on the ground.

You will:

  • Do the end-to-end of policy development and implementation: From understanding the need, developing policy solutions, operationalising through agencies and systems, closing the feedback loop and refining policies
  • Develop deep expertise and specialist knowledge in formulating benefits and recognition packages
  • Develop policy acumen for national-level strategic considerations, future needs, economic and manpower trends across the public and private sectors
  • Be a thought leader in advocating best practices of how Public Service benefits policies and strategies can evolve to be future-ready
  • Forge deep partnerships with key stakeholders, such as HR leaders, agency senior management and HR systems and tech teams, to land your policies
  • Manage agencies’ clarifications and requests, and innovate on the operational front through tech, process and policy redesign, to free up time for more impactful work
  • Have opportunities for stretch assignments that involve cross-cluster collaboration on areas such as compensation, performance management, talent mobility, ops and tech
jobRequirements:
Strong analytical abilities, data-driven with detail orientation. Comfortable with quantitative analysis, particularly in Excel

  • Curiosity about problems and the why, and resourcefulness to navigate the macro context to design and implement effective and timely solutions
  • Strong communicator in written, slides and spoken
    • Ability to communicate complex issues and policy solutions simply
    • Ability to extract and distil complex analysis into key decision points for senior stakeholders
    • Willingness and drive to effectively engage a range of stakeholders to ensure that policy is successfully implemented
  • Bias for action and relentlessly resourceful in getting things done
  • Experience in policy, HR and/or government a plus
  • Understanding of tech and innovation a plus

Applicants will typically be notified on whether they are shortlisted or not within 4 weeks of the closing date of the job posting. Successful candidates will be appointed on a 2-year contract in the first instance.
